cards.name: Professional Materials
cards.content:
Please have a look at the information below and [[make contact|contact us]] with any questions. Brandon most frequently provides strategic consulting, leadership coaching, team facilitation, and cultural learning. These complimentary areas of practice have lead him to work with a great diversity of business people, facilitators, activists, and academics, admiring most those who generate the results they require by crafting a culture that supports teamwork.

 

Presently--


We are always looking for a new challenge to leverage our experience in:

  • Issue analysis and conflict management: [[Conflict Done Well]] (tm) through [[Martial Nonviolence]]® and [[http://peacepractices.org|Peace Practices]]
  • Systems analysis, culture building, long range planning, and strategic development
  • Higher Education as a Supervising Instructor, Lecturer, and facilitator of online learning
  • Qualitative business intelligence analysis
  • Humanistic user-experience design
  • Member services and enrollment systems architecture
  • Alternative dispute resolution litigation support analysis
  • Board facilitation and team building
  • Project Management and Process Analysis
  • Enterprise Operations and Administration
  • Human and Technology solutions oversight
  • Non-Profit Creation and Development
  • Campaign and Event planning

Previously--


Brandon co-founded and served as CEO of [[Association Building Community]], a non-profit supporting communities practicing the process arts. He created and directed the [[http://peacepractices.org|Peace Practices]] project, ABC's internationally funded  [[Conflict Done Well]] curriculum adopted by schools in the San Francisco Bay Area, and has served the Learning and Development needs of many individuals and enterprises.

Representing ABC, he created the position of Executive Director and the first professional administration for Aiki Extensions, and was honored to then serve on their Board of Directors for many years. AE is a non-profit which builds local and international capacity to use redirective rather than oppositional methods of conflict resolution.

Brandon was co-founder and Chief Instructor at FreeAiki Dojo in Berkeley CA which offers traditional aikido as a base for learning my conflict facilitation method - [[Martial Nonviolence]] (MNv). He was born and educated in Dallas TX, emigrated to California for a two year aikido apprenticeship, completed professional facilitation certifications in mediation and community building, acquired graduate degrees, became a husband and a father, and returned with his family to North Texas in 2018.

 

Specialties

  • Supervision and management
  • Community building and conflict facilitation
  • Mediation and negotiation
  • Academic research and teaching
  • Non-profit administration
  • Ensemble creation and team building
  • Spoken as well as media communications and performance
  • Broad I.T. skills
 
Brandon asked a long-time CEO client what he tells people that leads to successful referals. He forwarded this:
Brandon has extensive experience working through conflict in management environments, offering exceptional communication tools and soft skills, is comfortable engaging with C-level executives as they assess and make strategic decisions, and is serving right now as an enterprise-level executive coach.
 
His primary area of professional interest involves clarifying the risks associated with "what we chose not to know" by investigating the culture and mythology of businesses, divisions, and project teams. With his help, limiting organizational assumptions are uncovered and analyzed independent from individual agendas in order to push beyond self-justification. Most people don't know that this work requires skills like his, or even that it is possible to reframe difficulties as an opportunity to practice "[[conflict done well]]." I know he will put his experience at your service with confidence and confidentiality intact.

Please request an account to sign in and view more.

cards.name: Facilitation Resume BW
cards.content:
After devoting myself to a live-in apprenticeship in aikido for two years, I began assembling certifications in mediation and community building and academic degrees in depth psychology and cultural mythology in order to effectively practice the process arts (also see processarts.net), which is to say group process design and facilitation. In 1999 I co-founded and continue to volunteer direct Association Building Community, a distributed community and non-profit dedicated to community-building through the process arts. Since 1999, it has been my pleasure to complete two graduate degrees while working with dozens of organizations and successfully facilitating over two thousand hours of group processes, working globally to redefine and practice peace as "conflict done well."

 

Brandon WilliamsCraig Ph. D.

Berkeley, CA

(510) 962-3921 Skype bdwilliamscraig
brandon at williamscraig dot com

culturesmith.com

Conflict Done Well ®

cards.name: mythicity-context
cards.content:
William Doty deals exclusively with Mythography, and makes an essential contribution by bringing the idea “mythicity” home to mythological studies, and then by building a body of work which presupposes it. He begins by familiarizing his reader with mythicity by tracking its origins. In 1975, Wilhelm Dupré used the term in Religion in Primitive Cultures to introduce “the ‘mythic’ modality” which

unites the depth of time and space [. . .] toward the invisible, ideational, and universal. In other words, mythicity is not only the meta-empirical reality of man’s consciousness, which assimilates the empirical world as the manifestation of meaning, but it also initiates a movement to leave behind all figures and mythological concretizations. (264, 67)

This is as much to say “myth is the most interdisciplinary narrative,” while making explicit other aspects of a post-modern view of consciousness itself.

 

Dupré’s “modality” suggests an interpretive approach which understands ideas like “time and space” as framing experience figurally, as non-literal expressions. He goes on to propose a consciousness that is mythic and “meta-” which suggests an attentive interpretive style, perhaps as metanoia, for example, implies a process-level reflection and fundamental change based on experience. Finally, he virtually recapitulates the archetypal view by connecting mythic consciousness with both “the empirical world” and the making of meaning such that mythicity dissolves “mythological concretizations.”

 

Eric Gould takes mythicity further in a post-modern direction, noticing that contemporary mythography effects its own recovery from the utilitarian reductions of modernism through disappearance. Myth recovers itself by becoming absent as a literal thing, dissolving its use as a label for other people’s ideas about divinity and reemerging more true to itself as a non-literal, fictionally altered state of consciousness: “pure mythicity[. . .] in which a sign or a system of signs is full and open-ended at once” (Mythical Intentions in Modern Literature 119). “System of signs” and “full and open-ended at once” are two more ways of giving “mythological” its post-modern sense.

 

When Doty credits Gould’s Mythical Intentions in Modern Literature with developing the concept of mythicity as “the philosophical function of the mythic as an element of consciousness” (Doty Mythography 1st Ed. 241), he draws the line of Dupré’s “meta-empirical reality of man’s consciousness” through Gould, into James Hillman’s indication of the pervasiveness of mythicity when he proposes a “mythical style of consciousness” (Re-Visioning 100). One of the primary functions of post-modern mythographers, as distinct from critics of literature, students of religion, and social theorists, is to make clear that myth can no longer be thought of by unconsciously mythic disciplines as a handy tool or undeveloped terrain ideal for planting with progressive ideas and putting to some use. Mythography, or mythological studies and creativity, has not only its own rubrics but also reflects an understanding of human consciousness that is central to both ancient and contemporary thought, even beyond what is termed post-modern. Doty follows Hillman into the latter’s “animated mythological terrain” (Doty Mythography 2nd Ed. 211) based on myth being no-longer-a-thing in the hand of literal agendas but, where functionalisms are concerned, being an “‘absence’—which of course means that any putatively rationalistic epistemology cannot be used for the study of mythology” (Mythography 2nd Ed. 453). That is as much to say that mythologies are absent, effectively invisible to any approach based on the commonplace that knowledge is based on reason rather than experience, instead of seeing the two as inextricable.

cards.name: RQ 20100623
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

The band of intrepid adventurers continued their long walk to the banks of the Zola Fel. Fights of the previous week left the party completely
unscathed, due to the healing 6 matrix and plenty of magic points. Using the island as a navigation point, the party approached to less than
a kilometer from their target. Mel found signs of some kind of ambush or fight which involved no less than 12 combatants, many or all of them being broo, and the group decided to backtrack at least an hour away and camouflage a camp in order to avoid problems.

The party expertly set up a camp and moved to their regular watched. On second watch, Graves heard a group move in to within 100 meters and begin to set up camp. Graves remained, silent, vigilant, until he heard the group prepare to light a fire. At that Graves confronted them. They sounded clearly inexperienced, unaware of the danger of what the party believes to be over a hundred broo divided into three camps just two kilometers away.

By fourth watch rubble runners attacked the nearby camp. There was a pitched battle and the occupants ran screaming like little girls into the
party's camp, followed by a train of rubble runners. Max shot one of the adventurers and the party, after discussion, took pity on the noobs and dispatched the rubble runners hastily. The group decided that it was best to bring the noobs along. They were strong and dumb and might be useful. They were more of a danger in terms of attracting attention if they were allowed to follow the party, which they were likely to do if they weren't taken in. Phasia gave them a long talking to and Patsy was put in charge of keeping them in line.

The party moved carefully towards the goal. The sounds of a fight around the tower confirmed they were not alone, but Mel surmised that perhaps the brook wouldn't have two fights in them that day Graves expertly moved forward  hiding and sneaking and surveyed the area.
He found a sunken area that provided excellent cover and began to reconnoiter the ancient sewer line which he imagined using to access the
river unseen by the broo.

He was met however with a huge snake and jumped out of the water just moments before 150 cm fangs sunk into his leg. He returned in expert stealth and silence to the waiting party and shared the information he had gleaned. The party discussed the situation and came up with a plan of action. They snuck as a group, the big guys sneaking surprisingly well, to the pit and the party surrounded themselves in the pit to await the snake's return. They put some meat on a rope with some blood and tried to lure the snake in. It worked! The snake arrived, rearing its ugly head. The party shot at it and Graves' crossbow bolt in particular cut into it viciously. The noobs were more than they appeared to be however. Patsy screamed a warning as they struck. No longer appearing lost or docile, their faces took on a twisted visage of malice and, located on each corner of the pit, drew weapons and cut down into the pit. With a snake in the middle of the party and ogres surrounding the party, the situation looked like a death trap -- one from which escape was unlikely. The party burst into action. Peri and Phasia shot and struck out at the ogres. Then the unexpected happened. the snake, surrounded with too many targets and caught up in its own coils, struck hard and fast, hitting itself and allowing Grave's parrying blade to cut into it deep to boot. the snake died instantly. Don was sad, but rallied as the ogres still had a chance. Peri was taken down with a poisoning wound to the head. But they didn't really. Barbie can rushing in with a bison and slew one of the ogres summarily. He was greeted with arrow shots from across the water and was rendered functionally incapacitated, but still managed to wheel the bison around and get to cover. Another ogre, grappled by patsy and attacked by tim, fell to a combination of bow and sword. the final two, chaos cowards that they were went of running. Ken's leg had been badly hurt by a blade venom which could not be healed, but all other wounds were healed.

The party considered running immediately but the coast seemed clear enough and so they decided, so close to their goal to spend a half an hour looking for treasure. That goal was so richly rewarded. the bottom of the river had so many silver coins that they were ubiquitous. Graves swam, sputters, searched, swam, coughed, swam, sputtered and searched, eventually joined by Peri. Graves had better luck swimming and searching because of Peri's earlier poisoning, however, she couldnt be so effective. The party took their cool treasure in the deluxe loot bag and began to hear home. It was quiet at first.

The first encounter was slaughtered within 6 seconds. A giant rock toad that could eat a person in a single swallow. It died. As is the way in the rubble, however, many fights are unfair. So when the party saw in the not-too-distance a group of elves with bows they knew there would be a fight. Mel warned the party about elves and bows and the party sprang into action. Three darkwalls shot up as the party initially went to cover and then relialized their only hope is to bring the fight to the elves. Rushing, charging, casting light walls as fast as the runelord of Aldria and his spirit could dispel them, the party rushed into combat. however there was a gap between the darkwalls and the elves created by a succession of casting within visible range and dispellings from the side of the elves. As a result barbie on the bison and mel burst through the last wall to see three elves with spears set for charge. Barbie thankfully for mel took the brunt of the attack, as a charging bison is oft to do. Impaling himself on a spear, accepting multiple impaling hits Barbie on the bison still managed to gouge the runelord, disabling his arm and nearly trampling him. Arrows were murdering the party as they tried to concentrate on the runelord. The battle was looking bad until the party changed tactics. A darkwall blocked the bowmen from seeing the fight and graves approached
from the rear with his humanbone blade venomed knife. Tarkals bow broke in the fight and so he switched to a melee weapon and
the party joined the fray, trying instead to killthe bowmen and simply hold off the runelord. One by one the initiates fell - the party suffered its losses too though. Everyone was wounded and the runelords allied spirit was dispelling walls, befuddling party members and healing the runelord as fast as he could be hurt. Once all of the iniaties were felled, many from a stab inthe back by graves or else Peri or Phasia punishing staff with crush, it was just the party and the runelord. The runelord fought on however. For over thirty combat rounds (6 minutes)
the fight continued. The runelord died three times, each time brought back by his god. Mel was killed and even his armed was stabbed and killed separately. Finally beatedn down , exhausted, the party won. They looted the bodies healed who they could of their own and found a spot nearby to hide and camp to wait to see what the next day in the big rubble had to bring.

cards.name: RQ 20100605
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

As we started our week off in Pavis, Graves started his Quest for a War Goat. Unfortunately, a Vast Conspiracy seems to be afoot to prevent Graves from finding said Legendary War Goat of Extraordinary Magnitude. Instead, Graves contented himself by going to the Lhankor Mhy temple and taking classes in Old Pavic.
   The other party members spent some time hanging around Gimpy's, only to be entertained by an angry barbarian, sick with grief, who announced (in Praxian, so none of them understood him, but Gimpy translated) that he had shamed his tribe, and was going to kill himself, along with as many patrons of Gimpy's as he could take with him. Phasia promptly befuddled him, Mel handed him an ale in exchange for his axe, and he was rapidly disarmed and being led down the street to the market by Mel. Unfortunately, he snapped out of his Befuddlement well before reaching the market, and Mel and the barbarian had a rather comical battle, with the barbarian punching Mel's plate mail to little avail, and Mel trying to wrestle the barbarian to the ground without causing him serious injury. Eventually Mel prevailed, and fell on top of the barbarian as the town watch arrived.
   With the town watch's assistance, Mel learned that the barbarian was of the Bison tribe, and had been entrusted with one of their holy relics, a "Waha rope", allowing any animal to be held without difficulty. He got drunk at Gimpy's and the rope was stolen, so he had agreed to find the rope or die trying. Unfortunately, being a barbarian, his complete investigative skill set consisted of "kill as many people as possible and then die", which was not that useful in finding the rope. Mel convinced the constabulary to lock up the barbarian for 24 hours, during which time he would try to find the rope.
   Unfortunately, Mel's investigative skills were barely better than the barbarian's, so he enlisted the aid of the rest of the party. Graves asked an urchin for information (the small, childlike kind, rather than the seafaring spiny kind, though with Graves you never can tell), and the urchin demanded 10 gold wheels for information. The party concluded that someone important must have stolen the Waha rope to make the information that valuable.
   Peri and Phasia approached the girl who manages the "line standers" at the entrance to the Pavis rubble. She knew the information, and agreed to provide it in exchange for an unnamed favor at a future date. (Turns out she's a priestess of a cult of a goddess that protects children). Apparently some Lunar bigwigs were in town for the celebration of the Yelmalio high priest's anniversary or some such, and had been asking about artifacts that would be "important to" the barbarians. The Lunar bigwigs were staying at the Silk and Plume, the nicest inn in town.
   A plan was hatched. Peri and Phasia turned on their feminine charms and got a pair of dates to take them to the Silk and Plume. They overheard plans to give the Yelmalio priest an "important gift", and noticed them carrying an ornate box of exactly the right size to hold a Waha rope. Mel went to fetch barbarian boy. Graves and Tarkal hung around outside the Silk and Plume, waiting for opportunity to strike.
   Unfortunately, the plan went a bit amiss when Mel, trying to lead the barbarian back to Gimpy's to get his weapon, spotted the Lunars leaving the Silk and Plume. Mel drew the barbarian's attention to the Lunars and the box, and the barbarian gestured for a weapon. Mel looked away and the barbarian grabbed Mel's sword and charged the Lunars. Mel chased the barbarian, yelling, "Stop, thief!" The barbarian cast a spell what wiped the mind of the box carrier. (Scary stuff). Another Lunar summoned a special elemental called a Lune that drove the barbarian insane. Deciding that discretion was in order, the party allowed the Lunars to proceed unmolested. The barbarian died, and the rope was not recovered.
   Fortunately, it turns out that getting the barbarian killed in a horrible way was exactly what the barbarians wanted. They invited the party to a feast in their honor, and party members were given great gifts. Phasia received the barbarian's spirit so she could bind it. Mel wanted an animal to feed to the trolls, and was instead granted a war bison. Phasia named it, "Curly", in the hopes that if Mel didn't name it, it wouldn't die. Graves asked for a war goat, greatly confusing the barbarians. He ended up getting a nice bow instead. Peri and Tarkal got nothing, though Tarkal did take second in a drinking contest. (Mel rode his bison around, greatly impressing the barbarians, and Graves fell off a bison, but redeemed himself by showing great prowess with a bow).
   The rest of the week passed relatively uneventfully; Mel finally met with the trolls at the "troll market" that takes place every night just outside the rubble, but was unhappy to find nothing but merchant trolls, barely better than trollkin. He and a troll traded insults, he gave the troll a pig, and little was accomplished.

   Finally, back into the rubble! Peri and Phasia retrieved Ken and Barbie, while Mel rented Patsy 3. Best... Patsy... EVER, as you will see! Mel tested Patsy 3 by having him jump onto Curly's back. Patsy 3 promptly fell off, thus proving his worth. Ken and Barbie were unimpressed.
   We were escorted by Bison riders towards the southern breach into Pavis, so we were finally avoiding using the main gate. We were pursued by two priests in white robes. We stopped to find out what they wanted, and, when they refused to tell us why they were following us, Mel handed Patsy 3 his crossbow and instructed him to take a shot at the priests, figuring Patsy would put a good scare into them without hurting anyone. Needless to say, Patsy 3 rolled an 04, and impaled one of the priests in the leg, promptly crippling him. Best. Patsy. Ever. As the party fell over laughing and the priests cried, "We're non-combatants!", Mel replied, "This isn't combat, this is target practice," and gave the priest a Healing-2 so he wouldn't bleed to death. The party proceeded unmolested around the outside wall of Pavis, and into the breach.
  Unfortunately, the Bison riders' idea of a "safe" way into Pavis involved riding between hostile Yelmalio worshipers on the left, their allies, the hostile elves, on the right, and hostile trolls beyond that. The bison riders suggested that the unmounted party members (everyone except Mel) would be in trouble. Tarkal loaned Patsy one of his bows. Hilarity ensued.
  A group of 15 Yelmalio horsemen charged our 13-member party (the five of us, Ken, Barbie, and Patsy 3, and five bison riders). Our six mounted members rode off to harass the Yelmalians, and Mel acquitted himself nicely by nailing one of the Yelmalians in the head with a crossbow bolt, dropping him. A second Yelmalian dismounted to heal the first, and Mel and the bison riders charged him. We lost a bison to a planted spear, but both Yelmalians lost their lives. In the meantime, the 13 remaining riders charged our unmounted party members.
  Peri and Graves performed to their usual standard, impaling and criticaling with abandon. Tarkal hit a couple of times. Phasia criticaled. Patsy 3 shot Tarkal in the back with his own bow.
  Yelmalians dropped. Arrows flew. Patsy 3 shot Barbie in the arm. Tarkal took Patsy's bow away. (He was 3 for 4 with a bow. Just 'cause 2 of those 3 hits were members of his own party...). The Yelmalians fled, minus several party members.
  After vanquishing the Yelmalians, the bison riders left us, and we proceeded to the Cradle Wash, finally coming within 1 km of our desired destination. That night, Mel finally heard trolls, and invited them to dine with us. Mike the troll came out of the darkness and shared our food, and we told stories of our adventures with the Rock Biter clan. He suggested that if we wanted to endear ourselves to the local trolls, we could defile the temple of Krarsht in the Devil's Playground. We told him we'd keep that in mind. Otherwise, it was a highly successful meeting, and the trolls at least know we know troll ways, even though those ways frequently involve killing each other, so we're not safe from trolls.
  We decided to call an end to the gaming that morning, just before heading in to our final destination. We reviewed the map, and Graves' study of Old Pavic paid off immediately, as he rolled a 17 and translated the map for us.

cards.name: RQ 20100522
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

We finished our week in New Pavis almost uneventfully: Peri and Phasia rented themselves slaves from McCleary's (they named the blond-haired, blue-eyed one "Ken", and the barbarian impala rider "Barbie". Remarkably, "Barbie" liked his new name better, as it indicated that he was covered in barbs, and therefore more manly). Mel rented "Patsy 2", who was quite enthusiastic, but who didn't quite reach Patsy's manic "yes-man"-ness. The only event worth noting was that "Worse than Death" claimed another victim, this time right within the walls of New Pavis. We weren't particularly worried; our heads probably aren't valuable enough for him/her to bother with.

Back to the ruins, with the usual waves to the bettors, alms for the poor, and complete disdain for the non-slave mercenaries.

Our first night passed mostly uneventfully -- we heard nearby rustling, but a check in the morning revealed that it was a lone humanoid camper, so we figured he was using our proximity as a shield.

The second day brought forth new misadventures. A band of baboon warriors, including a rune lord in full iron plate armor, ambushed us. Graves was hit by five Disruption spells. Tarkal tried to help, and was similarly hit with multiple Disruptions. Graves bravely returned fire with a MultiMissile crossbow bolt, and managed to impale the rune lord's leg, taking him out of the action, or so we thought.

Both parties cowered in cover, them to heal their fallen leader, and us to reload our crossbows and figure out how the heck we were going to deal with a rune lord in iron armor. Graves expertly hid in cover and moved to higher ground to get a better shot at their party. Peri dropped arrows over the wall between us, and, being Peri, managed to nail a baboon in the head.

Soon, a shimmering baboon popped over the wall. Phasia tried to Befuddle it. Unfortunately, it had some kind of reflective spell placed on it, and Phasia Befuddled herself. The baboon was slain by the hail of arrows that also hit it.

The baboons tried to flank us by going around the outside of the fallen building we were in, but Mel and Patsy 2 were guarding the rear. Mel gracefully leaped over the wall at the first sign of trouble (an 03), while Patsy 2 gracefully banged his face into it (a 98), and was rewarded by another hail of Disruption spells. Patsy bravely stood his ground as the Rune Lord came around the corner, accompanied by one baboon wielding a "magic stick", that seemed to be able to cast Healing, Protection, and who-knows-what-else spells. The other four baboons came pouring over the wall. Two of them engaged Mel, while a third engaged Ken, and a fourth headed for Peri.

Battle ensued. Patsy 2 bravely engaged the rune lord mano-a-mano for two whole rounds, before Tarkal and Barbie joined him. Graves fired the occasional arrow, though he was impeded by the rune lord's allied spirit, who kept nailing him with Disruptions every time he popped his head up to shoot. Ken and Peri killed their baboon, and Ken went to assist Mel while Peri went after the rune lord.

The rune lord did what rune lords do. Patsy was impaled through the head and died. Peri was impaled through the chest and almost died (-5). Tarkal was crippled in the abdomen and continued fighting from the ground, leading to his being impaled through the leg, and even with his massive 22 hit points, was reduced to -5 hit points. Things looked dicey. Fortunately, Phasia chose that time to decide that it would be better to attack the fuzzy beasts. She healed Peri while Mel quickly dispatched his baboon. The rest of their party focused their efforts on "stick boy" and he dropped. Mel, choosing between the rune lord and the last baboon standing, chose the last baboon, and was lustily derided when he rolled a critical and killed it instead of the rune lord.

The rune lord, seeing his party vanquished while only one of ours was down, decided that discretion was the better part of valor, and high-tailed (high-rainbow-butted?) it to parts unknown.

Mel healed him after the critical. He even got to take a shot at the departing rune lord's rear end. Stubborn man, that Tarkal. We have the "magic stick", though we haven't figured it out yet.

The party found plenty of loot: The magic stick, some loose change, and jewelry worth over 1400 silver pennies. THEY decided that discretion was the better part of valor, and headed back for New Pavis.

On their way, they were intercepted by a representative of one of the bettors, who offered them 600 silver pennies (total) to stay in the ruins for six more nights, or even more if they killed Ken and Barbie. The party declined and he withdrew.

The final night was marked by an attack by four fairly incompetent Wolf Brothers. One of them failed to manage his jump roll to get to our camp, and plummeted off the roof. The others managed to miss various attacks and parries and were cut to ribbons alarmingly quickly.

The party returned to New Pavis, sold their loot, rested for a week, and planned their next misadventure. Ken pointed out that entering by the Barbarian gate would eliminate most of the dangers they'd been facing, so that is the plan for next session...

cards.name: RQ 20100424
cards.content:
{{+date}}

 

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

We got hammered enough by the stupid rug rats that we're only good for 1-2 more fights. (I used up both of my POW crystals healing people from last time). I would guess that we're going to have to bugger out, heal up, re-equip (better leg armor, anyone?), and head back in. A waste of time and money, but a lot better than finding ourselves deep in Broo territory with no hope of getting out.

With this assumption, starting at 4:00 pm on Saturday (minus Graves and the presumably-honeymooning Berwyn) would give us time to get our tails handed to us one more time, we could probably quit by around 10:00 pm, and there's no Troll in the Troll Hole to disturb us. So I vote in favor.

The party spent the next two days shopping in New Pavis.
- Graves and Mel went to the main market, where Mel was hoping to buy some fine lamp oil with which to burn broos. Graves was enchanted by a crystal merchant, who offered Mel and Graves great hospitality, and Graves proceeded to talk about a "greater, longer-term partnership" between the merchant and himself. He invited the merchant to dinner at a later time, and managed to procure a Protection-2 matrix at a discounted rate. Graves returned with Peri at a later time, and continued to press for a long-term relationship, and specified a time for dinner. The merchant eventually arrived for dinner, all prepared for his marriage to Peri, only to find that that wasn't what Graves had meant at all. He left politely, but obviously devastated at not having the chance to wed a "teenage girl looking for drinks". Graves returned to his establishment and purchased large sums of crystals (a Healing-6 crystal and something else I missed), but had to deal with the merchant's son, as the merchant
was too devastated with loss and remorse to deal with Graves again.

Mel had a far less melodramatic purchase of two 40-liter kegs of fine odorless oil, though Graves tried to make the purchase more dramatic.

Peri and Phasia did girly things that I didn't understand.

At last, the party set off for the Pavis ruins. You are not supposed to use the dominant tribe's animal as a pack animal, so, as the Bison tribe had just suffered a humiliating defeat, Mel purchased a bison to carry the oil. On the way in, a salesman offered slave mercenaries for only 200 silver pennies each, with a 100 penny rebate if you returned them alive. Mel joyfully bought one, named him Patsy, and made him ride the bison. Other party
members were less than impressed, though Graves desperately wanted a slave of his own.

The party quizzed Patsy on his previous exploits into the ruins. His first was apparently uneventful, and on his second, he performed an admirable impersonation of Nodwick by living off of rubble runners for several months after his party failed to return. The party's first encounter was a group dedicated to the rebuilding of Pavis. They were suitably mocked. The party was then attacked by roughly 40 rubble runners (racoon-sized crosses between armadillos, rats, and crocodiles). Lucky the bison was eaten. Mel had his usual luck, and probably would have died again if Patsy hadn't bravely jumped on top of his prone body and protected him, along with his troll arm, which is apparently far deadlier when Mel is unconscious. (Mel: 2 rubble runners. Troll arm while Mel was unconscious: 4). Graves performed the majority of the damage, and Mel took the majority. Remarkably, no one fumbled and finished Mel off. Once again, Phasia and Peri did girly things that I didn't understand. Tarkal was there, too, it seems to me...

We called it quits when the Troll returned to his hole looking rather bleary-eyed, and Lisa threatened to rip the arms and legs off of anyone who tried to prolong the game, or make any "Urkel" jokes. We didn't understand either. At the moment, we are healed up but fairly low on power, Lucky the Bison is dead, the oil is gone, and we're pondering what to do next.

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

 

 

Peri, Phasia, and Mel arrived in the 3-building village to the southwest of Alone, only to find the residents suspicious and terrified. Most of the denizens were gathered in the tavern, with crossbows trained on the door and the door locked. Peri's brilliant, "16-year-old girls looking for drinks!" got us in, and we learned that some portion of the Orlanthi army had resorted to banditry once the battle was lost. The villagers had lost most of their material possessions to bandits, and were below subsistence level. We offered to hire a guide to take us to the next town, and were provided with Timmy/Willem/"that kid", a 12-year-old boy we would pay 20 silver pieces per day to get us to the next down, and who we would then escort safely to Elpin with all his worldly goods to get him away from the war. Mel was outraged that the villagers thought so poorly of Orlanth, and donated a Wheel to the town. The party was saddled down with letters and packages to deliver on their way southwards. Our rations consisted of overboiled chaff, that had the advantage that it could be used as sling stones in an emergency.

The first leg of our journey was uneventful: The first night, some nearby traveler was eaten by zombies, but apparently that was enough to sate them. We arrived in the second town, which seemed rather prosperous, although low on supplies. They informed us that the Lunar census had already come through, and taxed them almost everything they had in order for them to become Lunar citizens, but now that they were citizens, they were left to their own devices. We got better foodstuffs and proceeded south, with "that kid" still guiding us.

The third town was the rare "two building" variety. We warned them of the coming census, and they promptly hid many of their valuables with our assistance. They were grateful enough that they offered to let us stay for the census and claim we were residents so that we could claim Lunar citizenship, but we declined, worried that the census-takers might have truth-sensing spells. They warned us that the south was rife with bandits, and the southeast was held by two Wind Lords who were trying to regroup the Orlanthi army on the north side of the river.

We traveled towards the Wind Lords, and were captured (without a fight) by an Orlanthi scouting party. (Tulgar's "Detect Enemies" spell nearly got us killed, but did convince us to cooperate). They bound our weapons and escorted us towards the main Wind Lord camp. Unfortunately, about halfway there a second, far less savory Orlanthi party joined us. The leader of the first group surreptitiously cut our bonds in case things got bad, and that night none of us slept. While Mel and Tulgar feigned sleep, Peri and Phasia were in grave peril of losing their dignity. Fortunately, Phasia's brilliant oratory roll kept the rogues talking through their entire watch, and they were sorely disappointed when the next watch arrived and they did not get their way. Unfortunately, the leader of the unsavory party was on the next watch, and "liberated" our lead mace troll gift from the mule, paying Peri the paltry sum of 20 silver pennies for it. Surrounded by one group of known enemies, and a second group that would have to choose loyalties once the fight broke out, we chose cowardice.

The next morning, we approached the leader of the first party and asked his advice on how to get our property back. He said that the only reasonable course was to challenge the leader to one-on-one combat. So, as the parties arrived in the Wind Lords' camp and prepared to part ways, Mel declared the unsavory leader a coward and a thief, and challenged him to one-on-one combat. Imagine Mel's surprise when he learned that battle magic was allowed, and the enemy leader knew Bladesharp. The battle raged far longer than anyone anticipated; Mel drew first blood, but had a great deal of trouble penetrating the leader's chainmail armor. Mel's defense was offset by the Bladesharp, and the leader bloodied Mel in many places. Finally, the leader landed 13 points in Mel's abdomen, and Mel fell, BUT DID NOT DIE!!! (Miracles!) The enemy troops were so impressed with Mel's persistence that they healed him, and the leader himself helped Mel up (but kept the mace).
 Both Orlanthi parties decided that Mel was an honorable and valiant man, and the leader of the good party promised to mention all of Mel's deeds (all one of them) to the Wind Lords before we had our audience. At that point, the divine creator (Don) was forced to toodle off and pick up a Russian of unknown origin, and the game ended, just before our audience with the Wind Lords.

I believe that step 3 is always, "Profit!"

> Tarkal recovered her axe from among the broo filth and was
> rewarded with a case of soul wasting disease.

Ah, those wacky Broos! Don't we love them so!
Discussion of the fate of the crate. My understanding is that we're going to:
(1) Attempt to travel with the air elemental to the Rock Biter clan, arriving there before sunrise.
(2) If that fails, send the air elemental on ahead with a note attached saying, "Warning! Iron inside" and hoping the trolls don't take too much offense.
(3) Rest for a week with the Rock Biter clan, allowing Mel to recover, and donating anything we can't carry to the Rock Biter clan.

I think that's the best plan possible: I trust the trolls with Apgar's stuff a lot more than I trust the Orlanth temple in Jonstown, and they are unlikely to eat Mel, since he's so thoroughly tenderized already. (Even an elf would struggle harder...)

I just wanted to raise the possibility of sending Mel and the elemental all the way to Jonstown, and hoping the Orlanth priests are honest enough to wait for us. I don't like it, but it does reduce our load.

Well, Mel to Jonstown takes Joe’s primary character out of the game for at least half a session but does add the ability for him to be healing while off the road so if the party tries to make it to Jonstown (relatively) quickly then maybe he can be back in character before the end of the play session. It is also possible (probably?) that they will provide healing.

If I remember correctly the crate contains both Mel and Apgar's  Iron Armour and sword and a nothing else of real value.  Now since taking anything iron anywhere near the Trolls without being officially a "TrollFriend" could prove very dangerous to the rest of the party.

However, as Joe pointed out I would trust the Trolls more than anyone in town, and since it is Apgar's possessions that we are carrying and he was a TrollFriend to that clan , and since we are returning to the clan with news of the the Trolls who went with Apgar we might get away with bringing the Iron into the area.

As much as I like the idea of just sending Mel and the Elemental along I like the idea of keeping our cards close to our chest and everything together.

If anything we could always throw Mel on a litter and send someone, healthy, of equal or lesser size ride in the crate to JonsTown.  Of course this plan would depend on travel time, a day in a crate, OK, more than that would not work well.

So unless we are going to send someone else to Jonstown I vote we just aim the crate at the Troll village.

Btw that iron armor has a street value equal to perhaps all of your silver and the gods blood crystals combined. If I remember correctly purchasing iron (when you can purchase it) is 100x the cost of bronze armor.

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Bruthe]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak| Tarkal]]

 

On Tue, Feb 16, 2010 at 4:28 PM, Don McClure <don@digi-element.com> wrote:
    Players:
    Bruce (Jeff)
    Phasia (Joanie)
    Graves (Brandon)
    Cantrememberlisascharactersname (Lisa)
    Mel (Joe)
    Kurst  (Tim)
   
    The game started with the party reaching Jonstown, which looked like a martigras festival just came through. Or an army. More probably the latter. The party took the road north to Heron Green, a smaller village, after crossing Danger Ford, where a group of 150 warriors held a second defense to cover for a retreat. Since its never been used,  it was mainly filled with veterans of multiple battles who didn’t feel a need to be on the front lines and get the glory. The party briefly discussed the road north and then finished the road to herongreen.

    They spent almost no time in the town, but did notice a well traveled road heading to the northwest and indeed some straggling groups of warriors who perhaps had not bought the provisions they needed or had a lame horse or were too drunk to travel properly. In clear diametric opposition is the 1-horse dirt path headed north east, marked only by the sign in tradetalk “Danger: trolls” . Needless to say, the party took the road less traveled. Contrary to popular belief, the party ran across a legitimate but limited business opportunity to mule up some supplies top the town of Alone and make a few silver pennies. The party agreed and hoofed it for two days at maximum load up and down hills in the beginning of the summer.

    Alone is a 9-stone-building-thatched-roof town with large pointed stakes protruding on the inside of buildings, doorways, and around the well. The party quickly found the general store, Fizzy’s, where the goods were to be delivered and met one of the brothers Fizzy who explained many things. Firstly, that the spikes were to protect against giant wasps, secondly thanks for the goods, here are your silvers and thirdly, thanks for the bottle of Pelorian brandy, maybe I can offer you a group discount on dark tongue training.

    The party spent a week learning dark tongue a language ideal for sneaking around and not being heard. The party learned about troll customs such as how to be invited into a house (you will have a sheet placed over you and a ritual blessing of “I extend my darkness to protect and comfort you”_ and also when entering a troll house that they will go around the room twice and explain the things not to touch. The first round is instant death and the second is only probable death. The part was also taught some ability to tell the clans of the Vale apart and how to offer gifts.

    The party headed north and then northwest to attempt to enter into the Vale as close as possible to Rockbiter territory. They ran across a hunter holed up in his cabin, with whom Graves had a bright and productive conversation. On entering the Vale the party was attacked by 6 Broo (chaos goat warriors) well organized into two rows. Lisa dropped one with an arrow and upon contact Phasia drooped another with her quarterstaff. Disruptions were cast and missiles fired. The battle looked favorable to the party  until the pivotal moment where Mel, on horseback and after exchanging blows with one of the cretins, was stabbed through the leg on his horse and fell unconscious as the horse, thankfully, road forward and in the direction of Graves, who could heal him, and Lisa’s character was stabber through the eye with a spear after trying to parry it with, well, her bow, which turned out to be less than wholly effective as a parrying weapon and in summation, slew her then and there, killing her, dead.

    The party though did manage to rally and kill the last of the attacking spearmen leaving their blockers with little recourse but to run. Of them two got away. Graves searched the bodies and found: (1) evidence that they had been very recently intensely trained (2) evidence that a charcoal moon had been drawn on their left hand and then smeared off and (3) a disease spirit which infected Graves.

    The party pulled together their corpse, their gimp warrior, and sneezy and headed deeper into the vale. After a day they ran into trolls and after negotiations were invited to visit the clan. After some talking and some gift giving and some orating the party was given access to shelter and a shaman and ended up staying with the rockbiters for a full week to recover. A shaman of the trolls took a journey to the spirit plane and recovered the spirit of Lisa, which was shoved ceremoniously back into her body and she awoke. Graves had his disease healed. This involved both Kurst and Phasia to owe the shamaness a favor – one big favor and one small favor. 

    The party found out that these broo attacks also include a mysterious 7th broo which the party suspected already and that the broo attacks to the northwest had forced the trolls to send more hunting parties in that direction as opposed to the center of the vale. The two consequences of this have been (1) that the trolls do not have as good of an idea of what is going on in the center of the vale and (2) that the troll hunting parties have been running up more against humans and as a result have increased tensions with the town of Alone.

    The party also found out that Apgar definitely came through and, rather than go after the queen bee jelly, decided to follow up on a Lunar trading caravan that evidently had passed through recently after his arrival (maybe a season). Some trolls had gone with him. No one was heard from again.

    The vale is very dangerous. Nevertheless, the party headed out into the vale. After a fight with giant ants which left Joe almost dead (again) they came across a trail which lead to the opening underground from which broo and sandaled footprints were apparent.

Errata:
(They Call Him) Tim's character is named Tarkal, Lisa's is Peritonitis "Peri" Anadonia.
You probably meant Saturday, Feb 27th
The disease spirit which infected Graves did not make him "sneezy." It gave him (mild) Brain Fever, which sounds much more manly. His brain may have become sneezy but only I know that and will be taking it to my Graves.

Additional errata:
- The broo speared my right arm, so I'm relatively 'armless. Fortunately, I chose to be left-handed at the beginning of the campaign, because I find that being contrary is often useful.
- I died twice (went to 0 HP), once with the broos, and once with the ants. Remarkably, with the house rule that you can be healed from 0 HP within X rounds and survive, I survived both encounters. Who knew 0 HP would be so common?

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Bruthe]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak| Tarkal]]

 

From: Don McClure <don@digi-element.com> Date: Wed, Feb 3, 2010 at 12:27 PM

The party topped the crest of a hill to look upon Jonstown. The town of Jonstown was visible somewhere in the middle of a sea of tents of all shapes
and sizes. The din of training and carousing could be heard long before individual faces were visible. In the town the party split up. Mel (Jo) and Tim went to visit the temple of Orlanth to determine Apgar's next steps. There they met with a priest willing to cast a divination. The divination generally pointed to the north and the east. Bruce (Jeff) went to town for bromance, found some Donandar-worshipping bards (Donandar being the 'Lord of the Dance' -- god of entertainers). Bruce pumped the bard for information and was able to get secure an invitation to join a thieves cult if he stole a magic cup from a wind lord.

Aphasia (Joanie) and ??  (Lisa) strolled around town looking for trouble, which they found quite handily in a fight between several Vingan warriors and barbarians from Prax over the role of women in society. Lisa joined in the fight and represented. ?? (Eric) watched the various fighters train and spent the most time
watching the Humakt, which seemed the most disciplined. The magic cup evidently turns bad beer into decent beer. Bruce conceived of a plan to buy a keg of bad beer and a keg of decent beer and 15 or so cups. He also borrowed from Iswalde a magic coin which when flipped and called, will allow a person to tell any sort of lie to one other person and be believed. They then went to see the wind lord and his initiates, standing around a table taking turns drinking from single cup. With new beer, the party (sans Jo and Eric) interpolated itself into the drunken escapade. Lisa and Aphasia distracted a few with her womanly wiles and Graves told the story of the fight against the scorpion men. At the proper moment (which Lisa created picking up her earing), Bruce switched the cups -- and fumbled, dropping and breaking one of them. The party isn't sure which. Bruce put whichever cup he had intot he bag and pulled out another cup, one which didn't look particularly like the magic cup. The drinking was coming around to the Windlord when Lisa pulled him away. The party then extricated itself and ran to the tavern, where Bruce became convinced by his 'employer' that he had broken the magic cup, but Bruce was still allowed to join, simply without the credit of the magic cup against training. Once there they heard a bellow from a mile away concerning 'thieves' and decided to leave that very night for Jonstown. The party walked late into the night.

At Johnstown the party slept and then chatted with various folk. Eventually the party met with Gringle, who owns a pawnshop and who recently bought an item which was raided from Baboons. When Bruce was caught thieving from the shop, the party (sans Bruce) was pressed into accepting payment to defend the shop. The party prepared the shop by putting two people upstairs ina position to fire down on the main room, boarding up the majority of the windows and centralizing the majority of fighters in a place to respond to an attack either in the front or the back. The owner, Gringle, also a priest of Issaries, detected that detection spells were being cast and enemies were nearby.

The party met with Apgar's 'second wife' who knew Apgar was truly married and had an arrangement with him both because they had children together and
to avoid some kind of levy she claimed was placed on homes with no man as a head of house for the town's defense. She mentioned that Apgar would always
enter into the Vale of Flowers on the northwest end, as close to Rockbiter clan territory as possible. Apgar had a friend whow as of the rockbiter clan. She asked that if they find a green scarf that they return it to her.

That night, at Girngles, the evening started off silent. Girngle and Quackjohn seemed relaxed, the defenses we in place, and the party was prepared for a fight at a moment's notice. The baboons approached, bat on the front door sand climbed to the roof. Much to the party's surprise they began pulling off ceiling tiles. A group of hired mercenaries then broke down the back door and closed to engage in melee. The baboons seemed to have some magic and as they dropped in from the ceiling cast disruption. The fight was brief and bloody. Eric ran one of the mercenaries through, baboons were killed by arrows from Aphasia, Graves, and Tim. The mercenaries were killed and the baboons surrendered. The party was paid and headed back to Johnstown.

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Bruthe]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], and [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]]

 

From Duck Point the party ventured to Westtown (I misspoke during the game). In the town the party sold about one third of the peppercorn =-- some to individual rich people and 100 lbs to a merchant. Inquiries were also made concerning Apgar at the local Orlanth temple, which was in the center of town and which was surrounded by the general market.

The temple over the course of the next day did Divinations. The priest told the party of one part of the Divination, wherein the names of Joe’s character and the priest were inscribed on leaves and thrown up into the wind and both were carried by the wind to the north, though Joes name came face up and the other leaf of Apgar landed face down. This was considered by the priest to be a bad portent. There was also some kind of a name on the wind like “Trintan”

The party was asked to escort an elderly scholar, Iswalde, on their further journey to Boldhome. About halfway along the trail, the party  was a pproached by a young man, a shepherd, who told his  desperate story of scorpion men waylaying him and his family. The party continued along the road, and as it was dusk and there was no joy to be found fighting chaos at night, chose to camp along the road and wait for day to walk through the area where the scorpion men attacked. Eric’s character and Lisa’s character flanked the party on either side of the road and the majority of the party with Isalde and the young man waled with the hand cart down the road.

True to form, the scorpion men laid on the party, three of them brandishing swords along with their poisonous scorpion talks. They had the torso of a man and the legs of a scorpion and stood one and a half times the height of an average man. As the scorpion men approached, Lisa’s character impaled one through the heart with an arrow, dropping him. The second was killed in general melee and the third was wounded by Joe’s Character and then Eric, sneaking up behind, jumped on the foul creature’s thorax, stabbed it in the back and then slit its throat.

The party tacked the dead beast to their camp and found there that one scorpion man had already been killed the night before, with the other three not bothering to even awaken, and that the hostages had been dragged some 200’ from the camp and hidden below. The party recovered successfully the wife and the father and the older brother. The party accepted an invitation from the family and joined them at their  herdstead and was greeted by all of the inhabitants within a day’s walk, who had been called for a feast. The table groaned with food as three goats had been roasted and much of the jarred delicacies were opened for the occasion. Brandon was selected to give the speech telling of the deed, which needed to be translated by Iswalde.

The father presented the party with gifts such that the farm was probably near bankrupted – 10 goats and 200 pieces of silver. The party had a brief moral quandary about the silver but eventually took it, leaving the goats in the farm’s hands to care for them.

The party from their made it to Boldhome, a city cut into the side of a mountain with walls so thick it is many minutes’ walk to pass through the gates, a city held up by seven temples built out of the rock and holding up the interior as pillars.  Strangely, the party was actually approached by temples asking them if they would like to join their cults. Even the acolytes sent to ‘recruit’ the party were surprised by this – it had never happened before. The party spent 5 days going door to door selling peppercorn for the best price and afterwards took a week off to rest. Some trained skills, others (such as Eric, and unknown to the rest of the party) made discreet inquiries with those who murder for money. Lisa went on a hunting expedition with her newfound friends and got the stags antlers made into a helmet. Brandon joined the temples of Issaries and Orlanth – Joe joined Orlanth.

The party after a week headed north to Johnstown. Along the way, stopping early that day, they came across what looked like an abandoned road that lead to a village, equally abandoned. Upon further investigation they found one woman alive and several villagers who had seemed to have been eaten. The party searched the houses and eventually flushed out 2 ghouls, who of course immediately attacked Joe and Eric, who were out front. Using a strange scream they demoralized Eric, who steeled himself to swing nonetheless. Joe fought the other courageously as Brandon and Lisa closed to the fight. As Brandon and Lisa arrived one of the ghouls was dispatched, but the other bit into Joe badly enough that he was incapacitated and poisoned.

The party dispatched the other ghoul, saved the woman. Eric raided the houses for cash. The party met up with Iswalde back on the road and all headed together north to Johnstown. On arriving the party agreed they would spend at least a week healing and so cleared checkmarks for increases for the second time that evening.

Participants: [[Don McClure|Don]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Bruthe]], and [[Joe Good|Mel]]

 

 

From: Don McClure <don@digi-element.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 28, 2009 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Next Game Jan 9

Eric – sorry to hear you were sick.
Lisa & Brandon – hope your vacation is going well
Jeff, Joe, Joanie – thanks all for showing up
Next Game – Jan 9th 1 PM

Last game synopsis:
The party agreed to find out what happened to the Wind Lord Apgar, who lead a group of mainly young Orlanth initiates on along journey to the Vale of Flowers to the north northeast. Neither divinations to the god of storm and wind nor to the god of safe travels on roads were able to provide any information. The party was given a week of additional training in weapons, as insisted by the Sword of Humakt, and were given 20 bags of peppercorn to trade along the way, of which half was meant to fund the party’s journey and the other half to be sold on behalf of the merchant who funded the venture. The party was told in confidence by the wife of Apgar that he had a woman in the town of Apple Lane just outside of Jonstown who he no doubt would visit, despite his blustery denials.

The party journeyed up north along the river as riverboat guard and were attacked by newtlings, who snuck on the boat at night. Two of the crew were murdered in their sleep before alarms could be raised. A pitched battle ensued in which party members tried to get their armor on as they were being skewered by tridents. Through successive healing spells and wearing down the enemy’s magic, the party was able to prevail. On the boat a merchant from Peloria was met, who taught some to speak Pelorian and spoke of the glory of the Lunar Empire.

The party rightly guessed that Apgar would take the most dangerous and direct route and got off the river at Wild Temple, which is located in the middle of Beast Valley. There were only a few tents and maybe 60 humans out of 600 or so people there. The humans were mainly traders with the beast men (centaurs and other half-beast-half-men, ruled loosely by the hero Ironhoof) and priests of different off-center cults such as ancestor worshippers, as well as shamans and the priests of minor god who use the Wild Temple. The languages spoken here were mainly beast-speech, sartarite, and tradetalk. The party was told by an Orlanthi priest  performing an ancient ritual that Apgar did in fact pass through. The party took the slightly safer road to Duck Point.

Upon reaching duck point they found an orlanth temple and a wind lord of orlanth, a duck, whose name was not Howard. He did not remember Apgar as he was fighting undead in Delecti the Necromancer’s swamp at the time but had heard vaguely of a wind lord coming through town. The merchants of the town don’t remember the journey. The party not speaking Sartarite at all has become a bit more of a problem as towns connected by roads are being entered and a single culture (Sartarite) is becoming more dominant and a smaller percentage of people can be interviewed.

I forgot to mention our finances, and we're going to have to decide how we're going to work them at some point: Is it one giant pool, or do we divide evenly after each session?
Here's the situation. For the December 12 game:
- We had 24 silver pieces (S) in a community pool
- Lisa has a "bag o' stuff" worth 200 S. We didn't touch it
- We received 200 S from the troll. Joanie and I assumed this was to be divided evenly between the four of us, so we took 50 S each. I spent mine on a large shield. Joanie kept hers.
For the December 26 game:
- After being felled by my comrades (did I mention I have a Charisma of 8?), we were forced to pay 40 S for additional guards. We used the 24 from the pool, and Joanie fronted the additional 16 S.
- For the trip from Wild Temple to Duck Point, Joanie had to pay 13.5 S for our provisions.
- We received no loot, except the two Healing-5 balms.
So in theory, if we're dividing treasure evenly among participants after each session, Jeff and I owe Joanie roughly 9.8 S each. If we're using a giant pool, then participants need to agree before we do foolish things like buying shields. (A shield which, I should add, saved my life quite nicely when a newtling impaled me with his trident).
The most logical thing is probably a "split" -- 25% of each session's take goes to the pool, and the other 75% goes to the players, but that's also the most complicated. Which probably shows why I'm a mathematician.

Addenda:
- We traded two bags of the peppercorns already: One for a cart to carry the remaining 18 bags, and one for three (now two) Healing-5 balms.
- It will be just me on the 9th; Joanie is otherwise occupied taking the kids to multiple birthday parties.

cards.name: RQ 20091212
cards.content:
{{+date}}

Participants: [[Don McClure]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Lisa aka Peri(tonitis Anandonia)]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Joanie aka Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Jeff aka Bruthe]], [[Joe Good|Joe aka Mel(anoma)]], and [[Brandon WilliamsCraig| Brandon aka Graves]]

 

On Dying Day of Death Week during the particularly rough Sea Season of 1601 the party is shipwrecked near a village one day West by sea from Nochet City. On reaching shore, members of the party swim back out to the wreck and down to salvage what they can. Phasia brings back _____. Graves brings back a box with a decorative egg inside.

On the shore, the party is beset by small ugly bipeds, later revealed to be called "trollkin". On dispatching the trollkin, members of the group cobble together what armaments and armor they can from the deceased, and proceed to the village. The village, Elpin, features an odd jobs board and temples to Orlanth (Wind Mastery) and Ernalda (Earth Fertility) from which Riverboats trade . [something about Hortlanders] Dragonewts are seen and described.

 

Thane Griswald (Windspeaker?) offers a reward for Troll Killing upon which we intend cheerfully to follow.

 

An Orlanthi Runelord, named Apgar, has been gone for over a year, and we receive directions to travel up the main road and take the second turing on the left to find a walled, four building compound. Turns out Apgar had a lover down Apple Lane who also kept him away for extended periods.

 

On pursuing the Apgardian agenda, we are attacked on the main road by bandits who came from the southwest: 8-10 trollkin + 1 dark troll. Weapons include slings, rocks, and magic. After besting the aforementioned combatants, we discover that the Shadow Plateau on the other side of the river has lots more trolls.

 

After meeting Mrs. Apgar and various others attached to the estate we hear a story of Trolls and Gods wherein Yelm/Sun is slain and darkness/hell pervades. [Zirakzeran?] [Any priest but Sun or Dark to may learn spells fo 500sp?] The party sleeps the night, during which a sheep is lost from the compound's stock.

 

Day 2: Farmers breakfast after waking

The party spends eight hours in the forest during which we battle 1 Dark Troll and 6 Trollkin. The Dark Troll pays ransom in the end to save himself, but Peri (Lisa) shoots him anyway. He runs. Graves (Brandon) pursues but loses him, thanks to a "Darkness" spell the troll is able to cast around himself.

 

Back at the compound, accepting the quest to seek Apgar, we are offered and accept two weeks of training at the Temple of Orlanth [equiv. 200-400sp/person/wk].

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Jeff Hohenstein|Bruthe]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]], and [[Eric Winters|Berwyn]]

cards.name: RQ 20100410
cards.content:
{{+date}}

 

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]


With no small amount of trepidation, mainly due to the party's concern that a certain forced-teetotaler  Windlord would soon be judging the life and death of the party on a forced permanent alcohol withdrawal hangover, the party entered into Crickston, home of the Orlanth Liberation Front (OLF).

Crickston had some two thousand orlandth warriors and an equal number of refugees. All looked like they were from the more purely Sartar families and all were wildly, rabidly Orlanthi, with some other lightbringers and earth worshippers mixed in. A palisade , in constructions, with an inner ring of warriors standing no more than two meters apart guarded the nine buildings
that once made up this fishing village. The party was escorted to the first barricade and then asked to either show they were Orlanthi or else join the cult on the spot.

Of everyone Tarkal refused and he stayed outside with six orlanthi as the remainder of the party went in  to meet the Wind Lord. The party cleaned up, and met with the Wind Lord, who was flanked by a man in iron with the death and truth runes on his shoulders. The Wind Lord seemed to have a recurring wound in his abdomen. Phasia described the party's journey quite eloquently. Near the middle the frothing young Orlanth priest shouted out that they must all be spies because one of them wouldn't even join the cult and began accusing people left and right. Graves basically shut him down by turning the question on him and the Wind Lord himself silenced the Wind Voice.

Out from the shadows steps Iswalde (Now caller Ernor) who vouches for the party. The Wind Lord puts the responsibility of the party into Iswalde's hands.

The party is lead to a tent and given burkas to wear if they step outside and are ferried rather quickly and quietly to Boldhome. In Boldhome they are put up in the finest part of town and everything they could ask for is brought to them -- training, spell teaching -- whatever. For twnty two weeks the party trains as Lankhor Mhy pour over the scrolls.

In the end the party is sat down by many of the luminaries of the town and informed that they alone were qualified to perform a ritual that would protect some future army from the effects of the Crimson Bat. To perform this ritual the party needed to meet certain criteria. One of those criteria could be fulfilled in the far off city of Pavis. The party acceded to their
noble calling and in an armored wagon and with 10 pounds of gold were moved to the shoreline over two weeks, where they met a Sheshnelan trading vessel headed to Corflu.

In the small village of Corflu where once stood a mighty port town the part bartered with a river captain who agreed to take them up river. Initially the fee seemed exorbitant but the party did see the captain paying bribes up the river through sun country. The party was then ambushed by roving nomads who through a volley of arrows and spells before running.

In the fight, Tarkal nearly died to an impale into his head and many were wounded. Graves distinguished himself with a multimissiled crossbow bolt that managed to kill three barbarians in a single hit! Three of the guards of the boat were killed outright and two were maimed. Of the barbarians, it appears over twenty died within a few seconds of conact.

In the city of Pavis the party met with their contact, Gimpy, rented a room from him.  Peri worked her usual magic at the bar and met up with a potentially useful contact. Graves made a definite impression on the bar. Mel met with a character by the name of Herbi who sells maps and bought a map to a potentially lucrative endeavor -- to whit -- to go diving for
treasure.

cards.name: Draft Letter Frager v2
cards.content:
Sensei,


I'm writing to reconnect with you and ask for a short meeting. My name is Brandon WilliamsCraig, and we met as I was departing from a day of work with Huston Smith and you were arriving for a visit. After meeting you in Dr. Smith's foyer and having him instruct me, in no uncertain terms, that I should teach for you, it has been my pleasure to watch you in action, especially at events surrounding the launch of the new image archive. My only regret is that I didn't appear at your proverbial door and begin knocking sooner.

 

I just finished my Ph.D. at Pacifica Graduate Institute and, after dedicating myself to completion for the better part of a decade, am seriously in need a job. Shortly, I will need to take work of any kind that will lift the burden of supporting us from my wife's shoulders, and if I could chose any job it would be working for and learning from you, offering students a window into the work of James, Jung, and Hillman, while widening my reading of Huxley and Rogers and assisting with whatever administrative duties presented themselves.

 

I have attached a resume and CV, outlining my teaching, administrative, and aikido experience, but what I hope for most is that you will read my letters of recommendation and communicate with Huston Smith, David Lukoff, Kayla Feder, or any of the other professionals of our mutual acquaintance, and let me know when it would be convenient to meet in person. I would have liked to bring more finesse to this letter, and I hope that it hasn't come across as too personal, but I am profoundly motivated by both my financial situation and a strong desire for authentic work that reflects my vocation. Please let me know what next steps you consider appropriate.

 

Warmly,

 

Brandon WilliamsCraig

cards.name: Draft Letter Frager vDad
cards.content:
Dear Sensei,

My name is Brandon WilliamsCraig.  You and I met in passing at the home of Huston and Kindra Smith. Shortly thereafter,  Huston, whose council I greatly value,  suggested to me that the professional direction that one chooses upon the completion of their PhD degree is of the greatest importance.  In light of this, he suggested that an alliance with you would be, in his view, my ideal next step.  Since our brief meeting, I have familiarized myself with your mission.  Once again, I am awed by Huston's insight.  You and I do share profoundly in our common goals.  As I write to you now,  it is my hope to communicate a strong desire to be helpful without any trace of presumptiousness. But, although you have already made major contributions, and I arrive hat in hand, it is my belief that there is synchronicity in our meeting that could profit us both.
As I am clear that your life is dedicated and very busy,  I will try to be brief.  My current problem/opportunity is immediacy.  I thrill at understanding the Chinese symbol for chi which represents simultaneous states of great peril with great opportunity, but the thrill is somewhat  obscured by the anxiety of the immediacy of next month's bills.  Although I work with Kayla Feder as a Fourth Dan Aikido instructor in Berkeley  and my wife, Lisa,  works full-time as a Montessori directress, the crush of undertaking and  completing my PhD degree has put us in dire straits financially.  It disappoints me to approach you with so little finesse, but, being a man of my word, I will bring all my energy and commitment to my next opportunity to work and I would so like my desire to be of service to be fully utilized. 
I have attached a resume and CV, outlining my teaching, administrative, and aikido experience, but what I hope for most is that you will read my letters of recommendation and communicate with Huston Smith, David Lukoff, Kayla Feder, or any of the other professionals of our mutual acquaintance, and let me know when it would be convenient to meet in person. Once again, I would have liked the tone of  this letter to have been more gracious,but am profoundly motivated by both my financial situation and a strong desire for authentic work that reflects my vocation. Please let me know what next steps you consider appropriate.
Warmly,
 
Brandon WilliamsCraig
