cards.name: SCT2010 Invitations
cards.content:
To the process

 

Sent 20100813

 

It is often the case, approaching an event that will work with difficult material, that participants question their energy level and commitment to the process in the days before gathering. This message provides final details before we gather tomorrow, and asks that you revisit and renew your intention to participate, in whatever way we have agreed.

I have been working intensely on this conflict for several weeks such that I had to get some other things done in the last two days, which reduced the speed with which I responded to your emails. I am VERY grateful for the materials sent to me, have read them in full, and have included them in my prep. I hope, beyond adequate expression, that you will attend. I also hear from some (and accept) that you are having your doubts. I hope to reassure you that your best hopes for the event are still very achievable.

What is in danger is the opportunity for voices to be welcomed which have not been given adequate hearing, especially in a public forum, and have the community bear witness. If you don't come, not only is there a risk of unheard voices feeling even further isolated (or failing to appear at all), but also the community will not be representative and the differences which need air will not get it. If the event loses the presence of those with a deeply considered critique, another consequence will be the unfortunately accurate narrative that an authentic process was created by a professional facilitator in response to concerns and, at the last moment, those with a grievance withdrew and prevented their concerns from being addressed. Obviously there is more to it than that, but that becomes an indelible part of the story, more often than not, in situations like this.

Personally, I put an immense amount of time into this because I believe in the right of the community to hear every member fully, and because I hoped to make it more likely that each participant might have an opportunity to give and receive something near what they need. Even so, don't come because so many of us have put so much effort into giving a real conflict process a chance. Come because each individual has a right to be heard in and by the community, and because we have momentum, after needing it for so long, to model how this is done for the future (not just the dojo's but rippling out to every body of which we are members), to learn to respond early and reduce needless suffering, and to stick with the process despite the potential disappointments.

Please

  • Email me to confirm your intentions (and send your survey and agreement if you haven't already) This is me asking you directly, "will you be there?"
  • Visit http://culturesmith.com/wagn/Shusekai_Conflict_Training_2010, sign in, and click on the > arrows to scan the gathered materials.
  • Dress in your gi (no hakama but with an obi) with a shirt underneath, so we may train and then head in less traditional directions by opening or removing our gi tops. Please do not wear scented body products if at all possible and make any special needs known by phone (510) 962-3921 or in the moment.
  • Bring:
    1. Food, either to share or eat yourself, depending on your mood/needs at dinner time.
    2. A water bottle or identifiable and sturdy drinking receptacle
    3. A brief personal check-in to start, lasting at most ten minutes. What is the most important part of this process' past you'd like folks to keep in mind? What is the most important aspect in the present that is entirely independent of outcome? What is the most important potential outcome of our time together?

Looking forward to tomorrow,

B

 

Sent 20100808

The Shusekai Conflict Training will be this Saturday and Sunday, Aug 14th and 15th, which is by far the most widely approved of date. One hitch has occurred, however, in that Aikido of Berkeley has a children's gasshuku happening until 1pm. As we intend to use AiBerk as our site, this shifts us into meeting from 1 until 9pm with a one hour dinner break. As suggested before, we will close by meeting Sunday morning, in an as yet undecided location near the Downtown Y, from 9-10:30am.

If somebody has a line on a space with mats available all day Saturday, or a place near the Y for Sunday morning, please let me know. Until you hear otherwise from me, the above schedule is our plan. If you are on the fence about coming, please find a way to join us. If you are still on the fence, after this impassioned plea, please make contact and allow me a chance to address any questions or concerns you might have. Please also visit http://culturesmith.com/wagn/Shusekai_Conflict_Training_2010 and give the materials there some consideration, particularly the FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions). Since the materials are specific to this training (and therefore only for Shusekai members), sign in is required. If you have any trouble signing in, please request an account using your full name as your ID, and I'll make sure you have access right away.

Looking forward,

Brandon


 

Sent 20100804

 

Brandon WilliamsCraig here, with an invitation to the Aikido Shusekai Conflict Training. Various issues are outstanding which require the careful, martial attention of the community. A facilitated response derived directly from aikido principles has been chosen to assure the conflict is done well hereafter, in response to current concerns, as well as in order to cultivate a full and ongoing community conflict practice. If you would like to participate in the training outlined below, please complete the following steps:

  1. Read this email in its entirety before responding to any individual item.
  2. Visit http://www.doodle.com/x3nmsx2x3infhph5 and outline your weekend availability through September.
  3. Send your responses to the information requested below to brandon@culturesmith.com.
  4. After a day or so, look in your email inbox for an invitation to the Culturesmith.com website and respond by signing in right away to verify your contact info and find the preparatory materials at http://culturesmith.com/wagn/Shusekai_Conflict_Training_2010, like what to bring, who is invited, some suggested reading and explanations, etc. Culturesmith.com will include resources which need your attention before we meet. Sign-in required.

The process I offer will not technically be a mediation, for several reasons I will explain, but will be a conflict training workshop, and will include the survey and agreement below, keiko, exercises, and group process circles, at very least. I will begin with a strong facilitator model in which I am "sensei" and the participants are learning process arts, in this case an interrelated system of theories, called Healing Friction, which lead to ways of working through conflicts, called Martial Nonviolence. Participating in the survey and agreement below is mandatory, as is making a donation to support the professional time dedicated to creating the process. Payment details are in the agreement, but I'd like to have an informal guarantee from several Shusekai members that they will make significant contributions. Payment will be in one lump, over and done before we start. Please contact me by email so we may have clear expectations.

 

The group will meet for a weekend retreat lasting 9am-12pm and 1-5pm on a Saturday at Aikido of Berkeley, with a final gathering and closing on Sunday morning near the Downtown Berkeley YMCA from 9-10:30. If you must miss any part of the training, please make that abundantly clear in your responses. The process will also include two neutral observers/elders, one male and one female, who may offer suggestions to make the facilitation more nuanced and act as parallel listeners when a participant finds they have a need but insufficient time or safe space in the group. Neither will directly facilitate.
 
Please forward this email to anyone you suspect may need or want a voice in the proceedings, but do not release it to others. This exchange includes design information I depend on to make my living, and fascinated but otherwise uninvolved parties muddy the waters.

Looking forward,

B

Please let me know what next steps you consider appropriate.

cards.name: SCT2010 FAQ
cards.content:
Question: What's the plan again?

Response: Saturday 1-6pm and 7-9pm at [[Aikido of Berkeley]], followed by a Sunday morning concluding session near the YMCA from 9-10:30.

Here is the Invitation/Agreement again

{{SCT2010_Invitations|closed}}

 

 

Q: This is a bit complicated for me.  Just let me know when it is.

R: Apologies for the complexities. As there is important stuff wrapped up in all the words, how may we work to be sure we have similar expectations and are working together? That is what the poll (to figure out a response to "Just let me know when it is"), agreement (to be doing the same work), and questions about the conflicts (to be headed in a useful direction) are about. If it seems complicated, might it make sense to ask somebody you trust to accompany you through the material? What would make this process more you-friendly? Please ask for whatever you need and don't overload yourself such that you lose your way and interest.

 

Q: Do I have to come/stay for the whole thing?

R: In order to address boundary concerns, I've built into the design a structure which will allow both participation and the opportunity to reinforce separation from the dilemma and the Aikido Shusekai community, should that be needed. We may be to a point of closure by dinner Saturday and end early, or may not, but anyone may opt out of Sunday morning to make clear their independence from the remaining work to be done. I request that, instead of making plans to leave early, everyone invest in this being about shared training which everyone values for its own sake, and not being only about Aikido Shusekai or the current dilemma.

 

This process will succeed in so far as it is about conflict education and not about any particular agenda. Imagine it like an excellent classroom of any kind. An effective student is obligated to have their own check-list of things they have identified as needing work, but they are in the learning situation to go through a guided process of inquiry and application. This work (Martial Nonviolence) is about both talking and walking "aiki" values that are often hard to materialize in real conflict. It is not about getting anybody to come back to Shusekai, or removing anybody from Shusekai, etc. so the logic of, for example, "I may not want to keep training" would not lead to "so I am not committing to being there any longer than the time it takes to be heard." We (the participants) don't know what precisely will happen or how much or how little time it will take to find essential bits of learning. We do know that the group will know what it has chosen to do with its time when we adjourn no later than 9pm Saturday night, and again at 10:30 the next morning. I ask that you trust the process.

Especially as we are now meeting 1-9pm at AiBerk on Saturday, I really hope your participation will be open minded and open ended - with no plans to leave before the group adjourns, so that the process may have its own integrity and everyone may see that everyone else is there to learn how to hang-in. Staying makes process agreements possible even when the heat feels a bit much, without resorting to what could feel like hit-and-run tactics. Having the community provide allies to endure the heat of conflict together is the behavior that is lacking and the consideration several people feel they were unfairly denied, and I think it will make a big difference if everyone hangs in to the end. If you feel like you might want to leave, in fact that might be the perfect time to say that aloud - you would like to but won't because conflict requires real commitment to carry off well.

 

Obviously, in the moment the student may choose to leave the mat or the classroom to do what is best for her/him, but I hope to articulate that option while shifting things, as facilitator, so the heat does not get too much for anybody to keep training after a water break or a bit of time to the side. Please help get folks there and offer reassurance that they may rely upon the support of your presence. At the same time, it is necessary to make clear that each individual is responsible for her/his own training with the support of the community. That support has been lacking up to this point, and the gathered group will change that behavior when we meet.

 

Q: What's the cost if you get a lot of people (i.e., if the number of people and their income levels puts you comfortably over, say, $1250 for 1.x days)?

R: I have thus far:

  • created five meetings (on average an hour each) with Nick(x2), Lisa, you, and Justin,
  • spent at least ten hours in phone and email consultations and negotiations (and at most 15)
  • devoted five hours of design and web-based preparation
  • committed to eight and one half hours of facilitation during the event

which, under normal circumstances, would total a minimum of $1425 for a non-profit, directly vision-aligned organization and at least $7125 for a for-profit business or ideologically unaligned group. Professionals in my position most often have no organizational support infrastructure, no healthcare, no retirement, etc. and so charge from $50-$250 an hour, depending on the group served. At this time I have been looking for sustainable employment since March and am nearing the point of accepting any income of any kind. I don't expect Shusekai to generate a large amount, have done the work thus far with no real promise of remuneration, and am very happy that you have such high expectations of financial support. I will give Aikido of Berkeley an offering for the use of the space. If we generate upwards of $1000, I'd be happy to entertain proposals about putting that money to some other use, offering ongoing consulting or a follow-up session, or some other experiment.

 

Q: I find myself needing to change my responses to the Doodle poll. But I can't, because of the secret/locked nature of the poll. 

R: Notify me by email and your entry will be deleted so you may have another go.

 

Q: My schedule makes the proposed dates problematic for me. I'll see what I can do. If it's possible to add more dates to the poll, that would probably help. Otherwise, I'll work with what I've got.

R: I don't know what might get in the way of your attending (perhaps a bit of group help/trouble-shooting can help?) but, as delay is one of the primary issues causing escalation, I highly recommend the maximum amount of flexibility and scheduling ukemi on the part of everyone truly committed to a meaningful conflict process. If the scheduling process could happen with a minimum of misunderstandings and projections on anyone's part ("THEY are just trying to delay/control/escalate/etc by making the logistics difficult"), I think the process will be significantly smoother.

Q: I can't/won't come, but the work is essential. Is there any way I can help?

R: I totally understand and respect your decisions to opt out of the conflict process. I'm also craving your experience and voice in helping to create a best possible outcome based on the community's capacity to deal with conflicts of the kind which continue to arise. Please respond to the poll questions, so we have your wisdom to work with. I'm happy to receive/make individual calls, but I lack the time required to convert an interview into an accurate and 100% confidential record I can print out, make notes on, read several times, etc., which is what I need. If you don't mind writing a bit, I could call/meet as well to ask some questions and clarify some points. Please believe that each individual is a unique source for information/perspective that can really make a difference. That is why I hope you will reconsider your shedule choices and attend.

 

Q: If you're not mediating, but rather teaching conflict resolution, why the issue tagging in the invitation poll?

R: Because the process of identifying issues and classifying them according to their energy value for you (Big Deal vs distraction) not only maps the terrain of the dilemmas to aid the participants and mediator/facilitator, it also prepares the group to own and locate itself within that territory. I'm not offering conflict "resolution" either, but conflict facilitation training. We will map the themes and hot spots together. This is different from triage for a problem that will be resolved, the object of mediation and conflict resolution, and takes a bold step into the idea that we live in and through conflict as a community. Aikido doesn't prepare you to finish off your uke, only to transform the fist fight from what they thought it would be into something mysterious in which "resolving" The Opposition is not the aim.  Likewise, [[Martial Nonviolence]] assumes the constant presence and value of conflict themes, thereby causing most particular disagreements to transform into processes in which all relevant issues may be addressed in a satisfying and sustainable way.

 

Q: The Opposition is not going to change, so what's the point?

R: "Getting other people to change" is not only allegedly impossible, running counter to the Individualism that is our widely touted birthright as Freedom Loving People, but seen as improper, impolite, and better not spoken of so it may be left exclusively to psychotherapists and other trustworthy concerns, such as multinational advertising corporations and militaries. In reaction agains the mechanisms of industrialism and its propagandas, Progressive mythology holds that one must change oneself or not at all, in order to truly Find and Be Oneself. I have said to many potential participants that changing [Insert Name Here] is not the object. The object, as in aikido, is to train individual and group responses so that differences, which are ever present in some form, and conflict, which is the natural result, are received through means other than The RAC (some combination of the usual three options: Run/Attack/Collapse, or RAC). Specifically, the community is encouraged to train and then work together to get at layers and complexity, valuing the group learning process over any one person's fantasy of an ideal outcome, and expect to go on doing this As Long As You Both Shall Live. What if aikidojos practiced all of aikido and were able to use the high-stakes relational randoris which inevitably arise as training?

 
It is unlikely that Insert Name Here will be told what to do, especially if Insert Name Here is situated in an oft and deeply desired position and/or benefiting from the current chaos. If Change is a good slogan but otherwise meanginless without specifics, then what lessons should the community learn and practice to make Change (the only constant) a move toward what is equitable and even inspiring? Notice that the question is not "what decisive resolving action(s) should be taken" but what environment/practice should be created so that each individuual may make reasonable and authentic ongoing decisions in the group context, given the nature of recurring dilemmas. People frequently make unfortunate choices, especially where others people are concerned. I have no evidence/belief/faith that this can be fundamentally altered as the temptations/dilemmas/self-deceptions are often archetypal (the shadow side wrapped inextricably in the role being played). But the community, being at least a bit freer of the archetypal spell than the players, can be educated to respond in aiki ways just as certainly as their bodies can be taught to blend better at shodan than when they were 6th kyu.

 

Q: What's involved in the 3-day debrief?

R: Everyone has three days after the final gathering to send me whatever works for them as a debrief. I will ask for things, but what is most important is what they think is most important given their experience of the process.

{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]


The game opened with the party leaving the gates of new pavis and entering the rubble. Full of hope and opportunity, the party made its way to the shadow market. At the Shadow Market Mel made a distinct impression on a Great Troll: to whit, in order to get the attention and respect of the trolls, Mel approached the Argan Argar trader, named Benei, and asked him who his guards for the caravan were. Benei pointed to a great troll and two dark trolls. The party then proceeded to kick the guards' asses and so earned the job of caravan guard. This tried and true troll strategy worked better than perhaps desired as the party found themselves the sole guards of the caravan.

On the first day the part encountered, in the middle of the night, a Jack O Bear. First signs that thee was a problems included two trollkin suddenly and mysteriously expiring. The party rallied as the jack o bear and four broo entered the camp. The Jackobear first used its chaotic power of befuddlement on Perri, in order to avoid the death faced by so many before.

The broo ran up to attack and the party met them. Ken fought two, Phasia parried for the befuddled Perri and eventually changed places with her to fight two more. Graves and Mel joined the fight and others fired arrows from the second rank.

As Phasia cast spells and parried, she found herself facing three opponents, including the jack o bear. While wounded, Perri did not fall. The party one-by one dropped the broo and the jack o bear fell to arrows. The party cleaned up the rest of the broo and the camp cleaned itself up and got going.

The next encounter happened early morning. Broo tried to ambush the party carrying a large gorp. This didnt work out. The decoy that was raised up didnt convince the party to fire unfortuantely-- well except graves. However, the real fight started when both of the  broo carrying the gorp appeared. However, both broo were impaled in the same combat round. They dropped the gorp who devoured them. One of the broo cast a spell to command the gorp to attack and as the broo ran the leader was hit with an
arrow -- another impale -- that dropped him. The party ran from the gorp and disrupted it to death -- mainly due to Phasia and her strong magic pool and power.

The next encounter happened later that day -- a hit and run fight with Yelornans who traded light and dark walls with the party. The party was peppered with arrows, no one died. The Yelornans were peppered with arrows -- no one died.

The final encounter was at night prior to getting to the troll camp. Six ogres attacked the party. The party was at a disadvantage, not having armor on, but eventually overcame the ogres.

At the troll clan, Benei told the party that the humans he was talking to when mel interrupted were asking about the party and whether there had been any resurections done on party members. The party remembered that the troll asked the party about it in front of the humans and mel had responded. The humans went away happy. The party spent a week with the trolls, relaxing, healing, rolling on checkmarks.

cards.name: Corresp w ASUC reps
cards.content:
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Motoki M <motokifreemail@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 24, 2010 at 11:12 AM
Subject: This is an email from a different ASUC person.
To: Free Aiki Dojo <info@freeaiki.com>, Romain Barnard <rbarnard@berkeley.edu>

Dear Motoki,

I hope this email finds you in good spirits! My sincerest apologies for the slow response!

I hope hope I can be of some assistance with the answers that I provide you with : )

I would gladly like to help the Golden Bears Aikido Club become ASUC Sponsored.  Although I am no longer an ASUC senator, I was fortunate enough to train the incoming senators on bill writing so it wouldn't be a problemfor me to help you write a bill and to get a Senator to sponsor you.

To answer your three questions:

1)The club wants to hire an Aikido instructor. Can a club of ASUC collect money from the members to pay for the instructor?

Yes. You will have to pick up a form on the 2nd floor that is called a "Personal Services Agreement".

2)I heard that active members of a student organization are usually students, faculty, and stuff members. The club is considering about allowing visiting scholars, alumni, and residents in Bay Area to be members of the club. Does this type of membership meet the rule of a ASUC club?

In the ASUC by-laws it states that "The group must be composed primarily of registered students of the Berkeley campus;".  The way that the Student Affairs office in the ASUC has interpreted this clause is that there could be non-student members allowed into the club but the student members must at least make up 50% of the total membership.

Here is a helpful link that explains the ASUC rules and guidelines when it comes to funding:
http://callink.berkeley.edu/Community?action=getDocumentList&docTypeID=12893&orgID=21942

Also, since you are thinking about having non-student members in the club it is advised that you should write something into your constitution detailing what privileges these members are allowed to have (voting, other important things).

Here is link to required constitution info from the campus
http://students.berkeley.edu/osl/studentorganizations.asp?id=1048

<http://students.berkeley.edu/osl/studentorganizations.asp?id=1048>

3) I am thinking that only students and UC stuff can be officers (president etc.) of the club. Is there any ASUC's  rules deciding who can be officers?

Our constitution & bylaws state:
Only registered UC Berkeley students shall have access to funds contributed by the ASUC; and Only registered UC Berkeley students can vote to form and/or alter the group constitution; so only students can be officers.

______________________________
I hope this email has helped out a bit.

If you could send me a more detailed blurb about the Golden Bears Aikido Club (history, how many years its been on campus, what do you promote) and we'll get a senator to sponsor it and you should be ASUC sponsored within 2-3 weeks.  Also- if the club is in need of funds we can also ask the ASUC for funding up to $150 dollars or $200- I would just need a line item budget
detailing the expenses that would add up to that amount i.e table, chairs, instructor.

Also- I wanted to know if your a Rec Sports sponsored club?

Thank you very much for your patience!

Sincerely,

Franco

cards.content:
I continue to present and develop the research begun with my dissertation, The Myth of Peace: A Culture of Peacemaking, The Process Arts, and The Emergence of a Global Communitarian Mythology, as well as enjoy the writing and teaching that are central to my vocation. I value an atmosphere which encourages learning and the practice of inquiry, a collegiate setting which both sharpens students' thinking and nourishes the soul's expression. As a result, I continue to travel and remain open to opportunities for adjunct work and terms as a visiting lecturer. While engagement with concrete projects anyone may recognize as valuable is essential to my work, the ordered environment of the classroom and training space are also of central importance. I am well prepared to teach undergraduate literature and psychology, as well as provide classes in approaches to peace and conflict, mythology, the history of ideas, cultural studies and critique, and the philosophy of religion.

cards.name: CSL Constitution Template
cards.content:
Student Organization Name
Date Prepared:
Date Amended:

Date Approved (Center for Student Leadership staff):
Approved by (Center for Student Leadership staff) :______________________________

 

Article I - Name
What is the exactly title and any group acronym(s) that will be used in addressing your organization?

Name Restrictions:

  • The following names and terms cannot be used in any part of your student organization name unless your organization has received proper authorization from the Center for Student Leadership and/or the Office of Marketing & Business Outreach: Cal, California, UC Berkeley, Berkeley Campus.
  • The name "Berkeley" can be used only at the end of your student organization's name in reference to geographical location, i.e., "at Berkeley" or "of Berkeley." You may not begin your student organization name with the word "Berkeley".

Article II - Purpose
Briefly describe the purpose and objectives of your organization.

Article III - Membership
Describe who is eligible for membership in your organization.  Are there any restrictions on University students (e.g., grade point average, class standing, etc.)?

Include the following required language:
Only currently registered students, faculty, and staff may be active members in a registered student organization. Only active members may vote or hold office.

If your organization will be recognizing off-campus participants, including your groups alumni, they are to be considered "non-active" or "associate" members.  Describe who is eligible for this type of membership and what rights they have in the organization.

Include the following required language:
We will not haze according to California State Law. 

We will not restrict membership based upon race, color, national origin, religion, sex, physical and mental disability, medical condition (cancer-related or genetic characteristics), ancestry, marital status, age, sexual orientation, citizenship or status as a covered veteran (special disabled veteran, Vietnam-era veteran or any other veteran who served on active duty during a war or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized).

Article IV - Officers & Elections
List the officers of the organization by title (e.g., President, Vice Chair, etc.) or define the leadership structure if another system is to be used (e.g., spokesperson by consensus).
What officers constitute an executive committee?
Describe the process and required majority of votes by your active, voting membership by which officers will be elected or selected.
What time of year will elections occur?
How long do officers serve?
Which officer serves as the primary signatory?
How will officers be removed and/or replaced?

Article V - Meetings
How often will the organization meet?
Who will call the meetings?
What is quorum?
Will there be a call for special emergency meetings? If so, what is the process for determining when a special emergency meeting is necessary and how will you notify members of the meeting?

Article VI - Constitutional Amendments
Who can propose an amendment?
How are they proposed?
What is the required period of time between the proposed amendment and a final vote?
How will you notify active members that an amendment is going to be voted upon?
Incorporate into your constitution that an amendment will need a 2/3 majority vote from your active membership to pass (amendments change the structure of the group and  it is important to have 2/3 approval from the members at large so that there is strong agreement that the change should be made.)

Include the following required language:
All amendments, additions or deletions to this document must be filed with the Center for Student Leadership in 102 Sproul Hall.

If ASUC-sponsored, please include the following required language:
All amendments, additions or deletions must be filed with the ASUC Office of Student Affairs, 400 Eshleman Hall, within one week of adoption.

Article VII - Dissolution
Please address each of the following questions:
How will dissolution be decided?
What is the required majority of votes to dissolve the group?
What will you do with unspent funds?

If ASUC-sponsored, please include the following required language:
All unspent ASUC funds shall remain the property of the ASUC, all Graduate Assembly funds shall remain the property of the Graduate Assembly. Remaining privately-obtained funds may be donated to another nonprofit organization with prior approval of the ASUC Senate Finance Committee.

Optional Addition:

We encourage organizations to include an article in the constitution which cites the type of parliamentary authority to be used for points not covered in the constitution.  Many organizations utilize Robert's Rules of Order.  This often helpls guide groups in times of conflict, or when the constitution is not clear on how to handle a specific situation.

cards.name: BW Management Resume older versions
cards.content:
My first major project, in the 1980's, involved being dispatched to the headquarters of Greyhound International in Dallas to facilitate a reorganization of the central H.R. data system. I hired and managed two employees to recover and completely restructure filing systems in order to set the stage for a technology upgrade from paper filing to digital access. While working for Moving On Center, in the early 2000's in Oakland CA, I updated or removed antiquated or redundant IT components, centralized backup and network architecture, installed hands-free and automated phone and message systems, upgraded to the latest available Quickbooks and office software. As principle for Association Building Community, in addition to my administrative and community-building duties, I was contracted by Aiki Extensions, an international peace organization, to create the position of Executive Director and an administration from a far-flung collection of volunteers with no existing supervision. I raised the funds to provide my salary and in six months developed a virtual international office using free technology, coordinated operations and communications on six continents, brought online an improved website and web-based payment system, instituted consistent book keeping and then migrated that online, established a wiki for member involvement, and integrated a universal backup solution which doubled as content streaming for promotional materials. cards.name: Aikido Shusekai Transition YMCA 2010
cards.content:
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Nick Walker <walkersensei@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, Oct 14, 2010 at 8:19 PM
Subject: [Shusekai] The YMCA & Beyond (Important News)
To: Shusekai Aikido <shusekai-aikido@googlegroups.com>

Dear Aikido Shusekai Community,

As those of you who were at yesterday's class already know, I was called to a meeting today with Noel Panganiban (the manager who oversees the aikido program) and Hae Won Rhow (Noel's boss). I had some reason to suspect that they might be cancelling the aikido program.

The background that I wasn't fully aware of before the meeting is that within the overall Berkeley-Albany YMCA organization (which has been doing a major "re-branding" process and a general re-evaluation of its programs and vision), there's been a general stance developing among many director/manager types that adult martial arts programs - the nature of dojo culture, community, systems of rank, etc. - just don't mesh well with whatever it is the Y is trying to cultivate. A decision was made a while ago, in a big meeting of Y directors, to start phasing out ALL such programs within the Berkeley-Albany Y organization.

The news from my meeting isn't great, but it's not as bad as it could have been.

The bad (or at least bad-in-the-short-term news): we do have to find/create a new place to hold our classes.

Considering that we have to find another place to hold our classes, the rest of the news is pretty good. I've been at the Y a long time, and they know that I attract members and that my experience and qualifications make me an asset not to be let go of lightly. And I approached the meeting in an aiki spirit, and the overall tone of the meeting stayed quite warm and harmonious.

Our recent issues with the youth program staff over mat usage and such, and malicious complaints filed by certain former students, were touched on briefly in the meeting, but turned out to be matters of only minor concern from Hae Won's perspective, and didn't have much impact on how the meeting turned out.

What Hae Won had planned to offer me was that our program could continue at the Y for another month, after which I'd be welcome to periodically teach workshops on specific aikido-related topics (e.g., aikido-based women's self-defense; breathwork & meditation).

The deal that I walked out of the room with (thanks to taking an aiki approach) was that our program can continue as is until the end of 2010. After that, we can't have standard aikido classes at the Y anymore, but I'll remain a Y employee and retain the aikido program's Wednesday night time slot. The Wednesday night time slot will be used for an ongoing series of aikido-related workshops on topics of my choice - i.e., an 8-week term on self-defense, an 8-week term on ki breathwork & meditation, etc.).

So, we have until the end of the year to set up a new place to train. If we don't have one set up by then, we'll have an interruption in our training schedule until we've got a place set up - though the interruption will be mitigated by Eric's Monday night practices, Justin's Saturday classes, my Wednesday night workshop series at the Y, and the workshops Azzia and I will be continuing to put together in various rented spaces.

Arranging a new space will be a challenge, and will require a lot of initiative, organization, and commitment on the part of all of us, but I believe we have a group that can do it. And the continued Wednesday night workshops at the Y next year will provide an ongoing venue in which new students will regularly be exposed to my teaching and possibly drawn to join us in our regular training in the new space.

Since our regular Wednesday and Sunday classes will continue until the Y closes for its December Holiday Break, all belt tests scheduled for October, November, and December will proceed as planned.

Thank you all for your continued dedication to the dojo; I look forward to your company on the next phase of our dojo's development.

Nick

1. my one criticism (or concern) is regarding hagiographical perceptions of O Sensei in relationship to Aikido that I found in some of the Peace week literature. In my studies, it seems like he certainly believed in an idealistic, utopian construct of peace and harmony, and of course he believed in it in the context of the martial encounter. But I think it was actually his son who began to popularize a different construct of Aikido as a path to harmony in any socio- political sense (witness O Sensei's appreciation of rightist support -- he just wanted to practice aikido - he may not have explicitly advocated rightist political views, so I would describe him on some level as amoral, rather than political or immoral). 

I only mention this because we should be careful that we carefully evoke O Sensei's contribution to Aikido (perhaps emphasizing his technical vision), and not distort his idealistic vision(based on shinto constructs having to do with cosmological alignment in contrast, say with Reverend King's clearly activist approach to social change) with our own admittedly wonderful but different perceptions of aikido as a path to peacemaking. 

Ellis Amdur in particular has made some good comments in this context.		 Thu, Oct 7, 2010 9:53 AM Find...

cards.name: Support Aikido at UC Berkeley
cards.content:
An open letter to all who value education, aikido, and the places the two intersect and flourish,

 

My name is Brandon WilliamsCraig, and I am the Chief Instructor of Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley. Aikido and UC Berkeley have a long history which the Golden Bears proudly continue. Beginning in the late 1960s, a series of now well-known teachers founded and then guided the UC Aikido Club. [[Robert_Frager|Bob Frager]] Sensei went on to found the [[Institute for Transpersonal Psychology]], [[Stan Pranin]] Sensei founded the international Aikido Journal, and Allen Grow Sensei founded the Oakland Aikido Institute in which many Aikido teachers in California got their start. Several other well-known teachers trained at UC and remember it fondly. Paul Linden Sensei (Founder of [[Being in Movement]] and [[Aikido of Columbus]]) is one of these. Are you?

 

We would like to find out just how many more there are who benefited from UC Aikido. Since the Sixties, Aikido has emerged again many times as students and faculty trained in dojos nearby and brought their existing love of the art into demonstrations and informal training while at Cal. This is despite the active discouragement of aikido by those who see its practice as being in competition with a lucrative and well-established competitive martial arts program on campus. Several staff members and faculty have direct Aikido experience and know well its many benefits.

 

In the economic climate of 2010 in which UC Berkeley becomes first public university to top $50k in tuition, room and board [NPR] the best way to be sure university aikido flourishes is to support us in whatever way works for you. Please simply connect, with no obligation, so I ask about your inclinations and availability. We need financial support for professional instruction, mats, and a space to train, as even student clubs like us (and kendo and many others) are seen as competition. It would be our great pleasure to invite upper-ranking practitioners for a fund-raising seminar and ask you to share your stories from your time at Cal. Any yudansha might come and train with us as a guest instructor and share your expertise in a less formal setting. The bottom line -- make contact and express your desire to support us. We need you and Aikido's place in Higher Education can always use another champion.

Sensei,

Brandon here. It was an honor to be invited to teach and then to have a chance to work with you during the Aikido and Psychotherapy seminar at ITP. After lunch, when I suggested that I have every intention of working for you you welcomed the suggestion. For that as well I am grateful. My resume is attached, and more may be found at http://culturesmith.com/Professional_Materials. Recommendation and endorsements may be found on that page or be viewed separately here http://culturesmith.com/BW_Recommendations.

As initial exchanges about employment are improved by brevity, I must say that I turn to you not only because ITP represents the kind of program I admire because it is both courageous in looking forward and steeped in tradition, but also that Huston Smith once directed me in no uncertain terms to connect with and work for you. He encouraged me to be bold. I am a sufficiently proficient teacher both on the mat and in the classroom to be an excellent junior colleague in any academic or martial setting. This edge is sharpened by an intimate knowledge of what it is to be a junior colleague with lessons-a-plenty still to learn. I also have a documented record of success in educational and non-profit administration, which cannot fail to benefit ITP, as well as leadership certifications and hundreds of hour of experience facilitating groups. I have been seeking employment for most of this year, while restoring the Aikido Club you began on the UC Berkeley campus, and simply need somebody to give me an honest break - someone capable of realizing the unique combination my skill-set represents. If I don't hear from you in a day or two I will continue to seek you out until we make contact, just to be sure I have the correct address, etc.

With gratitude for your martial and academic contributions thus far and every hope that you will respond with opportunities, critique, and whatever comes to your mind,

Brandon

20100712-13

                                              Assorted Writing

 

Lobdell  Family Reunion 2010 Cedar Rapids Iowa    Monday July 12th, 2010, through next Saturday  The Hampton Inn

 

Yup! Me and ole Julie here at the the Lobdell Family Reunion in ole Cedar Rapids, Iowa.....a by god, fer piece from where I usually hang my hat. I'm a settin' here at my executive desk in room 222 at the ole Hampton Inn while Julie takes some nieces shoppin.  Got myself a nice slow internet hook-em-up.  Lookin' over some pretty damn dry academic stuff about ole Rudyard Kipling.  Feels  pretty damn jiggy for about the first five minutes. Then one begins to  ponder over one'e real situation.  Well this  is the third set of folks who secretly  think that I'm about as odd a human bean as God ( and trust me these folks definately capitalize God) ever put on this earth.  I drove over 14 hours to get here and this set of folks is lookin'  at me as if I wuz lacking thumbs. Yup, the third  brother-in-law who wouldn't shed a tear if I were horizontal and lackin' a pulse.

      Got subjected to a pool (cess) party last night at ole Alex's house in the burbs.  All the men stand around and talk real loud about baseball.  Well, god  knows, I love baseball! But, enough's enough. You should have seen the look they gave me when I said, "It must be pretty lonely playing center field."  and  " How does one avoid a rash with  all the spittin and scratchin?"

       Well there was an awkward moment so I moved out to the entry hall to play with the cat (the only highlight of the whole damn party).  There I was cornered by ole Uncle Gork - real name Bob.  An amazing old fellow who despite being significantly retarded is still able to be highly religious and talkative.  Interesting note: Uncle Gork's wife is in the Guiness World Records book as the "ugliest woman ever created".  This wouldn't be of any real interest except that she was the only adult who decided to take a dip in the ole pool.

     I was trying to get down an extremely overdone hotdog when she began to make the transition into her swim suit. There is just something about taking a dip when you're morbidly obese that flies in the face of appitite.  All the pits, dings, and flaps are pitting, dinging, and flapping and like the sudden appearance of a  snake,  you just can't take your eyes off of it.

       Back to Uncle Gork.  His rather simple approach to life, secondary to retardation,  manifests as obsession.  Let me start by saying that he had on an Emmi Lou Harris tee shirt that he had gotten at a concert.  Did I mention that he has all of her artistic output.  Anyway, ole Gork  perseverates in the arena of anything Harrisesque and glazes over the moment he senses that you are about to utter the slightest sound. This inner moment gives him the opportunity to formulate yet another fascinating tid-bit  obout the object of his affection.....yes indeed,  Emmi Lou Harris.

       Well this is probably about enough.   Oh yea....this morning I stumbbled down to the lobby for what they jokingly call breakfast.  I was trying to focus on a greasey tough biscuit, still half asleep (me not the biscuit), WHEN Gork sat down way to close to me an asked if I was aware that Emmi Lou Harris had recorded a Celtic album. Evidently, there was quite a lot about ELH that he had  failed to impart to me the night before.  As I casually glanced toward the serving area, I was horrified to see Gork's wife inverting the huge, industrial, gravy server and uploading about 5 gallons of the sticky stuff into a to-go bag. I guess if you're married to Gork and don't want to go to Hell - now there's an irony - it's safer, from an after-life point of view, to eat yourself to death rather than drink.  I've heard from some very reliable sources that God is a little chunky, what with all the angle food cake et.al.  The All Hallowed One is probably no stranger to an all-you-can-eat buffet. Just check your history, or as a last resort, read the dread Bible.  Now there's a supreme being with an appetite!

      Anyway, it's much more fun to write this junk than it is to read the Norton Critical Edition of almost anything.

 Keep your stick on the ice,

 Dadlio

 

Tuesday 13, 2010

 

Well I's been Gorked again this mornin'.  His gig is to monitor group homes for criminal adolescents in the Maryland penal system.  Between leers at young women in the breakfast area, he explained to me his unique approach to young thugs.  Look in the dictionary under recidivism and there is a picture of ole Gork.  Well, as you know, I love baseball and justice. So, I ask him if he wanted to see some porn that I had in my room, and upon arriving there, I beat him to death, cut him up into little pieces, and stuffed his parts into my saddle bags.  Oh, I forgot to tell you that I brought ole Clarabell with us.  Now what I need from you is some advice about what to do next.  The bags are now all soiled and stained with blood....wait, here is the problem.  The folks here are too stupid to notice, but ole Clarabell is a hard-core vegetarian and a neat freak. He wants nothing to do with this. Plus, the clean-em-up ladies will be here soon, so time's a wastin.

 Should I:

1.  Pack the saddle bags onto his morbidly obese ugly as hell wife and point her and her fat, retarded grandson toward Maryland?

2.  Drop of the bags at the kitchen and suggest steak and eggs for tomorrow’s breakfast offering?

3.  Submit my name and the bags to the Nobel Peace committee for next year’s consideration?

4.  Make up a sign that reads "Steaks from Omaha" and sell the stuff outside the front entrance of the Motel. I might sing "I'm an old cowhand" to draw a crowd.

Let me know as soon  as you come up with something.  It's startin' to warm up quite a bit here, and....................well ..........................

 Dadlio, (Clarabell says "Hi")

 

 P.S.  Emmi Lou Harris has shown some interest in the bags, but declines the contents suggesting that I put the remains out in back of the motel for the opossums. Now, I am currently on a first name basis with some very cool possums.  And, even though they eat poop, I'm quite clear that they would draw the line at anything remotely resembling ole Gork.

      I'm currently checking to see if there is an Emmi Lou Harris Fan Club here in Cedar Rapids.  If I luck out and there is one, I could drop him off to do some volunteer work..ditch him there, it wouldn't  be my problem.

      Seriously folks, (this bit is actually true)                                                                                                                                  I said to ole Gork, who really loves the Lord,  "Of course you know that Emmi Lou is Jewish."  He said "Oh no.....I don't think so.  She has done lots of Christian recording."  I said," No.I'm quite certain that she IS Jewish.  She's no fool and knows what sells. She records for all the big markets...Country, Christian, Celtic.  I used to play for her years ago when she was up and coming in Dallas. Yes, I'm quite certain that she is Jewish."  Poor old guy is desparately trying to find out if I'm right.  God am I one mean bastard?   I'm really glad that you didn't inherit that from me. Once he gets the real scoop on that, I'm gonna tell him that she's gay.

The Aidan Response

I had an unexpected response to our conversation about getting with your mom and discussing the history of Davy. I hung up and headed toward the library (UNT). On the way, I went down memory lane - thinking back over how Davy came to be in the first place - my family's response to the marriage - how Paula announced the pregnancy - and a host of other things related to becoming a dad. I was feeling really strong emotionally yesterday even in spite of the linguistic debacle. I noticed all the beautiful young women, the smell of the library, the frenzy of the last minute final exam crammers. I found a nice quite place and sat down to read until class. Instantly without warning and with absolutely no sadness, I had eyes drowning in tears. I've never experienced having copious tears without emotion! I have no explanation unless it has to do with my new approach to controlling depression and anger. Anyway, at that time, although you know the story as well as I do, I felt that the early story of Davy probably should be written down. The events leading up to the birth might be important to you in some way not yet clear to either of us. And there is absolutely nothing good to be gained, at this late date, by going back over how horrible the experience was for me in the presence of your mother. So, better to keep that part of the story a blog between us. I doubt that this kindness will detract from the story at all. Obviously, the whole story still has incredible currency for me 46 years later. What a surprise. I really have serious doubts that you need to know all this, but here goes.
I think that I was about 23 when I moved to Austin. I was first and foremost a jazz musician. The match between me and my new environment was surprising and amazing to me. I rolled in with the exact skills to be successful. Every band wanted to hire me and I became the pianist in the UT faculty jazz big band. I think that there were three students in the whole band. The school was academic heaven. What a rush. Your mom had graduated with a BA and had decided to open a theatrical booking agency. She wanted to represent me for private parties and so we began to work together. We weren't ever 'girl friend/boy friend'. I dated several girls that I had meet in classes. Your mom was intelligent, built like crazy, and sexual, and it wasn't long before things got very physical. She wasn't the kind of girl that I usually wanted to date, but the sexual attraction was more than I could resist. I was a 23 year old boy with drives like a Mack truck. I remember asking if she would take care of birth control and she agreed. I felt really guilty. In those days 'good guys' would only have sex with someone that they would want to marry if they 'had to'. I would never have married Paula voluntarily and so sex felt really risky for a lot of reasons.
One day during big band rehearsal, Paula showed up all excited. The band took a break and it was then that your mom told me the big news. I was going to be dad. She was thrilled and acted as if I were going to be thrilled too. I felt REALLY sick and said "I thought you were going to handle the birth control." She said that she really didn't know how to do this and had basically done nothing. BUT BOY WASN'T THIS GREAT. It those days, there was only one thing to do unless you were a real shit head..........walk down the isle.
Paula said that I really needed to 'ask for her hand' with her dad, wink wink nod nod as soon as possible. So we went to Dallas to meet the folks. Craig agreed but it was obvious that I was the last choice on earth that he would have made. He was the ultimate 'fat cat' in those days...obnoxious, overbearing, self-aggrandizing, pompous, and self-made. He wanted his daughter to marry someone just like him. AND once he found out why I was really needed to be there, he never let me up........never make any effort toward a relationship. Then, of course, there were Skipper and Jan.........my God what a pair. Martha was the only one who liked me. I'll always remember that in my heart. Martha, Craig and Paula then began planning the really big fat cat wedding.
I was the only child of two only children. My family was waiting and watching for me to do something spectacular. They wanted a great marriage, for me to be 'something' ......lawyer, doctor.......anything. No one in my family was really very special in those terms. So it was kind of up to me. I was smart, well educated, talented.........maybe......who knows. When I told them what was going on, the scream could have been heard 'round the world! To them Paula was an aggressive, arrogant, obnoxious, theatrical, spoiled, rich girl. They couldn't stand her. Forget about how they hated Craig who postured and talked of his amazing success and simple piety. I loved my grannies as much as you loved Martha and they were crushed and demoralized. I was sick and it only got worse.
If you're wondering what all this has to do with Davy, remember that he was the bun in the ole oven while all this was going on. Paula (little Paul) had always been perfect. It was a sort of a joke. She did everything right ........always. BUT what about now. We never really talked about it but I think this was a real turning point in the life of her mental health. All the sudden the simple act of trapping a stupid, horny, male had compromised perfection quite profoundly. ESPECIALLY WITH HER ADORING DAD...............not good. What IS Davy getting from all this?
My God, the wedding! It was worse than Mickey Rooney proclaiming "Let's put on a show!" The Craig family was united in the play........life was grand,.........what an awe inspiring event. Look at the happy couple. I think Paula was already showing. My family being blatantly non theatrical, looked like they were attending the mass funeral of some crazed, senseless killing. There was a group picture. My family looked like they were being lined-up to be shot. Before walking out to be married and lining up with the groomsmen, I experienced the most horrible, crushing depression that I have ever experienced......like standing before a judge and being sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. This is enduring and mindless defaulting! Labels fail here because even the "best families" handle events in this brutal manner. I no longer want this for us. I know that you REALLY want to be a dad. This is what I want as well. BUT let's change the rules once and for all. Let's give this child a chance by adopting honesty. Why pass on this old crap?

#3 Jesuit: Boys don't know that dads grow-up along with THEM. I thought, "Jesuit...now Brandon can have it all!" I didn't understand at that time that you were listening every time that Craig and I were spouting all that crap about being bigger than authority, and the captains of our own damn ships. So you decided to show them all by wearing a dread uniform covered with pin-ons. I didn't know what to do. Slowly I began to get it when I met the dads of the debate team. They were absolutely greased when it came to promoting their sons and the sons
of others who understood. I was a divorced, band leader living in Lewisville, driving a white delivery van, and desperately trying keep my work schedule and make payments to a soon-to-be ex-wife. They lived well, had excellent values, and intended that their sons have the same. When I saw how I compared to those men it made me sick. When I went to see Fr. Dillon about your not graduating on time the hem in pants cuff came loose where I had pinned it, and I walked out of his office trailing about two feet of extra pants leg. I felt like the poorest white trash. I know that those families weren't perfect by any means, I'm not that naieve, but they lived on purpose not by default.

I feel that inspite of me you have been very successful. So don't for an instant think that don't. What I am saying is that we both carry around loads of erroneous ideas which I largely take responsibility for, and I really don't want to see this family curse passed on. When your mother and I separated, I said for her to choose a counselor for us to decide what to do about you and Meghan. If you remember you told me in the dinning room "You're not leaving without me." After the second session, the counselor saw me alone. She said "Brandon should live with you. Without being too psychological, y0ur wife is a real looney-bird. I said, what a relief she had me convinced that the whole thing was my fault. She said, that is her one real talent. " The day that I had to take you back to Argonne was one of the darkest days of my whole life. I'll never forget it. Once and for all. I'm really sorry that I let you down.

I think that you have, for the most part, largely surpassed me in the psychological maturity department, so I'm not sure that I would make much of a partner in change, but, at the moment I don't see any other dads standing around and I'm never without hope of winning. I just cannot stand to give-up.

I'm taking this opportunity to initiate this because you are currently childless. Before Aidan died things were indeed different. I hear you say that Lisa is teaching you to deal with conflict. That doesn't ring true to me. Let's assume that this IS good for you. But, I'll tell you from experience that a new baby would, given the choice, choose a sane mother over learning conflict resolution. Why the hell are you staying? I stayed. I doesn't get better. It only gets worse. If you have "ruined her life" , tell her to haul ass as soon as possible and get a new life. God, lets change the future! There is absolutely no guarantee that a sane woman is in your future. That's the chance we all take, but Lisa is a by-God known commodity. Of course, if you decide to stay, and you know your situation better than anyone else, I will support you 100%, but I don't anticipate understanding. If you dare another pregnancy, stay until you've completed your doc. and Lisa has her training and a job, and bail out. This strategy would take a lot of the quilt off you if, in fact, that is what is working on you. Guilt directed most of my behavior with your mom after Davy died.

If Julie is correct, Just hit delete and I will totally understand. We'll never mention it again. If not we will begin the journey.

Love,
Dad

Theatre-Why We Love It.

Movie - Notes on a Scandal Judi Dench-rough, 70ish, private school history teacher, closet gay. Cate Blanchett (Sheba) -Youngish new art teacher, ex-hippie, married to older man - came from wealthy family. Scene - Judi has been rejected by Cate. She is in a bath tub with one knee up, on her back, and she is having a cigarette. The bathroom is a sickly pink tile bath. She is craggy, saggy, JUST barely covered with water. The music is a kind of string bass minor drone. The scene begins at the knee end of the tub and kind of slightly above the rim of the tub....about two feet from Judi. The camera moves along Judi's body very slowly towards her head. You hear her thoughts as she slowly smokes and thinks.

"People like Sheba think they know what it tiz to be lonely---- out of the drip,----- drip, of long haul, no end in sight, solitude. ------------They know nothing.--------- What its like to construct an entire week-end around a visit to the laundrette. ----- Or to be so chronically untouched that the brush of a bus conductor's hand----- sends a jolt of longing straight to your groin.--------- Sheba and her like have no clue."

Scene ends with camera directly above Judi (2 feet) Face, shoulders, upper chest, and cigarette. It's the kind of tiny scene that makes a rather ordinary movie totally worth all the money it cost to make it.

Ebertly,
Dad

I listen to people of all kinds quite a bit. One thing I try to remember each time I make a new connection is to end with a ritual question: "If you could ask for a favor, a bit of time, something that would bring you a bit closer to some goal, what would that be? I like to begin with offering a favor." Here are some recent answers with which I would like some help. If you know of any way to move these desires forward, I would appreciate a response. "I would like...

  • To have a willing person or two with no particular skill set donate one hour of "make the world a better place" time each week that I might direct to a single task of my choosing."
  • To have a gig working with kids in refugee camps making art."
  • To participate in a group of people willing to both sit in silence and stillness and also ready to move quickly, speak clearly, and work together all the while refining the ways they work through the differences that arise between them."

cards.name: RQ 20110122
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Mel]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]

 

While preparing to transport Al-Nadir's goods downriver, Graves acquired an intelligent young goat named William, along with a "goat whisperer". Phasia hired a Sword of Humakt to accompany us, while Mel hired Bart and Gart (Humakt initiates). Our merry band climbed aboard the enormous barge (50' x 150', if Don's estimates are to be trusted), along with 8 passengers and 15 crew members, including the captain, Bly.


Phasia and Graves were concerned about the passengers, especially the 5 passengers clad in white robes with cowls that covered their faces. So we interviewed each passenger in turn. To our surprise, the 5 cowled passengers turned out to be Brightgrain and his closest remaining family members and followers; apparently his payment of 4200 Wheels to us for saving his children was frowned upon by the Sun Dome temple, and he had been demoted to regional governor of the newly-acquired farms and territory outside of Pavis. Two passengers were a married couple looking for farming work. The remaining passenger, dubbed "Mike" by Graves, seemed to be a novice adventurer looking for "something". We allowed the passengers to come with us on the journey and we embarked.


   The initial trip downriver was peaceful; Graves trained with his goat. Mel trained with the Humakti. Peri worked on her tan, much to the distraction and chagrin of the Yelmalio. We dropped off Brightgrain, his family, and the married couple at the Sun Dome Temple without incident. Brightgrain invited us to visit him in the future.


   Past the Sun Dome Temple, on of the Humakti noticed something in the distance. Mel had Phasia cast Farsee on him and noticed the same thing: Some kind of movement in the distance. Mel notified the captain, who wasn't concerned: The attack would occur in 6 hours at the Robber's Rapids, and even if we lost the fight, the captain would be able to ransom his way out of it.

 

   We prepared for the fight, and, sure enough, 6 hours later Phasia cast Farsee on Graves and he saw the lookout at the top of a cliff just before the rapids. We proceeded on the barge into the rapids, where two rock walls provided ample cover for pygmy barbarians (impala riders) as they rained arrows on our ship. There were 6 barbarian archers on either shore, but Darkwalls, implanted medium shields, and general hiding in cover minimized our damage. It looked like the party would traverse the rapids without incident until... a horde of spirits engaged the party in spirit combat!

 

   The immediate thought was that we were being assailed by Worse Than Death, but the spirits weren't exactly world-class: Graves and Phasia were attacked by spirits with POW 5 each, and the spirits quickly realized the hopelessness of their situations and fled. Mel wasn't so lucky, and was attacked by a POW 16 spirit. Similarly, Tarkal was attacked by a POW 15(?) spirit, and Peri was attacked by a POW 13(?) spirit. Peri kicked her spirit's butt, but even with Spirit Shield, Mel and Tarkal were in serious trouble.

 

   Graves decided it was time to do something heroic, so he turned himself Invisible and swam to the shore from whence the spirits had come. On getting behind the wall, Graves discovered 25 pygmy warriors, 6 pygmy archers, and a full-blown pygmy shaman, complete with bones in his nose and his hair, very little clothing, and an unusually foul smell.

 

   Graves pondered the situation, and decided to greet the shaman with a Multimissile-4 heavy crossbow. The shaman was nonplussed, and perished forthwith, saving Mel and Tarkal from a fate worse than death. Unfortunately, the 25 pygmy warriors were also nonplussed, and pelted Graves with a barrage of javelins. Graves' thick skin, armor, and Protection-4 spell saved him from certain death, and, wounded, he ran for the ship. Mel gave the order to run the ship around so that he and the other Humakti could "kill them some pygmies".

 

   Graves fled and urged the boat to get back underway. Peri and Phasia rained doom on the pursuing pygmies. Mel chanted, "Kill! Kill! Kill!" Graves ALMOST convinced the boat to move on, but Mel and his Humakti comrades couldn't contain themselves any more, and poured off the boat to engage the 18 remaining pygmies. Tarkal came along to provide comic relief; er, fight.

 

   Pygmy slaughter ensued. The Sword of Humakt practiced his sword work on his victims, er, opponents. Mel got two slashes in a row, breaking the shield arms of both his opponents. Peri and Phasia shot any pygmies who didn't engage in melee soon enough. The Humakti initiates didn't die. Tarkal was hopelessly overmatched; he could not hit and could not parry, but the pygmy warriors couldn't overcome his natural armor and enormous constitution.

 

  Unfortunately, the scene on the other side of the river was daunting: A Waha pygmy Rune Lord, bearing twin battle axes, rallied his 31 pygmies and the 32 of them started riding along the river, most likely for a ford, or to cut us off. Phasia, Peri, and Graves concentrated their fire on him, but he had a Hero power that allowed him to split all missile weapons fired at him in half, making him immune to missile attacks.

 

  Mel sounded the, "Retreat with dignity" call just as he sliced one of his opponents in half at the abdomen. The Sword of Humakt split his attacks and killed both his opponents. The Humakti initiates made progress, killing one of their opponents each. Tarkal remained alive. His opponents were heartened.

 

  As time became scarce, Mel cut his other opponent in half at the chest, the Sword of Humakt killed one of Tarkal's opponents, and the two initiates continued their fight. Mel announced that the party was leaving without them. Graves Disrupted one of the initiates' opponents, but the initiate then wasted a round casting Countermagic on his opponent to ensure a fair fight.

 

  Finally, the initiates downed their opponents, Phasia Befuddled Tarkal's opponent, and the party was able to flee with dignity (except Tarkal). The Sword was impressed by Mel's work, and complimented him. The Sword was unimpressed with Tarkal's work, and instructed him never to stand in a line of warriors with the Sword again.

 

  The trip to Corflu was uneventful. Phasia bargained with the Sheshnellan captain, and Graves warned her that she might not be getting the best deal. We all worshipped the mosquito god to avoid being eaten alive. We sailed back north and visited the Sun Dome Temple. Graves met with an elder priest and learned that, if we returned the ransom, the Sun Dome Temple might look more favorably on Brightgrain. Unfortunately, the party agreed that Brightgrain might not appreciate the gesture. So we sailed north to Pavis, met with Al-Nadir, received over 14,000 silver for our troubles, and decided to spend 2 weeks training with our newfound riches.

Joe
