cards.name: RQ 20111217
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Ted Greer|Torath]], [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Cog]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]. Adding Brendan as Crazy and Ryan as Gohan the Barbarian for combat.

 

{{RQ DMc group treasury|closed}}

 

Fire Illusion Dark 1604

 

Seeking out the local, grateful shamen to help us bind spirits.

  • Cog gets a Spirit Block and then only a POW check.
  • Graves gets a 14pow 7int.
  • Tarkal gets a Spirit Block and then a 17pow 4int
  • Torath uses his gbx4 to enclose a 19pow 16int. The shaman casts bones and predicts that something interesting and significant will occur on our next journey.

1.5 days through forest NE we will find bogs (and no bandits because people don't want to die near the swamp)

Peri, Torath, and Graves get liquid animal fat in small clay pots in a rucksack (50sp per rucksack w 9clay pots)

As we are in Centaur country, no town per se, crossroads w a river dock and 8 or 10 non-permanent tents of 17-25 folks coming to visit Wild Temple. Semi-permanent residents (8-10 households) who are grateful (Ironhoof might look the other way for a season) and will care for them for a season.

 

We leave with 1wk rations per person and 1 ridin sable as a pack animal. It can get a bit below freezing at night and we are headed north. Raining cats and dogs. Tracking reveals that dead things get up and walk toward the swamp from here. Our feet sink a bit into the muck.

 

Wild Illusion Dark 1604

Spot Hidden revelas flickering lights in the dismall distance. Graves hears a forlorn banjo in the distance when we reach the edge of a swamp at early evening. Peri hears spirits offering some kind of entreaty. We return 1/2 hr back to more solid ground for evening camping.

 

God Illusion Dark 1604

Sparverius circles out and is gone for a while. There is a tower in the far distance and strange movements in the fog. Cog does not require his parasol, because there is an overcast natural to this area, except that there is a cold drizzle. Trudge, 2hrs, slogging (defense reduced), Torath is in the lead, followed by Cog (who holds the other end of Torath's rope, and then Peri, Graves, Phasia, Tarkal.

 

Torath comes on large feathers, white, some mottled. Then finds feathered arm w sword attached in the muck. Generic bronze sword in arm dead less than two days (Cog smells it). Seven Druzil were joined by something bipedal and began fighting suddenly. Duck tracks of one go off in a direction away from our "path". We move on. Those that make a listen roll go 5 late this round. Others miss the round as the zombies (1 Duck) arise from the muck around us.

 

Graves takes a hit to the head that does 6 through and drops him unconscious (-1) into the water where he begins to perish, hears voices suggesting that life isn't all it is cracked up to be. Peri sends Loiosh to Heal4 Graves. Cog jumped and landed on Gohan, almost killing him (he only weighs 1,500lbs). Crazy got his legs removed and then healed.

 

10am We notice that the transition from No-man's Land was a subtle transition into Hero Quest. It is a lot lighter. We are still in the physical world, but we are on the edge - where only heroes go. Peri begins to hear the spirits chanting "Daka Fal forgot" (he had separated the live and dead when they couldn't remember).

 

The hawk has been essential. Graves engages his Find The Path. Finds ruins, large foundational rocks, overgrown by moss, etc. In two hours we may have slogged 2 miles. Graves begins to navigate by patches of higher ground, and finds writing in Jresteli "Nothing dies here but hope". Several hear sound of stone dragging across stone. We cast spells as a skeleton in iron chain, greaves, etc. emerges with a classic skeleton broadsword. Graves Prot4. Torath DetEnem the guy but nobody else within 80m. Cog Disrupt bounce (Reflection at least 3). Graves engages and then everyone moves up. The nasty has a natural shimmer of 30, reflection, damage boost, damage resist, 160% attack + Bladesharp. Graves specials through his blend and breaks his back. We continue until

 

Graves gets Iron full helm and chain (1.5x at half the incumbrance) suit w plate greaves and iron bound medium shield (18pt) inside covered in four runes fused together to create unfamiliar patterns. Not magical matrix but used to consecrate the armore giving a hint to original owner. Will need to find ironsmith to get it made ready and spend 1 permanent oint POW to consecrate. Peri gets standard iron broadsword she can use once consecrated 1 perm POW (or not use battle magic).

 

Graves searches. 45 minutes later finds area looks it was a tomb  - stone above ground coffin, empty with pieces of jewelry. After SpiritShield2mtx he collects them wtih no nasty consequences: rare metals and gems (Phasia eval) total btw 3-4000sp.

 

The afternoon hsa two more skeleton fights (Torkal drops 6 pow points). Sparv says we are closer by the end of the day. directly before us there are swirls in the mist indicating something truly huge is between us and the tower, bigger than two houses and smaller than a mountain, mist moving slowly. Early evening looking for high ground. Not dry at top of mound but big enough such that bedding isn't wet until after two hours or so. Middle of night torches look to be moving in distance.

 

Freeze Truth Dark 1604

Morning. Points in bound spirits do not regenerate but personal pow does. Briny, cold, almost freezing, mid-thigh water. Fog never lifts. Leeches. A couple of hours with no encounters. Willow to the right seems to have severed heads hanging, open mouths and begin to cast spells. Vines have body parts in them, moving on their own. Disruptions fly. Cog is Fanaticized. Peri Countmgc3. Graves Countermgc2 and changes to composite bow. Peri lobs oil (25%+att bonus) and Tarkal casts ignite. Phasia Demoralizes Cog. Torath shoots a head and kills it. We perforate the heads, freeing spirits that attack us. Graves binds one by swapping it with his current 4pt. It is a spell spirit in the right nipple ring that is bat-shit crazy & for disruption only and it gives itself POW checks not Graves. Tree burns down, parts of bodies it is animating to pat out fire don't work.

10am

Smaller zombie fights. Not an hour or two goes by that we aren't attacked. Torath begins putting hash marks on his shield for all undead killed. Loiosh (02%) evil spirits about to be upon us. Graves SpiritShields himself, Gohan, and Torath. Cog SpiritBlock2. Two non-corporeal non-spirits form around us: shadowy, carrying shadow weapons, cold all around them and pull heat from us. Confusing and hard to hit (shimmer of 60%). Graves Blshrp2x2(1hp cost) and parries. Saved by SpSh. We can only hit them with magic and eventually win after Torath takes con damage 2 down to 15.

 

Graves finds a good place to camp and then Phasia finds one even better: dry all night and higher up. Guard group sees 35 skeletons wander past below. Get a good night's sleep, which is nice. Sparverius says we are nearer to the disturbance in the fog. It doesn't move much, so let's go around.

 

Water Truth Dark 1604

Mid day bad thing: ripples in the swamp different from ours (coming at us from different direction). Det Enemy (big and almost aroundish us). Zombie Octopus - four tentacles above water. Graves Prot4. Peri has Loiosh Fireblade Graves' broadsword. Gohan's leg ripped off. Graves left arm to -1, then Heal6. Cog got his left arm ripped off, shield vaporized, and lg shield pulled off. Phasia Healed Area on Gohan to restore his leg. Torath used the wand to zombifie Cog's leg.

 

We are now half way to the tower from where we started. Closer in there are less random daily encounters that were once random travelers or peasants.

cards.name: RQ 20111231
cards.content:
{{+date}}

[[Don McClure|Don]], [[Ted Greer|Torath]] absent but represented by, [[Lisa WilliamsCraig|Peri]], [[Joanie Albee-Good|Phasia]], [[Joe Good|Cog]], [[Brandon WilliamsCraig|Graves]], and [[Tim Schlaak|Tarkal]]. Adding Brendan as Crazy and Ryan as Gohan the Barbarian for combat.

 

{{RQ DMc group treasury|closed}}

 

Recap...

Water Truth Dark 1604

Mid day ripples in the swamp began to differ from ours (coming at us from different direction), and a Zombie Octopus ripped Gohan's leg off, almost doing Graves' left arm a similar disservice before ripping Cog's left arm off, shield included, and shattering his mace. Phasia Healed Area on Gohan to restore his leg, and Torath used the wand to zombifie Cog's left arm. We are now half-way to the tower. This much closer-in there are less random daily encounters that were once travelers or peasants. Now those predators are the prey. Allied Spirits continue to regain their power but bound spirits do not. During the night attacks are smaller and more dispersed.

Clay Truth Dark 1604

Wakening to crappy surroundings that Cog continues to love. The meat in our rations begins to move a bit and becomes inedible to all but Cog, who "already has more dangerous things in his gut." Our leather armor and various other items are Praxian and therefore had been prepared with peaceful cut. "Dingy magic" in the air.


Graves' tracking reveals things dragging themselves, and avoid things Super Nasty. There are no tracks (a specific dearth) headed toward the tower. We are moving slowly but Sparverius still believes we are headed int he correct direction.

Marching order: Graves, Cog (w rope to rescue him if he falls into a hole), Gohan, Phasia, Peri, Crazy, Tarkal

Phasia Farsees Sparverius. Graves Finds The Path 09%. a person and some undead have been walking back and forth through this swamp area (transition between hill and deeper bog) frequently and recently. Almost an extended camp area, back and forth at different angles, perhaps a territory in and of itself. Graves Spot Hidden sees person crouching in a dark cloak behind some bushes. Graves opines aloud how much it is a shame that lichen can reveal hiding people and a guy dusts himself off and stands up. He looks older and a bit dirty with stained robes and cowl up. Loiosh follows and sees him pass by two Thanatar guardian spirits. Eval: Stained Boy is 18-22pow.

 

Graves knows he probably has maddness spirits, maybe as many as an ancestor worshipper. The heads on his belt allow him to tap all their skills/abilities. Selfish and wanting power means they often worship other gods as well - Vivamort being a favorite second worship focus. A Daka Fal with "Free Ghost" completely dismisses a maddness spirit when its skull is destroyed and the Lankar Mai ritual is performed.

We opt that he is too much to take on right now and move on. Peri shoots an arrow into a tree and breaks it off for potential later use as a focus of the Giant's Compass, should we want to return to kill Thanatar boy. Graves too is confident he can return. We continue, assuming the nasty will be trying to harm us when it is to his advantage. We would try to cover our tracks, but it takes a heroic power to track here anyway, so NBD. Even Graves does not see tracks of any kind of humany thing.

We continue, making much better time until Sparverius tells us we are more or less right on top of the tower. Walking near some gnarled trees with protuberent roots. Avoiding the roots is not possible, as they form into Evil Wooden Warriors of Doom. Phasia offers the MtxProt4 for everybody. Graves SpiritShield1.


Tarkal and Crazy hurl oil. Crazy casts ignite and it begins to burn beautifully, beginning to walk toward us (takes 4 strike ranks). Graves hurls/hits with an oil pod. Cog Crushes a tree warrior and all the fire on all trees seemingly turns into an elemental and attacks Phasia (potential 1 overall hit point of damage per strike rank), which doesn't get through her protection. Phasia prepares to Dispell4 and Tarkal uses Extinguish (2) before the Disp completes. Two strike ranks later Peri's fireblade crawls up her arm but can't do damage through her Prot4. Graves casts bladesharp2(4) and moves to engage the one attacking Cog. Cog 01% spots a wisp of smoke at a distance and has his spirit cast Jump to land on/in a boiling cauldron around which three hags are casting. Cog disrupts their plans. Brief noxious cloud around the battle disappates and the wooden warriors freeze. Cog crushes the head of the first hag, but the second Taps 10 points of Cog's CHA, while the third Poisons him (he makes save) for 8 CON. Cog is one ugly, sickly, grumpy troll. Graves drops the broadsword to Xbow a hag's head into bloody mist, saving Cog from being "uglied to death."

We all POWx6 check and find the tower breaking through the mist. Twisted forms of various half-people, moving but attached to the walls, all look a us and simultaneously growl "what brings you here?" We explain and inquire after the master. It says "We ARE Delecti." Upon offering the wand, a hand comes from the wall and takes it within. An _uncomfortable_ wait ensues for thirty minutes. "This is pleasing to me. I shall take it." From the ground wells up gems and gold (twenty Enc. Phasia eval: no magic but 80k worth). "Those that wish may enter the tower. Treasures await." All except Krah-Zee and Gohan enter together but all end up alone...

 

[Don going into the other room with us one by one.]

{{+Graves adventure|closed}}

 

Walk out of tower to find Crazy and Gohan guarding 40lbs of treasure and a perfectly normal swamp with a path headed roughly south. The dingy/horrible weather seems to have cleared up a bit. Tower looks like a regular old ruin.

Turns out Cog was told he could take one thing out. Waded through skulls and found Mistress Race skull. Asked Delecti whether if he returned the skull to the trolls its spirit would be freed. Delecti granted "this boon". First flight of stairs led to gems and jewelry. Cog ignored and and continued upwards. On stairs up 4 zombies attacked and one ripped off a leg. Failed attempt to DI, so spirit healed the leg to 0. The zombies tried to rip it off again. Cog became grumpier. Came to three chained prisoners and stairs up that had an "even more powerful guardian". Ignored prisoners and stairs up and left with nothing but the skull.

Phasia went up stairs to an iron skeleton, until it fumbled 97% hit self to do max damage. After prayer of thanks to Issaries went to treasure room on second floor and got stuff. Then to prisoners. As guest could not help release but could negotiate. All Delecti would say is that she might take what she can carry. The duck was light, so could be carried. Up stairs turned Phasia invisible and just parried with two shields to help her get past. Found pouch w magical gem in three clasping bony hands room. Had to carry across skulls which tried to bite him. Duck turned out to be metaphorical.

Peri bi-passed teasure room, planning to come back. Encountered Ghostbuster screaming banshee, draining POW, almost killed Loiosh. One more room before returning. Dungeon: set all three free but could only carry duck with others as accompaniment. They didn't make it. Got treasure, carried duck, skeletons tried to bite. Got a Conceal spell.

Tarkal fought Zoidburg (large guy w lobster claws) and speared him. Treasure room. Unlocked all prisoners. To edge of pool. Carried duck across. One shot rune level Conceal until Rune Lord and can recharge.

 

Phasia evaluates Peri's treasure = 400sp value one nice ruby. Courtesy toward tower before leaving. Once leaving swamp, upon looking back the swamp looks like its old super-dangerous self.Two days out of swamp - very pleasant trip to Wild Temple to recollect mounts. We thank them and they thank us. We are back aprox 1/2 day to NE to Wild Temple. The party plans their trip back to Pavis. East would be directly through Lunar Empire. Cog wants to go south to go to Lead Hills w skull. All agree, but going NE through Vale of Flowers (Royal Jelly for William) would get us to Castle of Lead for Cog. Nah. Going south into Esrolia. No problem with bandits but definitely with thieves.

We decide to take a river raft to Nochet City. Five people on a boat with mounts would be 25/person and 50/animal to get to Nochet City and liquidate gems. In Nochet City, Graves begins recruiting: Slaves are 100sp x dominant attribute and kids are 50sp per (except Cha). Orphans are free. Phasia spends 550sp on an amazing hunting dog, puts bound spirit POW 13 in it, and fees it The Apple (Str 11 Con 17 Sz 8 Pow 13 Dex 16 Bites @60% for d6). Names it Griffin. Cog checks up on resurrection related agreeement follow-through. Peri pays 2900sp and trades in our old iron broadsword to buy "Saphire" from a weaponsmith.

 

Letter from Elejan's brother, Anadar, has been left, saying he will no longer be Elejan's lackey. All his literally tons of stuff has been boxed and is waiting under guard in a warehouse. Anadar has left. We guess we'd better get a boat. Can we send Sparv to Pavis with message? 18 days round trip tops. Clayton stays here as our representative? Silly to have anybody not a master bargainer (starting point) be here trying to figure out logistics of something large. Getting to Pavis is fast (to Corflu in as little as 7 days)/ Getting back is 3-4 week trip. Water flips right around the new year (in a few weeks). Phasia goes through all inventory with Graves' help. Some perishable fruits and veggies are artfully hidden and are perishing. We hire Clayton for 10% of whatever he can sell them for. We continue to go through and inventory gear. Graves gets iron armor reconditioned: 300sp and two weeks.

 

Financial details

80Ksp worth of Delecti's gems etc for wand, added to 89k letter of credit from Lion = 169k deal gross take

less purchase price Lion (45k) and Wand (15k) = 109k gross profit

Our 20% cut = 21,800 -3500 already paid us = 18,300sp + 400 from skeleton = 18,700

Divided by six main characters = 3000 each plus 700 for the group burse

 

January 1st, 2012

 

Recap:

God Disorder Storm 1604

People are planning trips all over, including to Sheshnella, when we enter Nochet City and visit Anadar (Elejan's Brother, a.k.a. Other Guy) El Nadir, only to discover his breaking-up letter and snarky preparations. Peri trades our iron broadsword for Saphire. Graves puts in iron armor for reconditioning. Phasia buys dog. Graves begins Fagen activities.

Tarkal consults Torath about putting spirit in bison and the feeding it the apple. Abomination? Nah, especially given Tarkal's riding skill. Could an animal with a spirit freed by the apple use a matrix? Don says probably yes. We test the Detect Life matrix

 

Trade goods have been organized w malice but not damaged. We look through 1% warehouse in one day. We hire Clayton to be manager and hire other Issaries lackies to help with inventory and re-pack. Hard to find workers in human population at this time of year. Clayton sends Hostvin, the wanna-be hanger on, to help. He does literaly what we tell him with no imagination. Phaisa goes to Issaries Temple. This town provides outsourcing for everything. Two groups: fairly reliable high priced people,or companies nobody wants to work with. Phasia believes 100 person days of warehouse activity are needed.  2-3 semi-skilled people and a bunch of physical labor. Unskilled: 4sp (bonded) or 1sp (shady)   Skilled: 10sp or 40sp. Twenty people could work at one time w/o getting in each others' way. Cog inquires after Argan Argar possibly available to help.

 

Freeze Harmony Storm 1604

Phasia hires 20 bonded unskilled laborers and 5 bonded skilled + Clayton + Graves.

Cog goes to Kigor Litor temple to report, and asks where to find Argan Argar priestess. In the market, of course. She trades with the northern hills and doesn't do shipping. For every master trader they lend, we must finance that troll's weight in goods (of the trolls choice) to trade in Pavis. Phasia and Graves nix it. Cog returns to say he is out of the loop. Argan Argar say they are open to negotiation. Phasia arranges for two Argan Argar master traders to consult and supervise our night shift. They are particularly good at sorting which goods should be kept here and sold slowly. We know what will sell in Pavis. Leather goods not required. Bronze armor and weapons are huge in Pavis. Last of weapons from Sheshnela (weapons move west to east) are still coming in but are being sent to North wall being built by armor. Durable food stuffs , dresses, perfumes, etc of civilization also big in Pavis. The trolls have a big dinner before weighing themselves.

 

Phasia will take care of getting the ship. They know a bit more about what the Trolls in Pavis will buy. Master Trader troll is a dictator but understands things pretty well. Doesn't know what humans sell to each other. It should be between 5 and 9 days to complete the warehouse while getting the ship and selling goods here in parallel.

Peri trains Spirit Speech for a week in nearby Esrolian Daka Fal temple (travelers are "visiting Uncles") with structured ancestor worship. She looks for somebody who is younger scholar/researcher/acolyte not so worldwise, naive, stupid who is likely to worship a hot adventuress. Lacky or squire who will follow and teach Spirit Speech for learning bow and sword. A yound woman, named Mele, is happy to follow and exchange teach/learn. She knows no weapons at all. For 125sp Peri buys training bow and broadsword.

At the port a hodgepodege of activity is almost always in progress. She seeks a captain and finds each archetype represented in the five in port at this time. She seeks stoic, seasoned, grizzled type who looks super-efficient. The Shesnelans are more available than the available Esrolians. A Shesh captain, Noah, goes on about The One God and the native spirit worshippers. She will attempt to get a price for the goods in his hold in exchange for his carrying our "Monsters" (trolls). Cooking wear and etc he has which will be much more valuable in Pavis. Phasia will buy his goods for Nochett price and we will then sell them in Pavis.

One of the trolls, that night, has found what he will be sending with us as well as some bronze pointy (barbecue) stakes, because humans like that kind of thing :-( At least he got a good enough deal. Graves finds that the troll Master Merchant never changes when he is there or not. He is metronomic and will take sales adivce but won't stop swatting the help. Peri outfits Mele with cloak, boots, satchel, leather armor, and she gives a 100sp necklace.


Water Harmony Storm 1604

 

Somebody has swept up the good from the market that Elejan usually buys. There are other things that are available here that somebody who doesn't really know Prax didn't buy. Phasia is able to buy them in fairly large number. Things that might fit bison or impallla, etc. Spear tips. No horse stuff. Graves begins to spread rumors (08% acting) that bronze horseshoes and combat saddles are in desperate demand by the Lost Horse Tribe.


The master bargainers who had been in town sat Phasia down asked if they should strike while the Lost Horse Tribe deals are hot. Cog gets initiates and heads off to crush trollkin. We buy a bunch of peppercorns to trade. Warehouse visited by incredibly old man. Has package under arm. Phasia offers tea. He allows how sad it is when two brothers fight. He offers the tin in his package for 1sp. Send Elejan his regards and let him know there are a few who will continue to trade with him. In the tin is a white leaf tea Phasia will take personal care to deliver.

The trolls here have developed a kind of mushroom not availble elsewhere and will send their body weight with us to be sold up north as rarities. Graves has found a few likely candidates by making offers, free and clear, and looking for a smart kid who, between 6 and 9 years old, can already know a good deal when (s)he sees one.


25% done w warehouse and everybody is hitting their stride.

Cog goes to scene of attack and makes tracking rolls to find that a dark troll was moving to the city and his retinue of 9 attacked him, joined by rebels to make 25. They were in cahoots and the survivors moved off together.

Clay Harmony Storm 1604
Cog and sentry spot each other and Cog tells initiates to hide. 15ish trollkin come to investigate (very well organized - front rank have shields and weapons, second rank has long weapons, third rank casting spells) and Cog jumps to land in the middle of them. Demolishes three and bounces a 1pt disruption. They yell "you can take our lives but not our freedom!" One trollkin says "countermagic" in Pelorian! Five attacks as they wheel. One hits with a damage boost! (grinding sound) They deploy to defend against the incoming initiates. Potions deployed. Cog jumps and nukes three more. A shield guy blocks twice and then three w damage boosted spears attack over the top. One of the troll initiates gets speared to death, the other gets crippled and lies on the ground but is able to defend himself by doing nothing but parrying, Cog manages to dispatch the remainder of the trollkin.

Four days total until
Cog gets back and reports that the Lunar Empire is supporting the trollkin.

We have 2/3 warehouse of stuff that should stay (none perishable) and a shipload of gear ready to go to Corflu and then Pavis. We make Clayton our rep. Graves attunes armor w one permanent point of Pow.
Guards will cost 10sp/day/guard. Six on site should be able to protect the stuff. 700sp/season including his salary. The stuff here will just be held. Phasia leaves 3000sp from her funds (to be repaid later from Elejan?) with Clayton. He will not trade it and the real estate taxes have already been paid for a year.
Ship ready to go.
{{+Contract w wards|closed}}
Graves has found, Raleigh, an 8yr old intelligent/crafty willing to take me up on my offer. There are some people in his earlier life he will need to pay back when he is old enough, and he needs to go and learn from me. Graves puts Raleigh in charge of:

  • large bronze shield, leather armor
  • dagger, short bow
  • riding sable (tethered to bison)
  • Pack with:

Phasia's Delecti gem monocle is not a god's blood crystal or matrix, can't see Graves invisible, distorts things like a magnifying glass when you set it down on something, but does not see at a distance. Paper with an unfamiliar script or cypher does not become comprehensible. This feels right but it does not translate. EvalTrea, Phasia looking at paper decides it is papyrus made in SW part of Esrolia. Used on Phasia's armor one can tell it is obvious that it is attuned to an Issaries priestess. We must not tell Greybeard that this exists.

We were in Nochett City for one week.

Water Death Storm 1604
Setting sail on the Sheshnelan cog. We are all told to be ready for a fight but otherwise to stay in our cabin. Tarkal and Graves take care of animals. Cog pukes a bunch, as does Raliegh.


Day Two ship on horizon around noon. Piece of hollow wood w mallet is banged on deck and a sailor yells "To Arms!" Raliegh will crank the Xbow. The other boat is prepared for missile fire. High shields fixed against our side to protect rowers. Front of bow has ram. Captain Noah ushers young man into a protected area and we prepare to fight the Esrolian pirates. Graves Prot4 Raleigh and himself preps to arc arrow fire from extremem range (then 8 rounds until ram). Phasia Farsees Graves who observes the opposition on their approach making sure to learn who gives orders. Captain and Phasia coordinate upcoming Lightwall. Graves sends Raleigh belowdecks. Captain Noah launches the maneuver and it almost works before they wheel and still get a ram, which breaks into Cog's area below deck. He casts his battle magic and prepares to defend inside the hatch.


Graves switches to xbow and targets pirate captain. Crit gets through to drop his leg, but others (MultMis3) do not. Gohan crits first pirate on board and pierces his left leg. Crazy popped out of the hold last round and is on the deck to engage and takes out his pirate's right leg. Peri almost fumbles. Captain Noah is not fighting but is in cover by virtue of the deck, which he is lighting on fire while 6 of us (Cog remains below) + 4 Shesh guards fight vs 33 of them, of which we have winged 2 and killed 2. Crazy fumbles and gets himself caught in the rigging. Phasia does 7 to her pirate's 6. Peri slashes hers 7 to his 5. Gohan misses and gets missed. Raleigh appears unbidden (showing initiative) to grab xbow and run back below. Graves goes invisible, has Millard bladesharp2 the broadsword, and heads for the Esrolian captain.

All the fire on our deck picks itself up and walks onto their ship. Gohan gashes another pirate's right leg, who then counter-attacks but is parried. Peri kills her guy in one. Phasia casts bludgeon1 but has her attack parried. Tarkal Glues his pirate's shoe to the deck. Graves finishes his transit to the other ship. Crazy got hit but didn't get damaged.

Gohan does 6 to abd. Phasia attempts to have Quark disrupt and fails. Graves has Millard cast befuddle on the Captain (Graves' invis not disrupted), backed by 8pow points and is successful. Graves holds while assessing situations/options: Spot Hidden reveals the mast and ship are covered w fire protective runes and the ship has only water/food for 1 week travel containers. Cog pops up from a hatch a hits one in the leg, having Craghopper disrupt another for a checkmark. Gohan kills his. Phasia takse out a guy with an abs smash, and Quark disrupts successfully. We have lost a couple of warriors on our side 6 of us +3 NPCs vs 19 bad guys. Peri ____.

Tarkal's spell spirit zaps one and then he fails to poke, avoiding damage. Graves gets behind the pirate captain and offers him his life in exchange for ending the battle. Captain Noah requires timber to repair and gets it before we let them go. Captain Noah commends us, invites us to dinner, and allows as how our Monsters may come as well. Cog declines. Decent Shesh wine and good dinner. Worshipping pagan gods offer useful tricks, apparently.

Three more days of traveling to Corflu. Graves messes with the captain when possible, offering excellent information on the local stories, etc Confound. Phasia gets into town and begins looking for barge up-river. They are expecting our competition but we got here sooner. Headman allows first come first served, we pre-pay 1000sp to secure the barge. We offload into the half-muck boards Premium Storage area. A few hours later an Esrolian ship pulls up. The trolls deck out and go stand guard. The guy from the other ship goes to talk to the Headman and then comes to Phasia with utmost politeness. She helps him to an understanding about "the second barge" that must surely be coming after the one we have already hired. Cog wonders aloud "When I Eat Little Man?!" at which point the interview ends abruptly.

 

Captain begins to take his leave (it will be at least three seasons before he makes it back to Sheshnella) and accepts a letter from Graves addressed to his father.

{{+Graves letter to his father|closed}}

The barge comes and we load.

There is an attack of the natives but we are on the barge with the multi missile battery, etc. and it is not Mr. Two Axe.

 

We make it to Pavis.

Thanks for the editing and updates, Joe!

  --[[Brandon WilliamsCraig]].....Mon Jan 02 22:38:06 -0800 2012

Standing on a dias, stairs down to 10' pool filled w skulls instead of water. Stairway going up to landing on the other side. Delecti voice "You can take anything you can carry. On each floor is a progressivley difficult trial." SpiritShield1. Walk through skulls up stairs tthrough door into room, filled w treasure of all kinds. Archway to side and stair to next level. Spot and Eval success (chk) to know 90-95% valuless. 1 weight unit of real treasure is the reward. Spot again, with attention on the room/structure/etc. This tower doesn't really exist: no privies, the stairs don't really make sense, dinginess is uniform in a way that real dirt isn't (narrative causality), treasure stacks look picturesque (after investigation of earler people, still looks perfect) and even fake shit takes forever to make.

Stairway: gentleman is walking down toward me in the other direction, asks to speak. Debate on whether it is good to or not to be alive during which Graves switches into acting mode and 01% ends up on the far side of him going up the stairs. Room: two people and a duck are chained to the wall. Keys hang nearby. They ask to be freed. Why? They are trapped and tell their sad tales: 1) Humakt came to kill zombies etc and was last one standing. Found tower. Overwhelmed by Delecti and revived. Bane to be here in this way. 2) Orlanthi adventurer who will fight for me for the rest of my life. 3) Duck, Millard, is the lightest and can be carried with the most additional treasure. What choice did the last person make? Nobody has ever been here before. Graves begins to leave and the duck kicks into super-bargain mode and promises to serve for life. Graves frees him.

Stairway has a guardian - size 12 Gorp. Graves has bag (belonged to Eurmal), seemed to contain gems, actually a mouth that looked ready to consume. Thrown at gorp consumes it - one use rune magic spell Swallow. Up stairs to room. Three bony hands holding 1) scroll 2) mace 3) bag. Grab scroll. Open. Language. Strategies how to converse so as to confound.
Stairway. Peeking up looks like skeletal thing from swamp on hill.

Leave, carrying duck out - becomes allied spirit POW17 Int 15 1pt Lie 2pts Shield. Scroll grants 25% confound. Gems and jewelry = 1000sp.

cards.name: SGo Training Journal 20120106
cards.content:
{{+date}}{{+Narrative}}

 

Discussion

Please single click "+Discussion" to add this field if it doesn't exist yet, or double click existing text below to edit and add your comments.

{{+Discussion}}

 

Tags

{{+Associations|closed}}


You may want to hover over the lower right side of this card and click "watch" to be notified of new content.

God Fertility Storm 1604

Arriving in Pavis. Where to sell the bronze? Later. The Pavis dock looks well maintained, like prior to year of troubles. Our obviously cargo boat is plauged with peoplewanting to be paid to help. Far side of wall of New Pavis -> hill used to have 4-5 dozen Orlanthi cottages and now has 2000 people in a ghetto. Phasia hires the number of people required ($ taken by Don out of final %). Unloading into Elejan's warehouse. Torath goes to check on house and let Artos know we are home. Tarkal will hang with unloading process (intends later to look for somebody to help bind spirit to bison when Cog goes to his tribe. Spirit options: Trolls? Praxian Barbs? Spirit Worshippers among Orlanthi? Rural agricultural folks?). Cog goes to help with unloading and hide from sun in warehouse. Peri takes Melé, looking wide eyed at City ("It's like a city but smaller, and boisterous!") and goes back to house w Torath to into Artos. Handwritten note on door on New Pavic (Sartarite+Pavic). Melé reads "Ran out of money. Staying with Istar the Maul. - Artos". House not locked, but anything Valuable is gone (has probably been sold). Maybe squatters but not trashed. Graves supervises unloading. Phasia heads for Elejan's with Griffin and Sparverius.

 

Pavis feels a bit different, things built up/changed. Arrives at Elejan's tent, where he is having a cup of tea w potential client. Phasia gets the nod and waits until the client leaves happy. Is polite until Phasia explodes with news. He listens, offers tea to slow her down, and asks questions for understanding but letting her go on most of the day. Complimented on Great Job and Excellent Friends for support. Word of this journey will change the perception of Phaisa (and of us) through the whole of Pavis. Gives him the tin of his favorite tea. Spot Hidden reveals that Elejan is in a lot of pain and not very well - aged a bunch in the last year or so, though eye still gleams. Phasia should not have been left in the position when his brother had to go his own way - apologies. Once the warehouse is completely squared away our obligation is complete. Talking specifically about artifacts and $. Phasia shows her Delecti Gemonocle and he judges it unique. Sends Graves his best and asks her to lets him know he is welcome at any time. Elejan has a chest brought full of cheap bags with 100 written on it = 183 weight units of silver (each 4 pounds) = 720# silver. The letter Phasia sent with a trade caravan (supporting letter of credit) arrived but he didn't get the letter she sent. She send Sparv w note to get Graves. Fifteen minutes later three runners arrive - the chief slave of Elejan and two others - and invite Graves to come to Elejan's. They will take over the unloading.

 

Torath and Peri go to Isthar the Maul. The outside is still attractive, combining various tribal markings (the Pan-Waha Look), welcoming to everyone. Two living rooms as before (wife formal Pavic + his fire in middle Waha style). Isthar welcomes them and they drink water together before sitting by the fire. He speaks of Artos coming to stay with him for a month and summons him. He is so happy we are back as it has been horrible (what transpired) and wonderful (to stay with Isthar). Peri wonders aloud about Gimpy's health and financial well-being. A new residential occupancy tax (seasonal to get a place in the water line) was avoided by his leaving. Peri has concerns that the house was left unlocked and that things are missing. He tried to visit regularly and didn't expect that problem in this neighborhood. Maybe the value of the good lost would have exceeded the taxes saved? :-) He requires silver to prepare the house? Torath hands him 12 pounds of silver (500sp) and he gets the point and is ashamed. He disappears to prepare the house. Fermented buffallo milk is had by all. They stay for the requisite 7-9 drinks while Torath tells our stories of derring do.

Raleigh disappeared for a while. On returning we have a conversation about NEVER going anywhere without coordinating. By 4pm when the messengers arrived to free Graves, Tarkal, and Cog. Graves has saved the party some money in potential losses. Graves feels bad about letting Elejan down, says so, and is forgiven eloquently. Cog is given his mug of Troll Yummy and begs a boon. Cog is to choose a merchant from his tribe to send to trade w Elejan. The representative will be treated like family and may come after dark.Cog goes to find a First Through The Breech Argan Argar, gives him his 3000sp, and sends him to buy the bronze from Elejan and deal for the mushrooms. Conversation ensues between them: trade on behalf of western trolls for goods (the western trolls get a great deal), then gets 12,000sp for the 3,000sp. Those we represented did VERY well.

Our house is now 3x relative occupancy with all the folks and animals coming and going. Around 6pm the food arranged for us arrives: pig on spit, barrels of beer, seems party related. Minstrels are coming. The courtyard (could be for training) is filled with people's mounts. Artos is everywhere serving everybody all the time. Wait. There are two of them. Literally. Peri asks if he went to Greybeard. Turns out he did and got cloned. At midnight the Artos in the kitchen ceases to exist and the plate he was carrying drops. Guests: Priest of Pavis heard we are back and new High Priest would like to give us a welcome and blessing. Runner from Gimpy's says come over when we have a second. Neighbors drop by occasionally, bringing welcome but not staying. Party until the wee hours. Torath sneaks of to Gimpy's to pay the 400sp we owe him. Gimpy asks how we have been doing. Torath asks him how he dealt with changing cultures. Gimpy's dad was a mason. There is a right tool for every different kind of rock. Promises of everyone dropping by later to swap stories. Local gossip: Kirby seems to be selling maps in place of Herbie. Kost the Tracker retired, some others tried to pick up his biz but failed and the biz went away.

Freeze Stasis Storm 1604
9am another slave shows up from Elejan with two more chests of equal value and a bag w 50 god's blood crystals. This is 10% of what will eventually be 15% (after liquidation). 2500-3000lbs crystal +matrixes = 65,000-70,000sp value & Gods' Blood 40-50,000sp value

Graves asks the urchins where Eria priestess of Voria is, finds her, and acquaints her with his plans to choose wards, make them apprentices, and teach them to be free. She expresses interest, reservations, and looks forward to seeing how things work out with Raleigh before blessing or objecting to the endeavor.

 

SIX WEEKS

Cog went to the First Through the Breech Clan, found the high priestess, presented her with his tale 03% and the skull (Mist Race Troll) and was granted an agreeable  mate (he must be able to do one pull up) and lead armor and weapons, tithing 90% of his cash. He is told about former great hero of this clan who had a great weapon Maul named Sunderer. He left to adventure, following a man named Arkat. If Cog finds Sunderer he may use it until he dies or whatever. Hobo the Trollkin is granted a bronze mace that once belonged to a Dark Troll. 

Torath works with Eria to further the goals of Green Daughter in the Pavis area, and will work to see the bison tribe. He willl fund her, but there is a competing Lunar God named Danfive Xaron (severe - orphan's and ex-convicts) whose priest the Lunars want her to wed - thereby pulling the minor goddess into the sway of the Lunar Empire.

 

Tarkal leaves his god with Greybeard for a while longer and trains. Unlike in the past, adventurers divisible into have and have nots, there is a thriving training business as people are coming out with 1000-2000sp each adventure. They are paying to move up and prepare and finding more reliable small stashes. Adventureres are almost all Sartarites tending to specialize more, learning one or two specific skills, getting mentors, acting like professionals. Not seeing a lot more runelords, however.

Cog tells Karg Sons as a group that the Lunars are providing spells and support for Trollkin rebellion. They don't get it. It doesn't fit into their world view. Deaf Ears.

Phasia bought Bludgeon 4, Xenohealing 2. Pays for Daka Fal instant spirit teaching of Quark to learn Spirit Shield 2 and Protection 4 and for
Takes nGryff to learn Mindspeech 1. Also Extension1 and D.I.1
Elejan sends mirror so gem can read itself: If you are better at eval the more facts you will find through gem. No item may be ever checked by gem more than once. If you miss the initial role bad things happen to the user - dibilitated in the skill for a while.

Plath, an Orlanthi ancestor worshipper, approaches Peri for help to become a Runelord. She investigates him, by asking his adventuring companions (found via Gimpy) and making her "strive to be a desirable ancestor someday" speech, and agrees, allowing him to cast magic to protect himself when he summons his spirit (he gets a malign 3d6) and beats it, with two potions and a matrix by his side. He thanks her and offers 100sp as a gift. She send him to donate it to Eria. Is there anything he can do for her? A bottle of brandy :-) before he leaves for more adventure the day after tomorrow. Next day he brings a bottle to her that we transported from Nochett City.

Prot4 matrix goes to Tarkal

Graves trains spells up
Bladesharp 2 > 4    3500
Countermagic 2 > 4    3500
Spirit Shield 1 > 2    1000
Shimmer 1 for Sparv    500
Countermagic 2 for Sparv    1500
Farsee for Sparv    500
Goes to shrine and spends to POW for Shield and Detach Limb

4th day notices 04% something wrong about my trainer. She's not quite acting right. Turns out to be Tesserson. I must be back in Pavis around the beginning of Storm Season next year to make The Big Sacrifice. Luckily I'm already illuminated, or I'd pretty much already be a dead man. I'm not the only one who is going to be sacrificed. Keep a clear distance from Lightbringers and be nice to Lunars. Our group is the only one that can really fight the bat. Remember the ultimate goal is to drink from the blood fountain, by being a favorite of the Royal Family, by doing something amazing for the Empire. Graves asks for something cool and he tries to lie that a coin is supermagical fortunate, thereby giving Graves a POW check. Gives Graves smelling salts to wake his teacher and disappears.

During Sacred Time Tesserson looks me up again with a plan. There are Esrolian initiates of some random goddesses are coming with horse products ;-). We Lie them into a ceremony, Oratory/Acting/Confound convincing them we are doing it for their goddess (but in fact serving Eurmal). We succeed and collect their initiate tithes = 450sp, leaving them with self-inflicted wounds in their arms which they must allow to heal naturally. Get Runemagic back in the process.
Torath tracks down and hunts and kills/Peaceful Cuts a desert lion, binding a 16pt spirit and sacrifices for rune magic through Green Goddess and hunter cult at the same time.
Cog's shaman binds a troll spirit for/to him. Remember to make sure it doesn't die permanently.
Peri takes part in Daka Fal ceremony, telling story of her hero quest, gives people ability to get Free Ghost runemagic. Melé dragged along. Worships a Nochett City lesser goddess and becomes a lay member of Daka Fal.
Elejan attends but is not running ceremony this year. another Master Merchant does and Phasia is given seat of honor in the hall. Turns out the net worth of our trip was near 500,000sp. At the end of Scred Time Elejan is going to be closing down his tent. Many of the priests have bought large lots of his goods. Ceremony role fails but a pathfinder is available in this larger congregation to offer Pathwatch. Phasia takes it.

Water Disorder Sea 1605 (Week 5)
We explore the possibility of inviting Greybeard west to where the Jresteli Egg was found in Nochett City.

We hear Plath died two days into rubble. They got a map and got treasure but were ambushed on the way back by tusk riders. Running fight, escaped w treasure. A few days after the word arrives, a crying woman shows up on our doorstep. She declares herself the mother of Plath. He can't be summoned. What did he do wrong? Peri divines and fails. Goes, prays, and tries again to contact his allied spirit - succeeds: "Somebody (swirling mass of souls that looked like a man) came and saved him, taking his soul away from me suddenly."
We investigate if the map guy, Kirby, and the guy putting maps together are associates of WTD. That way they send a new Runelord in to get munched frequently. Also could be funded by Lunar Empire to reduce Runelords who might resist their influence.

Two more weeks of training after Sacred Time: Graves trains Repair (in Millard)    1000sp and teaches Raleigh Acting. Torath continues investigations. Discovers that he may be the only person still alive who really knows the Rubble, from Kost's point of view. After he was crippled by the Illuminated Lunar his entire group was murdered. The maps aren't really accurate and people are reporting information back that isn't correct.

We all go to the Temple of Pavis. Graves has a tension reaction when he passes into the Harmony of the temple. As Citizens we are invited to sit in the VIP portion during the ceremony. The High Priest takes time to shake all of our hands. He is Caden, one of the two liberals we helped and by whom we were helped. He took Polis Protector's position and is now know as Polis Agrandis, intending to grow the city. They built 40 of the planned 200 buildings within the walls for Orlanthi in what used to be the Zebra Pens. It is considered pretty good housing. Peri asks and finds that it costs 3000sp of labor to build a house in the Rubble. Taxes have been an issue preventing the rest from being built yet. Taken on more food from Yelmalians with extra taxes.

 

Would we like to store any money with temple to pay for home/parcel tax 200sp/season 1000sp/yr for water and grain. Citizenship/lease pre-paid for 99yrs. We pay 1000sp for the year 1605. We are offered Council positions, especially to replace mentors who are retiring ;-) We are seen as the people who saved the city from The Year of Troubles.

 

Raleigh is within sight 85% of the time and otherwise wanders no more than up to a few minutes away.

Peri goes to visit Kirby the Mapguy and threatens him, almost accusing him of being in league with WTD. Torath agrees to 100sp down and 15% (or 300sp) and buys the map Plath's group used (since it is a new season). The original costs 1000sp. Torath and Graves examine the velum and Graves gueses it may have been aged with lemone juice and a candle.

Week 5.75

Another 27,000sp delivered to our house. Graves buys Fire Arrow matrix for his 4,500sp.

 

Master Merchant Tejan just bulk purchased 1/8 of Elejan's empire, but doesn't have his flair/tea. Phasia buys Elejan's Mass Detection matrixes pinky ring for 15,500sp.

Phasia and Peri go to Elejan's house. It is designed to redirect sunlight for light but is remarkably cool, with two fountains providing cool water. A slave greets/welcomes them. They wait for tea while Elejan prepares. Tejan communicated with him that he had underpromised and that business is VERY good. Phasia expresses regret at Elejan's retirement, etc. He is philosophical and inquires after them. Elejan apologizes for being naughty and sending all payment in silver to make sure its true weight is appreciated. Thanks for all that he has done for us and for Phasia. Elejan insists he is happy. Phasia allows as how his brother is a butthead and that we'd be happy to find a resolution to his "illness". He is comfortable not going after the cure. Elejan recommends we close the Rubble as a chapter in our lives. The Rubble is one of the reasons he chose to retire - came across an interesting fact that disturbs him. Came across the same coin seven times in a season and decided he was not doing a service by supporting adventurers. Over the course of the conversation honeyed nut treats are brought out with fruit and thinly sliced ham.

Graves goes to talk to Greybeard

{{+Greybeard notes|closed}}

Options:
Could follow map/path trod by Plath to seek WTD
Doraster
Troll artifact - "Sunderer"
Jresteli Egg quest

 

 

NOTES:

 

Of the take from Elejan we each take:

  • 10,000sp and 5,000sp goes to our shared pool.
  • 100 units of god's blood crystals (maybe each gets a 13, 6 one's, and a 2)(Every size crystal denomination we want up to 20 - a whole ton of 2s and 3s - none are attueneable i.e. all saleable).
  • The final 27,000 gets split similarly 4,500 each

Discuss:

Illumination

You have a crossbow and one bolt and must kill two enemies at once. What do you do?

The Jresteli Egg and WTD.

Kill WTD and then gather Greybeard's friends as we go through Nochett City.

To: Otto Alexander GIZ <alexander.otto@giz.de>
Cc: Bill Leicht <whiteleicht@earthlink.net>, ae-board@googlegroups.com


Dear Alex,

First let me respond separately re the Warriors for Peace Academy. It is a terrific idea. The Peace Dojos International team should be informed and other like-minded folks. I'll cc Bill Leicht and the AE Board.

Best,
Don

On Jan 1, 2012, at Sun1,3:34 PM, Otto Alexander GIZ wrote:

Dear Don,
//

 

The Aiki work on peace, conflict and development in the Philippines – your question comes at an interesting time since we work on a concept for establishing the Warriors for Peace Academy. We – that is Patrick Koop and myself. (Patrick works currently in Afghanistan but will return to the Phils probably in 2012.)
The WfP Academy will be a training place for Aikido and other educational and training programmes on conflict work and community development. The primary target groups are members from conflict-affected communities in Negros and Mindanao.
The Academy will include enough land for agriculture: self-supply by the Academy trainees; income creation through organic farming and capacity building for organic farming; and last but not least, agriculture as integrative part of a Warrior’s / Aikidoka’s way.
The WfP Academy shall be the successor to the first “Warriors for Peace Academy”, which was a two-year apprenticeship implemented in 2007/2008 in Bacolod City, with very similar objectives and programmes. In that time, we used the facilities of a local peace center, and the trainees from communities in Negros and Mindanao had to be accommodated in the neighbourhood. Now, the Academy shall become a permanent educational and training institution and also a venue for different stakeholders – a place with own land, buildings, legal status, etc. 
The NGO Warriors for Peace, president of which is Sensei Noel Fuentes, will be one of the main partners to the Academy, together with the Peace Agents Foundation (founded by Patrick) and other organizations who have been working together and with PAF for a longer time.
The first step probably has to be the purchase of some land (in Negros Island). Then, we can apply for funds to build the Academy.

 

So, that is was is keeping us busy apart from Ethiopia.

 

Best wishes,

 

Alex

cards.name: Thanatar notes from Ingest Scroll
cards.content:
from: https://sites.google.com/site/ingestscroll/cultsindex/thanatar

 

Thanatar

The Severed God

History

Before Time

Than was of old the son of the Devil; entering the world with his Father at the time of the Rent. He commanded his Father's most powerful legions. Than conquered half the World in the name of Chaos before Rhadamanthus routed him at the Battle of Truth. In vengeance, Than captured Rhadamanthus' sister Orenoar, Goddess of the Dawn, Mistress of Light and Knowledge; and carried her to a dark and secret place and there devised a foul magic whereby he removed her head with a fine wire and incarcerated her soul within it. Than then moved through the Darkness taking her magic and knowledge to supplement his own; with this knowledge he formulated another hideous spell whereby he could seize magic and knowledge from out of a living person's mind leaving him bereft of all knowledge and mindless. Thus were there several Gods lost.

The Lawgods could not tolerate such an atrocity and while the Lightbringers pursued the Devil, Than was himself pursued as he searched for his Father by Viking a son of Typhon the Stormlord. Viking slew himself to follow Than into Hell and thereby became a God of Death. Than fled, Viking followed on his heels until finally the Head Hunter was cornered by the Storm God's son in the shadows against the fiery rays of Helios at the centre of Hell. Viking's Axe sent Than's head flying into the Sun's Light where it was blasted and seared; Than's body fell and Viking departed believing him no more. When the Lightbringers came to release the Sun, Rhadamanthus found the Head of Than, along with the once beautiful head of his sister. Filled with a bitter thirst for Justice, he tried to destroy the Skull of Than and in so doing, discovered how to protect himself from the Severed God's Mind-Stealing power; but, unable to destroy the skull itself, he threw it into the Ocean. Unwilling to have such a trophy pollute the depths, Poseidon caused it to be washed-up upon the shores of an Island.

After Viking left, yet before the Lightbringers came to Helios in Hell; Than's headless body arose and went in search of its head. It searched all Hell, but it couldn't come near the Sun's rays and so it could not find it. Not finding his own, Than went in search of others; To this day, the body of Than stalks the Underworld taking heads and for a time wearing them upon its own shoulders until they decompose and are discarded. Somewhere, in a Secret Place in Darkness there is that place where Than first wrought his spells of Head-Theft; there lies the body of Orenoar, Goddess of the Dawn bereft of knowledge; many have sought for it, none have found it!

Since Time

After the rise of Time, the Skull of Than came to be worshipped by the people of the Island as a Death God. There it was discovered by a self-serving Priest of Poseidon named Markhor Nightstar and he it was who brought it back to the mainland. Possibly possessed by it, Markhor Nightstar used the skills of Demosthenes to research its origins and powers; subsequently he formed the cult of Atyar, Hornéd Devourer of Knowledge.

Meanwhile the cult of Than continued to follow their God as they had in Godtime, but with the Severing of Than, their powers where drastically curtailed. The Cult of Atyar grew until Rhadamanthus heard of it and recognising the cult as a remnant of Than, immediately launched a crusade to destroy the abomination. Atyar could not face the Righteous Wrath of Light and Truth and the cult fled and their city was destroyed; yet the cult itself survived for it merely dispersed and reformed in secret skulls across the World. It was then that the two cults of Than and Atyar were reunited, for they recognised that they worshipped two aspects of the same God. True unity was impossible for the Body and Skull of Than were sundered, but the cults benefitted each other immensely.

The Skull is said still to exist still, perhaps buried deep in a vault beneath some city, possibly secreted in a mountain cave, or even returned to its island of worship. Many Thanatari heroes have gone in search of the Skull, thinking to bear it with them into Hell thereby reuniting the parts of their God into One; so far all have failed!

Life After Death

Followers of Thanatar do not fear Death for they know they will be personally escorted to Hell upon their demise and serve their God as spirits, returning when summoned to serve their cult and answer questions. Both the Spirit which Summons them to Hell and the spirits of deceased cultists are demonstrable realities to all living cultists. Meanwhile, the bodies of dead cultists, (and any others who die within the Temple precincts) are, whenever possible, turned into undead that they may aid the cult even in death. Cultists are not granted a divint after death .

Runic Associations

Than originally was a God of Death, Darkness and Chaos. From Orenoar he stole Truth. Upon severance, Than lost Truth, whilst the skull had its powers over Darkness blasted away by the Fire of Helios. The reunion of the two cults created a lesser deity of Darkness, Death, Truth and Chaos.

Nature of Cult

Thanatar personifies the insatiable thirst for knowledge and power at the expense of others. As long as people exist who desire to subjugate others with fear and desire knowledge of things arcane and hidden, then the Cult will thrive in secret.

Socio-Political Position and Power

Wherever Skulls exist, the cult will be found trying to wield power and influence covertly. However, the cult dislikes force and pure terror, (methods preferred by the cult of Ma Fear). Thanatar uses more indirect, manipulative means. Many cities are secretly under their sway and yet the elders of such cities know them not, for the cult is subtle and secretive. Occasionally the cult becomes more prominent in areas dominated by Chaos where it may become the premier Knowledge cult ahead of even Demosthenes. Wherever there is knowledge to be gained, there will be found Thanatar's Cells and Skulls.

Particular Likes and Dislikes

No cult likes Thanatar for all fear they may wind-up dangling from a head-hunter's belt save perhaps for the Vampires. The cult itself pursues any knowledge, spurning none. It has been noticed that the cult is strongest in those places where the Moon cults are strong, but the Sun cults are not; the greatest Skull is said to be in Moonguard, yet Selene hates and fears the cult as much as any other. The events of Godtime cause the cult to pursue vengeance most upon Rhadamanthus, Humakt and Viking. All Life Rune cults are despised as weak. Opposition to Thanatar is spearheaded by Rhadamanthus and Humakt, and if a Skull is ever assaulted it is always by these two in unison and strength, the cult genuinely fears these two and will always try to undermine the powers of Light and Truth by subversive means. Though it hates all other Chaos Rieving cults, it only fears these two. Cultists dislike all symbols relating to Sunfire, especially Gold. The cult metal is Tarnished Silver, this and the cult's Darklight appears to point to a relationship with warped moonlight yet again.

Organisation

Temples are called Skulls; sub-templar groupings are called Cells, these are most frequently 4-6 man intelligence gathering units working for Skulls elsewhere.

There is little contact between Temples. Inter-Skull relations will usually involve competition for intelligence resources. In theory, Skull status depends upon the seniority of the Skull, in practise it is usually dependant upon power. Frequently Skulls practise one aspect of the Cult to the exclusion of the others.

Skull Infrastructure and Hierarchy

A full Skull has a complex structure headed by the High Priest of Dark Truths, immediately beneath him is the most senior Runelord, (who may also be a Runepriest), called the Doom Lord who directly commands the other Runelords, who may not be Priests, and are titled Doom Masters. Also beneath the High priest are the three subcult priests who are called the Head of Than , Breath of Thanatar and Horn of Atyar respectively. These priests, as well as heading the subcult, also form the heads of factions vying for dominance within the temple. Politics and Internecine warfare are important means of promotion. Except in extremely large Skulls, there will be no other full Priests. Beneath the Full Priests in precedence are the Doom Masters who are also Doomed Priests, dedicated to one aspect of the cult. The Initiates are divided into two classes, the Doom Seekers who may or may not be committed to a specific cult aspect, and the Doomed who are always committed to an aspect; the Doomed are divided into Doomed Warriors aiming at Runelordhood and Doomed Priests who have many of the benefits of a Runepriest including enhanced POW gain and reusable Runemagic. Beneath the uncommitted Initiates are the laity, referred to in cult parlance as the expendables .

Despite this complex and intricate structure, discipline is based upon fear and force. Advancement by assassination is common and should the High Priest die for whatever reason, often the ranking Full Priests will fight it out with their affinities for control of the Skull. However, a farsighted and powerful High Priest will often have groomed an underling for the post and have bought the loyalty of the Doom Masters to ensure an easy ordination. Alternatively a neighbouring Skull may make a power bid by forcing in one of its priests and transplanting enough Doom Masters and Doomed to ensure his survival. The Moonguard Skull does this often, reputedly with success. It has been known however, for the entire hierarchy of a Skull to extinguish itself in a succession war.

Centres of Power and Holy Places

Darkness and Death are everywhere, Truth is what you make it, therefore the cult has no obvious centre of power, though it is noticeably stronger in Lunar dominated areas and weakest in places where Rhadamanthus and Humakt are strong.

Individuals find comfort in being underground in the cult light, but Skulls may be found in cities or forests or caves.

Holy Places include the Island of Atyar, the place where the skull is, and the Tomb of Orenoar wherever these places might be.

Holy Days and High Holy Days

The cult seasonal Holy Day is Wildday of Death Week. Each subcult celebrates a High Holy Day in Dark Season. Than upon Freezeday of Death Week; Thanatar on Godsday, Disorder Week; and Atyar upon Wildday of Truth Week. The cult as a whole celebrates two other festivals; that of the Reunion on All Deities Day; and that of severance on Windsday, Death Week, Storm Season when all cultist abstain from cult activity and fast. Each festival has a particular arcane ceremony.

Lay Membership

The cult attracts all who seek power and knowledge. Such applicants must be willing, even eager, to decapitate others to steal their knowledge. Thus psychopaths form its laity in bulk. All races are accepted save Dragonewts. In certain areas, Thanatar forms a Shadow Government and is relatively easy to find, but normally only a person of abnormal perception and tenacity would attempt to even find a Skull and his reason would be psychotic.

Of necessity, all prospective laity must be tested extensively, this is abstracted as (INT+CHA)×5⁄2% plus 5% for any gift of value or service to the cult. Non-chaotics test at CHA−5 unless of an obvious chaos race. Failures are considered spies and are dealt with accordingly.

It is common for a prospective Layman to remain in this state for a considerable time, performing services for the cult without worshipping at, or even knowing of, the location of the Temple, but functioning in a cell composed of others like himself lead by a Doom Seeker. Such a one will gain no training, but will be told his services will be taken into account when he is adjudged worthy of membership.

Benefits and Requirements - The Talisman

Lay Members are taught the lesser Passwords and the Main Entrance to the Skull. They must attend all ceremonies and account for themselves on a weekly basis unless given specific leave by a Doomed Priest or higher. They are referred to as the Expendables by superior cultists. They are used as lures, shock troops, decoys, sacrificial lambs, unskilled labourers, etc. They will be admonished to shun all contact with Rhadamanthus, Humakt and Typhon and if observed with such will suffer summarily and gruesomely. Laity do not gain free room and board unless they serve as personal lackeys to a Doomed one, they may not volunteer for such service, but are picked.

Training

Half Price: Shortsword Attack and Parry, Mace Attack and Parry, Small and Medium Shield, Garrotte Attack, Move Quietly, Hide in Cover and R/W Local.
Full Cost: All languages and most other skills may be bought at full cost.
Double Cost: Cultists may learn to Speak Atyari.
Forbidden: Laity are forbidden to use any Axe.

Spells

Half Price: Disruption, Extinguish and Darkwall
Double Cost: Healing, Ignite and Repair

All Fire/Light spells save Ignite are forbidden and if it becomes apparent that a Laymen knows them then he had better account for this or his demise is imminent. All other spells are at normal cost including Cheeseslice.

Initiate Membership - The Doom Seekers

To qualify as an initiate an applicant needs to have attained 60% in a cult non-weapon skill. He must also demonstrate his ability with a garrotte by bringing the head of a victim killed purely by garrotting. The head must be fresh enough to verify the event by examination by a master of Garrotte.

During the Initiation ceremony on a seasonal Holy Day, the Initiate must produce his trophy and face the Cult Spirit Vox Sancti (Voice of God). This will test him subtly (Speak Atyari + Best Knowledge Skill + INT×5%) ⁄ 2. In return, the applicant may ask one question of the Spirit which will be answered truthfully, but cryptically. Usually the Initiate will have been instructed which question to ask by the cult. But he will be able to ask his own on a POW×1%. If he succeeds in the Test of Initiation critically or specially, then he may ask three or two questions respectively, the extra questions are always his own. If he fails the test then the Voice of God will Summon The Psychopompos, or Gatherer of Souls, to take him. If he should successfully fight-off the Psychopompos then he may reapply for initiation next season.

Upon Initiation, the cultist becomes a Doom Seeker and must take one gift and concomitant geas(es). He must sacrifice 2 points of POW on each seasonal Holy Day and once per year must provide a living captive for the cult. If he commits to an aspect of the cult, then he may have free access to the subcult library and find it easier to gain training.


Gifts of Thanatar
2D6 Gift Geases
2 Mastery of any Knowledge Skill 3
3 Raise non-raisable Characteristic 1 pt/3 geases 3
4 +2pt of Cult variable, +1pt of Non-Cult variable or 1 other Cult Spell 2
5 +15% on Stealth Bonus 2
6 +10% on Cult Weapon Attack and Parry 1
7 +10% on Knowledge Skill 1
8 +10% on Garrotte, Stealth or Perception Skill 1
9 +15% on Knowledge Bonus 2
10 Raise Raisable Characteristic 1pt/geas 1
11 Mastery of Cult Weapon or Garrotte 3
12 Mastery of any Stealth or Perception Skill 3

Training

Free: Speak Atyari, Garrotte Attack, Hide in Shadows and Move Quietly.
Half Price: R/W Local, Speak any Language, All Alchemy Skills, All Knowledge Skills, Evaluate Treasure, Spot Hidden, Listen, Acting, Disguise, Shortsword Attack and Parry, Mace Attack and Parry, Small and Medium Shield
Full Price: R/W any Alphabet, Oratory and Most Other Skills.

Spells

Half Price: Bladesharp, Bludgeon, Cheeseslice, Darkwall, Extinguish, Befuddle, Demoralise and All Detects
Double Cost: Healing, Ignite and Repair
Forbidden: Firearrow, Fireblade, Light and Lightwall (These spells will be forgotten if known.)

Harmonise isn't forbidden, but it will only work on a creature of the same shape as the caster, but lacking a head!

For both the Laity and the Seekers, payment is usually in the form of service and kind. Those paying in cash will be told to account for their wealth. Initiates must tithe 10% of all income to their Skull. They do not get training or teaching for these monies.

Doom Seekers do not gain access to Runemagic, but do gain free room and board should they need it, not necessarily in the Temple. They are taught the Major Passwords and at least one side entrance to the Skull. All Seekers are given a wire garrotte which they must bear at all times. For Thanatar, POW counts towards Stealth at Initiate level.

The Doomed

The Doomed are high ranking cultists which form the most effective element of the cult. Doomed Warriors are essentially senior initiates who may aim at Priesthood or Doom Master Status. Doomed Priests have the powers and abilities essentially of full priests. Most Thanatari Runelevels are too concerned with cult affairs within the Skull to concern themselves outside. It is the doomed who are used as the executive arm, therefore they tend to be ritually free of templar responsibility to the priests. They must worship an aspect specifically, but owe no allegiance to their Runepriests.

This makes the Doomed dangerous wild cards in the Temple structure and they are generally kept involved in extra-Skull missions to keep them out of trouble. The Doomed Priests of course cannot gain advancement unless a vacancy occurs above them. Both Doomed Warrior and Doomed Priest demand the enactment of a minor Hero-Quest.

Doomed Warrior

Doomed Warriors require 75% in five skills suitable for Runelord qualification and a POW of 15. There is no test, but must take another gift and geas(es). He is entitled to a Lay personal servant, he is responsible for his conduct, but not his safety. He also gains a guardian familiar (q.v.). He gains no special Divine Intervention nor Runemetal. They usually aim for Doom Master or Doomed Priest, if they become Doomed Priests then Thanatar maintains his DEX skills as for Runelord/Priests. They may sacrifice for all cult Runespells of their aspect non-reusably. His power is maintained as if he were a Runelord.

Doomed Priest

Doomed Priests require 18+ POW, 90% Speak Atyari and 75% Read/Write. They must pass a test, unless Doom Master, of Garotte Attack+INT+DEX. Failure is not dangerous, but demands a year-long wait to reapply. Fumbles are lethal!

Doomed Priests make their POW raises from 22, they may sacrifice for all 1 and 2 point Runespells reusably plus all reusable 3 point spells on a non-reusable basis. They must take another gift and geas(es) and gain a guardian familiar. They are also entitled to a Lay or Seeker personal servant on the same basis as Doomed Warriors.

DEX skills are limited to DEX×5%, but may be trained to this level, DEX may not be trained however.

Runelord Membership - The Doom Masters

Known as Doom Masters, Runelords of Thanatar are the skilled fighters of the cult and responsible for the defence of the Skull. Unless also Doomed Priests, they do not have to be committed to a particular aspect of the cult. They may sacrifice for all Runemagic non-reusably.

Requirements for Runelord are 15+ POW, Shortsword or Mace Attack, a compatible Parry, Garrotte Attack, Speak Atyari, Move Quietly, Hide in Shadows and one of R/W, Acting, Evaluate Treasure, Brew Poison or Spot Hidden at 90% and must know Befuddle, Darkwall and Cheeseslice IV and have the INT to maintain them. He must also have spent at least one full year as a Doomed Warrior.

Doom Masters have all the normal restrictions of Runelords, plus they vow never to attack a full priest physically until they also become full priests. If he breaks the vow, the Spiritus Punitis will attack him immediately.

He must take another gift and geas(es), plus all the normal benefits of his status. He receives 2-4 items of Tarnished Silver including a Shortsword and Garrotte. If he acquires it, he may also attune iron, but will be given none.

The Senior Runelord is titled Doom Lord and has access to Invocate Spiritus Punitis as a 3 point non-reusable spell. He is given a full suit of Tarnished Silver armour and a complete set of weapons.

Runelords are entitled to an initiate level servant.

Runepriesthood

In most temples, there is one priest per aspect of cult represented, as mentioned above, these are titled the Hand of Than , Breath of Thanatar and Horn of Atyar . To qualify, a candidate must have 18+ POW, have 90% in Speak Atyari and Read/Write and have been a Doomed Priest for at least 3 years unless there aren't enough Doomed Priests with the requisite qualifications. A new priest is ordained when starting a new Skull.

The priests have access to all Runespells of their aspect, but do not gain any Standard Runespells, but must steal them from non-Thanatari.

The priests rarely leave the confines of the Temple, each is entitled to a Doomed Warrior Servant. He must take another gift and Geas(es). They are subject to all the normal restrictions of their status. Priests must sacrifice 5 points of POW on a Holy Day and 1 point per day, unless on an extra temple mission.

The High Priest of Dark Truths, as well as his cult aspect Runespells, also gain Invocate Spiritus Punitis and Incarceratum Spiritus Mortis as 3 point reusable.

Runespell Compatibility

The cult gains no Standard Runespells save Divine Intervention, and must rely on that which they can steal from others. No stolen spells that are Fire/Light based or anti-chaos may be used. The priesthood gain access to the following cult Special Runespells.

Associate Cults

True associates are non-existent, save for Primal Chaos, which of course offers Chaos Feature as a 3 point non-reusable (q.v.). However Ishtar was associated early in Godtime before realising Than's nature and thus Thanatari gain access to Power Store as a means of storing POW for latter use with spells, (e.g. Consume Mind or Imperatore Spiritis).

Both Selene and Thanatar deny any formal association and no skills, spells or abilities are exchanged, but the two cults are often found together and sages believe there is a strong similarity between Thanatari Darklight and Selene Moonlight.

Orenoar should be a subservient cult, for Than took her head and knowledge, powers over light and Truth to forge the Darklight spell. However, the teachings of Atyar state that Orenoar volunteered for this abomination and thus revere the Goddess of the Dawn as an Associate. Obviously the Lightbringers view this doctrine as another disgusting Thanatari perversion, but far from their most evil or distasteful.

Temples

Skulls may be centred around converted buildings or deep in chaotic forests or mountain caves. They usually feature subterranean complexes with several entrances, very few of which are known to all cultists. In particular, the High Priest and Doom Lord will have their own exits, which they will use only in an emergency. The Temple will include a pillared Hall of Worship which is usually Tripartite in nature except for those Skulls worshipping a single aspect. The Hall includes the sacred Dark Flame. Each Temple will have one or more libraries, well catalogued and indexed, but accessible only to initiates committed to the subcult aspect. There are holding pens , usually hewn out of rock, in which are kept the sanctified victims and subjects for experimentation etc. These are usually well treated for they will provide heads and undead for the cult. There are waiting areas for undead, laboratories, training rooms and quarters for the privileged. The architecture gives away the cult's chaotic origin, for there are side chambers, blind endings, pillars etc. with no regard for overall design. Often a new pillar or wall is built merely to provide a home for a newly decayed skull, these are usually locked deep in masonry or else left in casual piles. Living heads are not uncommonly found on ledges at waist height. These are usually of unfortunate non-Thanatari who have been ceremonially executed , but are not deemed worthy of being carried as stores of magic or knowledge, a few cultists are also treated in this way; these heads are kept alive as punishment and their only function is to be decorative and serve as objects of casual sexual abuse by passing cultists.

Guardians

These are the spirits of departed cultists bound into other's bodies. They come into two types,

  1. Those bound into living bodies intended to serve in the world outside the Temple and can easily pass muster as ordinary citizens though usually very taciturn and somewhat glassy eyed. They have usually been dead a long time, are not easy to understand and frequently appear unable to relate to the modern world, and
  2. Those bound into undead bodies to take advantage of the undead's superior combat capabilities. These are intended only for use within the temple confines, except in very special circumstances.

Talismans and Blemishes

Lay Members are given special Talismans by which the Cult Spirits, Guardians and Insane Ghosts may recognise them. A Talisman is made from human finger bone, human hair, a shard of Tarnished Silver in the form of a hornéd Skull and is completed by the user sacrificing a point of permanent POW into it and smearing it with his blood. It must be worn next to the skin. Such a charm may be used by a non-cultists and is vital to any non-cultist wishing to spend more than a few minutes within a Skull.

Upon Initiating, cultists gain a hidden blemish in the shape of a hornéd skull which is always the mark of a Thanatari. The initiate will be aware of the location of his blemish for the Vox Sancti will appear to bite him upon the location and it will feel quite painful for some days.
