cards.content:
From Brandon WilliamsCraig: Scholars of mythology, religion, and psychology, please consider joining Huston Smith and a host of renowned theological scholars, and myself, in considering the relationship between myth and theology. 

 

Come (with or without a paper) to the next meeting of the [[http://www.pcts.org|Pacific Coast Theological Society]] on April 13th and 14th of this year at the Graduate Theological Union in Berkeley, California. Contact me to RSVP or for more information, if desired.

 

Call for Papers: Professor Smith requested this session to examine the relationship between myth and theology. I hope to choose a Saturday paper/presenter by February 13th, so everyone involved may have a chance to read and digest the material that will be presented. Junior scholars and those from underrepresented groups are particularly encouraged to make proposals. Sorry for the short notice.

 

Please email brandon at culturesmith dot com and attach your proposal, which should include a CV and abstract of no more than 500 words, addressing the relationship between myth and theology. Various examples of previous papers on other topics may be found here: http://www.pcts.org/journal/papers.html


Looking Forward,

 

Brandon WilliamsCraig Ph.D.

cards.name: Theopoetics and Mythopsychology
cards.content:
Find a place for


"Religion" includes the entire range of potential human responses that rise when making a way through the place where transcendent mystery and daily experience intersect. It is "an unstoppable force in human nature" (Smith The Way Things Are p151) because it wraps in one psychological package of cultural creativity a wide variety of related expressions that have always been a part of what it is to be human. Freud accurately pointed out the presence of delusions in religious thinking created "to comfort ourselves in an uncertain world" (The Huston Smith Reader p237). Also, he gave insufficient weight to the part of consciousness itself that is imaginal in nature, rather than being simply and self-deceptively delusional. Karl Marx correctly identified the mind-altering qualities of religion and its effect on large groups, but largely missed the ways that his own world-view was religious in character, as well as the ways that mythological tropes consciously held and participated in can bring out both the best and the worst in the human character. Religions invoke a range of related expressions, archetypal in nature, which allow the human being to get metaphorical hands on the disturbing parts of lived experience which do not lend themselves to straightforward handling. With poetic hands we ritually weave bigger-than-me experiences into a kind of understanding that deepens into nuance more than it provides measurable utility, potentially making us more human in relation to each other by bringing us in contact with limitation, power, finitude, imagination, and all the never fully known forces which scuplt the hidden contours of life. Mythology and Theology are two related ways of configuring the religious responses that are natural to human beings.

Find a place for

 

It may be helpful to introduce a few discipline specific distinctions.

Mythology has come to refer not only to texts touching on divinity, but also to any belief system imagined epistemologically. Imagined thoroughly, myth is a way of configuring and understanding human experience that consciously includes facts and fictions as revealed through complexes of images, rather than being a world view held simply as either fact or fiction. A term familiar from literary study, mythopoiesis, then has to do with the creation of narrative in which mythological aspects are either overtly presented or may be discerned. Mythography has to do with writing about the workings of mythologies, especially those dynamics which may be understood psychologically.

Psychology often refers to an "inner life" attributed to individuals, which shapes their choices in ways that requires "outside" influence and behavioral repetition to control, thereby shifting the movement of groups of people.

 

The nuances proposed by an archetypal approach to psychology have to do with application of the mythological imagination to psychological ideas. For instance,

"an archetypal approach" is acknowledged as a mythology and 
image ines mythology

 

Find a place for

 

From an archetypal point of view, for instance, Augustin's thought is an installment in the ongoing narrative of Belief as much as a movement in the mythopsychology and identity of Christianity. Belief is an archetypal image, a metaphorical tome in which monotheism is a chapter and Christianity a piece of Big News that gives the story a new heroic turn.

By "psychological polytheism" I mean perception of the full range of meanings within an archetypal context. In the relationship between the god/power called Belief and the avatar Christianity, each reshapes the other by being in relationship.
I wonder; might it be fruitful to draw attention to the relationship breaking, a sin, of institutionalization and show that the distance between Belief and Christianity, for instance, is what depotentiates the mysteries that Christian Theologians study?

Just as theology tends to become thinking about "God", hermeneutics tends toward being the process of thinking about interpretation, which can leave the process of engaging in interpretation out of the picture, thereby requiring mythology to recover. This is not a sally in the territorial conflicts of academic politics, rather it is an observation of the function of ______

Mythopsychology's archetypal approach perceives autonomous Belief imagining itself into shapes, without literally conceiving its images as things, and discovers in this imaginal autonomy myriad shapes of an archetypal image--the "body" of Belief, for instance, as "embodied" in the daily life of the world sensed, felt, thought about, lived.

Finally, mythologists must make clear why mythology is necessary. Perhaps most importantly, mythology comes at the discussion from the side, from the perspective of fiction, untrustworthily, dragging behind it the lamentably simplistic "oh, that's just a myth", rather than establishing first a buttoned-down, infinitely respectable, culturally demanded gravity of purpose. For instance, in the November 21st, 2011, New Yorker where Martin Amis waxes poetical about Don DeLillo's "prophetic soul" he is describing a mythographer at his craft. Please excuse the length of the quote, but its entirety is required to see how Amis closes with what may be taken as a glance over several of the core functions of mythopsychology.

{{Martin Amis on Don DeLillo New Yorker 20111121+Source Content}}

 

It takes a bit of patience to see where theology becomes obviously a part of the mythological (fictional interpretive) exercise above. This is even more so because the vison-granting "gods" overtly named, though with tongue firmly placed in cheek, might distract from that Power with Many Names mentioned above which is truly worshipped with sacrifices and fervor--World Trade, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, Crude Oil, Bonds, Banks, that is to say The Market.

 

 

The dilemma is not that theology cannot do the mythographic research necessary to become intimate with the types of "gods" to which Amis refers. The challenge comes in going against one's own corporate culture to do so, as well as the disrutping the system which has always provided established thinkers their sliced bread and butter-flavored spread. At this time in its development as a field, Mythology has the leisure of being expected to be counter-cultural, but it will continue to serve this function because of its nature not because of its novelty. In the end, "mythology" can err on the side of being too "New-agey" (at about the point where cultural comparativism becomes indiscriminate); but theology might could do with the exhilaration of shedding its tendency to be morbidly tentative and err on the side of poetic delight, thereby revitaliziing its instruction. The dialogue between Mythology and Psychology creates the "third field" of religious and literary study which comes athwart the common practice of many established disciplines, including the industries of written theology and clinical psychology, and extends visionary antennae by way of the imagination.

cards.name: shime
cards.content:
Sacred places are typically marked with a shimenawa (special plaited rope) and shime (strips of white paper). Placed at the entrances of holy places to ward off evil spirits, or placed around trees/objects to indicate presence of kami. Made of rice straw or hemp, the rope is called nawa 縄. The pieces of white paper that are cut into strips and hung from these ropes (often hung from ropes on Torii gates as well) are called shime 注連 or gohei; they symbolize purity in the Shintō faith.

cards.name: theology
cards.content:
__From Wikipedia__

Theology translates into English from the Greek theologia (θεολογία) which derived from theos (θεός), meaning God, and logia (λόγια)[12], meaning utterances, sayings, or oracles (a word related to logos [λόγος], meaning word, discourse, account, or reasoning) which had passed into Latin as theologia and into French as théologie. The English equivalent "theology" (Theologie, Teologye) had evolved by 1362.[13] The sense the word has in English depends in large part on the sense the Latin and Greek equivalents had acquired in Patristic and medieval Christian usage, though the English term has now spread beyond Christian contexts.

    Greek theologia (θεολογια) was used with the meaning "discourse on god" in the fourth century B.C. by Plato in The Republic, Book ii, Ch. 18.[14] Aristotle divided theoretical philosophy into mathematike, physike and theologike, with the latter corresponding roughly to metaphysics, which, for Aristotle, included discourse on the nature of the divine.[15]
    Drawing on Greek Stoic sources, the Latin writer Varro distinguished three forms of such discourse: mythical (concerning the myths of the Greek gods), rational (philosophical analysis of the gods and of cosmology) and civil (concerning the rites and duties of public religious observance).[16]

    Theologos, closely related to theologia, appears once in some biblical manuscripts, in the heading to the book of Revelation: apokalypsis ioannoy toy theologoy, "the revelation of John the theologos." There, however, the word refers not to John the "theologian" in the modern English sense of the word but—using a slightly different sense of the root logos, meaning not "rational discourse" but "word" or "message"—one who speaks the words of God, logoi toy theoy.[17]
    Some Latin Christian authors, such as Tertullian and Augustine, followed Varro's threefold usage,[18] though Augustine also used the term more simply to mean 'reasoning or discussion concerning the deity'[2]

    In Patristic Greek Christian sources, theologia could refer narrowly to devout and inspired knowledge of, and teaching about, the essential nature of God.[19]

    In some medieval Greek and Latin sources, theologia (in the sense of "an account or record of the ways of God") could refer simply to the Bible.[20]

    The Latin author Boethius, writing in the early 6th century, used theologia to denote a subdivision of philosophy as a subject of academic study, dealing with the motionless, incorporeal reality (as opposed to physica, which deals with corporeal, moving realities).[21] Boethius' definition influenced medieval Latin usage.[22]

    In scholastic Latin sources, the term came to denote the rational study of the doctrines of the Christian religion, or (more precisely) the academic discipline which investigated the coherence and implications of the language and claims of the Bible and of the theological tradition (the latter often as represented in Peter Lombard's Sentences, a book of extracts from the Church Fathers).[23]

    It is in this last sense, theology as an academic discipline involving rational study of Christian teaching, that the term passed into English in the fourteenth century,[24] though it could also be used in the narrower sense found in Boethius and the Greek patristic authors, to mean rational study of the essential nature of God – a discourse now sometimes called Theology Proper.[25]

    From the 17th century onwards, it also became possible to use the term 'theology' to refer to study of religious ideas and teachings that are not specifically Christian (e.g., in the phrase 'Natural Theology' which denoted theology based on reasoning from natural facts independent of specifically Christian revelation [26]), or that are specific to another religion (see below).

    "Theology" can also now be used in a derived sense to mean "a system of theoretical principles; an (impractical or rigid) ideology.

In academic theological circles there is some debate as to whether theology is an activity peculiar to the Christian religion, such that the word "theology" should be reserved for Christian theology, and other words used to name analogous discourses within other religious traditions.[28] It is seen by some to be a term only appropriate to the study of religions that worship a deity (a theos), and to presuppose belief in the ability to speak and reason about this deity (in logia)—and so to be less appropriate in religious contexts that are organized differently (religions without a deity, or that deny that such subjects can be studied logically). ("Hierology" has been proposed as an alternative, more generic term.[29])

Hierology (Greek ιερος, hieros, "sacred" or "holy", + λογος, logos, "word", "account", or "reason") refers to the study of the sacred and sacredness. It is generally pursued by those who find real truth in many faiths and especially refers to philosophical speculations about religion that involve the traditions of multiple cultures or belief systems. It differs from theology in that a god or gods are not necessarily a focus and in that it may include sources with no origin in Western philosophy or religion.

cards.name: BW Guidelines
cards.content:
LOVE. DO. FIRST THINGS FIRST.

Sex. Let tech wait. Write what's on your mind in pencil. Drink water with apple cider vinegar. Brisk movement (alternating nairiki and workouts) outside barefoot on the earth under natural light.  Five minute meditation. Hot shower, masturbation, cold shower. Choose three non-negotiables. Do the difficult things as early as possible.

  1. Rise well before kids and note dreams.
  2. While in the bathroom, read something brief but well written to get the fires lit [often the New Yorker].
  3. Shave shower and dress following the imagination where it leads.
  4. Wake, dress, feed, and launch the family.
  5. Begin work with original thoughts, physical warm-up/nairiki/bato, and creative writing that moves my thinking and original publishing forward.
  6. Turn to the computer when ready to work, but not before. Create Cs daily journal and ABC daily journal.
  7. Choose for all morning work to be about either family/personal or professional work
  8. Plan, survey email, opt in to To Dos based on priority [sometimes do - sometimes repaced with a truncation of #2 folllowed by just starting to do whatever worries me most]
  9. Estimate the time required for each task. Take a break by at least walking away and back again.
  10. Work on only one specific, chosen task for a specific, chosen period of time. When the time is over, move on to the next essential item. Return only if there is time after the essentials have moved forward. Take a break by at least walking away and back again.
  11. Repeat Plan, Estimate, Work phases as needed.
  12. Eat a real but modest lunch away from the desk.
  13. Choose for all afternoon work to be about either family/personal or professional work
  14. Repeat Plan, Estimate, Work phase.
  15. Nap
  16. Repeat Plan, Estimate, Work phase.
  17. Complete an End of Day evaluation and wrap up of chosen projects.
  18. Project tomorrow's necessities and pleasurable interludes
  19. Welcome family home, play, dine, bathe, read, pray, sing
  20. Journal/Report to self/daily evaluative auto-biographical ritual [replaced by time with Lisa either watching/reading fiction]
  21. Deactivate tech at least one hour before bedtime
  22. Sleep early enough to get eight hours, preferably 10-6 or 10:30-6:30
  23. Dream

Want to offer suggestions to others and be taken seriously? Take your own advice first and see how it works out. Course correct in motion and with less contemplation than seems comfortable.

Hold yourself in stillness until you remember how you work best and can follow through.

Create Order first.

Do original work before whatever is externally driven.

Is this the best use of your life? Course correct frequently.

Expect to move things forward in increments in order to be ready for leaps, but don't plan for or expect cinematic progress.

Truly perform. Deploy boldly.

Rest and recuperate.

Evaluate mercilessly, but don't treat everything mercilessly by habit.

As the last thing you do at end of day, prepare for tomorrow and end your conscious day with reflection.

Again.

Plan enough sleep and then stay faithful to the plan. It feels good at the time to work into the night, but the cost the next day is high and the work done is almost always less than it would have been in the same amount of time the next day after a full night's sleep.

{{+Source Content}}

{{+pdf version}}

{{+Discussion|titled}}

{{Rights|closed}}

TAG(S):
{{+Associations|closed}}

In common with his extraordinary ear for jargon (not least the jargon of everyday life), DeLillo's predictive powers have been much remarked. To take one graphic instance, it is clear that he never regarded the World Trade Center as a pair of buildings: to him they were always a pair of bull's eyes. In the novel "Players" (1977), Pammy Wynant works in the W.T.C. for a grief-management firm: "The towers didn't seem permanent. They remained concepts, no less transient for all their bulk than some routine distortion of light." This is certainly very striking--though we may wonder if the quoted lines shine brighter as prose because they happened to come true. DeLillo said long ago that the mood of the future would be determined not by writers but by terrorists; and those who mocked him for this forecast must have felt even worse than the rest us did on September 12, 2001.

 

Although the story "Hammer and Sickle" was published in 2010, by which time the fraying of Western economies was far advanced, DeLillo is already sensing the vague insurrectionary stirrings that are a phenomenon of the past couple of months. I would nevertheless submit that it is his general receptivity to the rhythms and atmosphere of the future that we should value, rather than the slightly carny business of comfirmable outcomes. And here DeLillo's angle of indirection is inimitably acute. Jerold Bradway is in a correctional facility for financial felons--in other words, part of a whole prisonful of Bernie Madoffs. Each weekday, the flabby culprits gather in the common room to watch a market report on a cable chanel. The presenters are two little girls. "Did it seem crazy, a market report for kids?" Indeed--and the more so when we learn that the girls are Jerold's daughters, Kate, twelve, and Laurie, ten:

"The word is Dubai . . . Dubai," Laurie said.

"The cost of insuring Dubai's debt against default has increased one, two, three, four times."

"Do we know what that means?"

"It means the Dow Jones Industrial Average is down, down, down."

" Deutsche Bank."

"Down."

"London--the FTSE One Hundred Index."

"Down."

"Amsterdam-the ING Group."

"Down."

"The Hang Seng in Hong Kong."

"Crude oil. Islamic bonds."

"Down, down, down."

"The word is Dubai."

"Say it."

"Dubai," Kate said.

And we are invited to look even further ahead: these, after all, are the reproving voices of our swindled children.


In the end, "Hammer and Sickle" errs on the side of overexcitement (at about the point where the girls' duologues start to rhyme); but overexcitement is something that the DeLillo faithful will be exhilarated to see. Creative gaiety, a sense of fun and play, has been too firmly suppressed by the almost morbid tentativeness of his most recent novels and novelas. Literature seeks to give "instruction and delight": Dryden's tag, formulated three and a half centuries ago, has worn pretty well. We reflect, all the same, that whereas instruction doesn't always delight, delight always instructs. Very broadly, we read fiction to have a good time--though this is not to deny that the gods have equipped DeLillo with the antennae of a visionary. There is right field, and there is left field. He comes from third field--aslant, athwart.

cards.name: Peace Practices at the Berkeley Lab
cards.content:
Proposal
A "Peace Practices" training for Berkeley Lab staff involves an original conflict resolution methodology, called Martial Nonviolence, which uses aikido-based movement and improvisation techniques to prepare professionals to work together easily, solve problems collectively, and build learning communities capable of innovation. This training has developed from teaching children and adults, both in Oakland and at UC Berkeley, and from the experience of Brandon WilliamsCraig Ph.D. in the areas of martial arts, professional theater, and executive leadership.
 
Impact
From elementary school  to university-level and post-doc students and other professionals, learning to do conflict well applies to supervisor-supervisee relationships, developing a collaborative style that leads to shared grant proposals, and generally increases the community feeling of a supportive work environment. The challenge in applying peace-making skills in a real world setting is the same as is found in the martial arts--the need for clear techniques and enough repetitions to be able to respond consciously in the midst of high pressure situations. This training provides those skills and the expectation of ongoing practice for successful application into the future.
 
Presenter
Brandon WilliamsCraig, Ph.D. worked in the professional regional theater for twenty years, became an aikido apprentice and then teacher, and has been primarily responsible for organizational decision-making in four different non-profits. He obtained state certification as a mediator and worked as a process arts (group process design and facilitation) professional before receiving graduate degrees in mythology and psychology. He co-founded and acted as President and Executive Director of Association Building Community (501c3). He holds a fourth degree black belt from the Aikido World Headquarters (Aikikai) and is Founder and Chief Instructor at both Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley and Free Aiki, his downtown Berkeley dojo. 
 
Brandon created Martial Nonviolence to bring body, mind, and spirit together in the process arts and social justice movements. This is taught by beginning with traditional aikido responses to physical conflict, and then extending principles of "conflict done well" to apply to interpersonal differences using theater techniques, addressing systemic and political conflict through group process design and facilitation. He is a husband and father, and it has been his pleasure to teach children and adults for over twenty years, welcoming those who were his students as children back as adults to work as colleagues.

cards.name: TRS PcPx appeal to parents 20120405
cards.content:
Dear Parents,

This is Brandon Williamscraig bringing you an appeal from Leslie Hites, the faculty and staff of The Renaissance School, and the children who have been studying aikido and Martial Nonviolence with me since last summer. We need your help. The TRS community has before it an unparalleled opportunity to provide your children with a unique year-round learning process called Peace Practices, that would include faculty, staff, and parents in the first life-skills and wellness training of its kind. 

Based in the nonviolent self-defense of aikido, Martial Nonviolence (MNv) begins with body movement and follows each childs' developmental sensitivity in a way that develops the themes and learning strategies that have made Montessori so successful around the world. The children learn to both fall safely and respond to physical attack with no harm coming to anyone involved. Then they extend body strategies into language that de-escalates, deconstructs bullying, and seeks understanding, both because this is martially effective and because it can dissolve the cycle of retribution on which violence feeds.

Martial Nonviolence (MNv) deploys the best qualities associated with martial arts training, include the ability to focus and maintain balance under pressure as well as the habit of taking personal responsibility for choices. Then theater techniques, learned during my career on the stage, are introduced to teach improvisational skills that add confidence and imagination to the search for mutually agreeable resolutions to all sorts of conflict. Finally, MNv leads to exercising compassionate leadership in groups. Maturing students learn to facilitate and find themselves able to shoulder the responsibilities of citizenship.

Everyone who has heard that this is in progress at TRS, and then comes to see it demonstrated, responds with enthusiastic promises of support and the desire to prioritize funding to make it happen this Fall. But the business of daily life intervenes, the needs of today muffle the promise of tomorrow, and the momentum necessary for this program to fly continues to be elusive. Thus far.

This is where you come in. We have cast the proverbial dice, betting that a world where families learn "conflict done well" is a world you will be excited to help come true. The time for looking forward to this happening Someday is done, as a perfect alignment of support is firmly in place. Never before have the following elements come together at the same place and time:

  • a well regarded school is so innovative as to welcome the challenge of actually applying Montessori's vision for peace to a whole learning community.
  • the staff and faculty continue to offer vocal support.
  • a high ranking aikido instructor with a Ph.D. is available with a unique and proven curriculum.
  • a successful history of many months, with ongoing positive feedback from parents, continues to demonstrate the benefits to the children.
  • a local non-profit is ready to provide fund-raising support for tax-deductible donations.

All that remains is action.

  1. Right now: please put into words the benefits of and need for a program through which children and adults learn to do conflict well together.
  2. Please join our Facebook Cause at and post your words there, or email them to me at brandon@peacepractices.com. If you don't have time to write at the moment and would like to make an audio recording of your thoughts, please call Association Building Community's toll free number at (866) 236-0346 and leave your message there. If video is your thing, posts to YouTube are welcome and will be curated to strengthen our growth. Twitter posts should mention @peacepractices &/or tag with #peacepractices
  3. If you can attend the Elementary Parents meeting at 6:30 on Tuesday, April 24th, please do so. I will be there to offer a brief introduction and answer questions at the beginning of the gathering.
  4. Send me information about any business leaders you know and think might be interested in promoting conflict resolution learning for our children and in the workplace. In this way we will be able to find partners and make our efforts more sustainable.

18 hours ago
Stacey Parry

  • Good Morning:) Of course, yes, please copy and paste your mom. I feel sooooooooo bad that I've neglected her. I'm just overwhelmed at the moment and am trying to simply maintain.Please tell her I love her dearly and will be in touch personally, soon. Things here have been so up and down. Just sooooo much at once. I won't even begin to discuss a 13 year old son who I love dearly and who loves me one moment and thinks I'm ridiculous the next. His favorite line lately...."Calm down Mother." Yesterday he informed me he is currently experiencing his first real "crush". I asked him if he got butterflies..."Yes, It is really weird and I find myself doing really stupid stuff. I just freeze..."

    Thanks for the kind words about my site. I have 6 more hidden pages that are really good.....I just hid them because I don't have time to ride that train right this second. It is coming together though.....I'm hopeful I can mix creativity, knowledge and a sustainable living soon:)

    I went to see the psychologist that I've seen for the last 11 years. Pat Lincoln. He's lovely. He always says, "I'm glad you dropped by....I can't wait to hear what's next....you have my number." I go in about twice a year for a "tune up". Well, I knew I was really on overload when just him peeking out from behind the cloudy glass between the waiting room and the office made me start to tear up....The only thing he said was, "Hey! Can I get you a water or a cup of coffee??" Don't think I stopped talking and crying for almost the entire hour. At the end of the hour I said, "I know that everything is gonna be fine. I know this in my heart. I've been here before, I'll be here again.....but right now I just have to walk thru this. The sunshine will come back.Just right now, I'm a bit overloaded..." He hugged me and said, "I tell people that if abnormal stuff is happening and they are feeling normal, that is abnormal. If abnormal stuff is happening and they are feeling abnormal, that is normal." So, I suppose I'm OK. Hehehe. 

    I'm off to MD Anderson...I am leaving Tuesday night. I have registration at 9:00am Wednesday morning. Then labs, then a CT Scan. I see the doctor at 2:00 Thursday. I have to fill out a 7 page history and take it with me. They called yesterday and said that the doctor would like me to clear my calendar for Friday, Monday and Tuesday of the following week, so that depending on what the CT shows, she can order more things....perhaps a biopsy...perhaps scheduling surgery. I just won't know til I see her and she gets the results of the labs and imaging back. 

    Besides this pesky little thing on my adrenal gland, I've got some external stressors that are making me cranky....and I have to figure out a way to find more time for me. I have soooo much to do.... At work, I am now the ENTIRE palliative Care Team. The other nurse left and I don't think they are they are going to replace her. So, the hospital is saving quite a bit of money and haven't offered me compensation for my new workload. The team consists of Myself, 3 docs and two hospitals. Way way silly amount of patients and work. I'm on call 24/7/365 now and find myself at the hospital at crazy hours. Thank goodness T doesn't mind going with me. I was proactive yesterday.... I wrote the VP of Nursing and addressed some issues regarding the logistics of my position and the fact that I've made myself available 24/7. I requested 1) that I get a laptop so that I might be able to remotely do the work ups on my patients and 2) that my position be made exempt instead of nonexempt so that my paycheck will reflect more adequately my work and so that I won't have to be a timeclock puncher. I would rather them give me a raise and then salary me. We will see what happens. My boss said that she was fine with me addressing the issues and to just cc her. Ummmmm, while I appreciate the freedom to address directly my desires, it would be nice if my boss would go to bat for me. However, she said that Marla seems to respond better to me and what I write....

    Brandon, I'm feeling frustrated. Can you tell?? LOL. I am hoping that I get some answers and I will be able to move ahead with things. I just feel corralled. I am ready to move to New Zealand and be a community nurse in the outback. Before motherhood, if I were experiencing all of this, I would have already been gone...not that it would change things. But you know me....I've always just felt if the stressors are mounting up to a level that is unacceptable, then God is telling me it's time to make a change. So literally, I would make a change, usually geographically.A new perspective seemed to always help me untangle things...I just feel a bit stuck at the moment. It will pass.

    Thank you for all the long distance love and support. I never thought I'd appreciate a social network platform so much! It's very comforting to know I can reach you quickly. It's amazing....distance nor time changes the depth of adoration, trust or closeness I feel....

    I DO have something intriguing happening and would like to share with you....A friend of mine owns a travel agency. She really has just begun this adventure. Her dad was actually a patient of mine last year. Anyway, she called and said that she and her husband want to get together with me. She wants to book "Healing Voyages...." She wants me to put together programs to offer during cruises. How cool is that??? And her husband wants me to do a podcast on death, dying, grief and moving forward....which he wants to produce. Hmmmmmm....that started the creative juices flowing. It got me thinking about several different types of voyages....my list was pretty long. I seem to have an archive of information to be shared with the world. We are meeting Thursday night to discuss it. She has a cruise she is booking right now for November and wanted to know if I wanted to offer a program then....Many many possibilities there.....a pretty fun thought....and certainly a great creative opportunity that could increase my income..and offer a bit of adventure...We will see. She and I agreed to keep praying about it, but we were both VERY excited when we got off the phone. I told her about you. I thought that you might offer specialty voyages too. It would be a great platform, there is money to be made and you and your girls could cruise a bit. I can fill you in on details if you would like. Her name is Joy Carta. She may contact you. I think this could be a cool thing for you as well, if you are inclined.

    So, there's what happening on Thornbury Street. I hope all is peaceful in San Leandro....PLEASE let me know what's going on with you. 

    Love you.

What we did:
 Changed the DHCP range on ABCGlobal.net router to clear up address conflicts.
 turned on MAC address filtering to allow only the four laptops to connect to the WiFi.
 set the password.  Confirmed the password works.  Confirmed you can't get in without a password.



A quick summary of what needs to be done to turn the Archive server into a full Media server;

Subsonic:
 confirm what ports need to be open for Subsonic to be used remotely.
 enable port forwarding on the ABCGlobal.net router
 enable port forwarding on NETRIKON

current stat:
 NETRIKON needs to forward the right ports to the IP of SBCGlobal.net.    SBCGlobal has uPnP capability so Subsonic can configure it automatically but that will only work for the one router.


Archive server conversion to home theater system:
 hardware upgrades, new video card with S-video out, sound card and IR receiver.
 software installation, drivers for new hardware, video media GUI and IR remote control support.

current stat:
 I have sound and video cards that will do the job, I just need to unburry the bin they are in.  I also have all the parts needed for a few IR receivers (also want two for myself), just need an hour or so to put them together.
 I've located a home theater software package that looks like it fits the bill.  But I still need to download and eval it on my media system.

 installation time; ~30 minutes to install hardware but the support software will need to be downloaded and configured so time for that is unknown.


I think we could finish the Subsonic setup and hardware upgrades to Archive in one evening, once we have access to NETRIKON.  There are still a few issues relating to crossing two firewalls that make the config a little trickier than it would be otherwise.  I am still researching it.

I don't know how long the rest will take due to the unknowns, the size of the software packages needed for the media server applications and download speeds.

Later, Tim

Joe-approved Description

Mytho-historical Elements

 

Resources

 

Advanced Races Guide Playtest

p5Fey (1RP)

A fey is a creature with supernatural abilities and connections to nature or to some other force or place. Fey
are usually human-shaped. A fey race has the following features.
• Fey have the low-light vision racial ability.
• Fey breathe, eat, and sleep.

 

D&D Wiki

http://www.dandwiki.com/wiki/Halflings,_Changeling_(3.5e_Race)

(Altered from Halfling) Changeling (3.5e Race)

Changelings were kidnapped as children by the fey, then returned years or decades later to the normal world. Their time in the mythic lands changed them in ways that are inexplicable and subtle. They have a deep desire to do something specific, but most do not know what it is. This leads most on to lives of adventure and exploration.
They appear normal but there is something disturbingly "off" about them. Other beings instinctively know that they are touched by the fey.


Changelings deal with other races, and they with them. Due to their nature, they are rarely at ease among others, and others are usually uneasy with them. They can be any alignments, but usually tend towards chaotic. They do not usualy have lands and try to follow the religious practices of their people, but just as often go yearning for some other type of worship. Changelings are often found in the most remote and unusual cults. cards.name: letter - James Leroy Valliant to Rosalie Valliant Blankenship Ash
cards.content:
[This is a transcription of the typed letter from James Valliant to his sister Rosalie.  Rosalie’s daughter, [[Martha Craig]] gave it to [[Marianne Gorman]] nee Montier, granddaughter of [[James Valliant]] sometime after 1975 when she moved to Texas.  I did not correct the various spelling and spacing errors and hopefully did not add any new mistakes to the text.  – [[Catherine Rutledge-Gorman]], June 10, 2012]


[[Pissy-Poville]]
Sunday Sept 25 1938


Dear Sister Rosalie:

            Your letter came day before yesterday.  I can hardly tell you how glad I was to get it.  Every one enthused over the pictures of children.  I think it would be hard to pick a winner among them.  Ours are not o good this morning, at least not Dickie… she keeps house and cooks so realistically that yesterday she could not resist tasting her mud or sand pie.  She isadorable , even when she is bad.  The baby was nine months old a week ago and is already walking around (holding on) her pen, has to be tied down in her bed and can make us think she will climb out of Dickie’s.  It is dangerous to put her on the floor because she crawles under or into everything in reach.  Dickie is the sole property of her grandmother…never calls on her mother for anything…every trouble demands “Grand-mothear” that is as near as I can write her word…both syllables are equaly accented.  It must be admitted she is spoiled.  Marianne is “Older” than her nearly six years.  And, very willful.  She will start to school at the begining of this term.  Maude had her in a convent or rather Sister’s school last spring but it was such a task to get her there and back daily that she wil not try it again.  The village school is not too good, but it has the quality of being very near, just outside the back gate, in the first block.  Over here boy’s and Girl’s schools are still separate.  Pissy-Poville is a small rambling village, has only a church, a bakery and a wagon maker.  No streets, but several roads intersect,  along these are about twenty-five homes…scattered.  One big farmer has his compound in the edge of the village, and it might be taken for a village if set off to itself.  We are about ten miles from Rouen, but there are other small towns two to three miles away.
    Of course we are all waiting breathlessly (almost) on each radio broadcast of news.  Just now it looks as war were certain.  If it were not for the children Pearl and I would probably be on our way…..but as it is we must wait till war is declared, if it is to be, in order to take the children home with us.  I have written Maude, a day or two since, asking about using her house at Dellass in case we should have to bring the children home.  It is a very difficult question we are facing…..If there is war there will be a mad rush for accommodations….and we cant start now without the children, and it might after all  be useless to take them.  I have my return ticket bought which makes it necessary for me to wait for infrequent sailings…..there is a boat from Liverpool on the 4th of Oct…….but that means a long journey and more expense. 
    About here people seem to be taking the prospect of war very quietly,perhaps solemnly.  The notce of Mobilization of classes #I and #2 was posted before daylight yesterday morning.  Of course these classes are to be used for filing out all the defense forces.  Gui’s cousinwas called a week ago.  He is a farmer.  Prayers are being offered for peace in chrches all over the country, but in times like this God seems very far away,with a great nation being swayed by a madman’s exultations in power and glory of war.  I thing Mr. Chamberlains visit and effort was the most determined effort any statesman ever made to avert a war….but also he dealt with probably the greatest will to war and conquest.  There are, of course, none so simple as to suppose that the Sudeten area and union with a few German speaking people constitute the Nazi goal. 
    Monday morning.
    As you will know by your own papers , this is the morning that the joint conference of British and French ministers announce to the world that German demands on Czhoslovakia are unactable (this is the completion partition and extinction of the Czch state) The future is ominous indeed.  It is the world at at another cross road…whatever way is taken none can predict where it will lead to.
    Maude and I are going to LeHavre this morning to the Consulate to register Marie Christine as “American” and I to see what arrangments can be made for getting home.  We will have to take anything we can get of course……and what that anything is only time can tell.
    Yesterday Gui and I drove into Rouen and around…we went to the top of a high bluff that overlooks the city like a great wall…..it is the site of an ancient fort, abandoned many years ago, as useless in the age of long range artillery, but it becomes useful again as a position for defense against aircraft raids….we found it already occupied by anti-guns and their crews…young reservist called to the colors in the emergency.  Like all youngsters they were thoroughly enjoying themselves in this new experience…..likewise the interest taken in themselves by the still, civilian population who came out in crowds.  The only barrier to keep the civilians away from the guns was a thin grass rope supported on sticks stuck in the ground….to the credit of the orderly French crowed there were none to crash that frail gate.  The commanding officer was a vetran of the World War, a reservist of course, now cumbered with an enormous (nearly) “Corporation” …or at least a very unmilitary on…probably a lawyer,engineer or accountant…..he walked about with a poncho over his shoulder, talking casualy and informally with the soldiers……you know in the French Army the privates in the company are the “Children” of the Captain…..there is very much less of the pomp and circumstance in the French than in other armies……and maybe that is why when it comes to the last trial they have somthing that holds them to the fight longer than their opponent……certainly no army ever stood up under greater punishment than the French took around Verdun,and were still there ready for another flight over the ground that the Germans expected to march across with arms slung over their shoulders.  Without knowing much of the language, I of course can not understand what people in the street are saying,but from appearance every one seems taking matters calmly….no sign of panic or grief…if there is any real dissension anywhere I can not hear of it…they look like they felt there is nothing they can do but “Take It”
    Tuesday Morning
    Maude and I went to LeHavre yesterday but I could not find out about anything in the way of a steamer home.  Last night we listed to Hitler’s speech last night.  Without being able to understand a word…it as easy to understand that it was an appeal to Germans to drive ahead toward their set goal and let the world do what it would…a defiance.  We got a free translation of it later on the English broadcast, which confirmed my understanding of its tone.  Please send my letteron to Maude and Della as I may not have time to write to them.  Love to all your little family…I am very proud of you and them.

                    [signed J.L in ink for James Leroy]



Interpretations and questions:
Dickie refers to Dixy May the second child of [[Gui Montier|Gui]] and [[Maude Montier]], born May 2, 1936.

Marie Christine refers to the third and youngest child born December 18, 1937

Marianne refers to the oldest child born February 4, 1933.

Pearl is the wife of James (Jimmy) Valliant the author of the letter.

Rosalie is James’ youngest sister living in Texas but I do not know exactly where. 

Della and Maude (not to be confused with James’ daughter Maude) refer to other sisters of James and Rosalie.  James was the oldest of nine children and Rosalie the youngest. 



Questions:

In paragraph #2, I do not understand the sentence “I have written to Maude , a day or two since, asking about using her house at Dellass in case we should have to bring the children home.”  Is  Dellass refer to the city Dallas or does it somehow refer to the other sister Della? 

I do not understand the sentence in paragraph #3 “There are, of course, none so simple as to suppose that the Sudeten area and union with a few German speaking people constitute the Nazi goal.”


Sudeten area refers to the Sudentenland, the "German" part of Czechoslovakia that was basically given to Hitler (many use the word "appeasement") before he decided to take the rest of Czechoslovakia and then Poland.

  --[[Lisa WilliamsCraig]].....Wed Jul 04 14:40:13 +0000 2012

Brandon

The White House

Office of the Press Secretary

For Immediate Release
July 21, 2012

 

WEEKLY ADDRESS: Remembering the Victims of the Aurora, Colorado Shooting

The audio of the address and video of the address will be available online at www.whitehouse.govat 6:00AM ET, Saturday, July 21, 2012.

Remarks of President Barack Obama
Weekly Address
The White House
July 21, 2012

As many of you know, early on Friday, at least twelve people were killed when a gunman opened fire at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado.  Dozens more are being treated for injuries at local hospitals.  Some of the victims are being treated at a childrenâ€™s hospital. 

We are still gathering all the facts about what happened, but we do know that the police have one suspect in custody.  And the federal government stands ready to do everything necessary to bring whoeverâ€™s responsible for this heinous crime to justice.  We will take every step possible to ensure the safety of all our people.  And we will stand by our neighbors in Colorado during this extraordinarily difficult time.

Even as we come to learn how this happened and whoâ€™s responsible, we may never understand what leads anyone to terrorize their fellow human beings.  Such evil is senseless â€“ beyond reason.  But while we will never know fully what causes someone to take the life of another, we do know what makes that life worth living. 

The people we lost in Aurora loved, and were loved.  They were mothers and fathers; husbands and wives; sisters and brothers; sons and daughters; friends and neighbors.  They had hopes for the future and dreams that were not yet fulfilled.  And if thereâ€™s anything to take away from this tragedy, itâ€™s a reminder that life is fragile.  Our time here is limited and it is precious.  And what matters in the end are not the small and trivial things which often consume our lives.  Itâ€™s how we choose to treat one another, and love one another.  Itâ€™s what we do on a daily basis to give our lives meaning and to give our lives purpose.  Thatâ€™s what matters.  Thatâ€™s why weâ€™re here.

Iâ€™m sure many of you who are parents had the same reaction I did when you first heard this news: what if it had been my daughters at the theater, doing what young children enjoy doing every day?  Michelle and I will be fortunate enough to hug our girls a little tighter this weekend, as Iâ€™m sure you will do with your children.  But for those parents who may not be so fortunate, we need to embrace them and let them know we will be there for them as a nation.

This weekend I hope everyone takes some time for prayer and reflection â€“ for the victims of this terrible tragedy, for the people who knew them and loved them, for those who are still struggling to recover, and for all the victims of the less publicized acts of violence that plague our communities on a daily basis.  Let us keep all these Americans in our prayers.  And to the people of Aurora, may the Lord bring you comfort and healing in the hard days to come.

The Dr. Horrible Syndrome

 

James Holmes is now infamous. Unless additional facts come to light regarding conspiracy and accomplices, he will be known for killing the most people ever to become casualties in a mass shooting in the United States. The Toledo Blade reported the following:

As the new Batman movie played on the screen, a gunman dressed in black and wearing a helmet, body armor and a gas mask stepped through a side door. At first he was just a silhouette, taken by some in the audience for a stunt that was part of one of the summer's most highly anticipated films. But then, authorities said, he threw gas canisters that filled the packed suburban Denver theater with smoke, and, in the confusing haze between Hollywood fantasy and terrifying reality, opened fire as people screamed and dove for cover. At least 12 people were killed and 59 wounded in one of the deadliest mass shootings in recent U.S. history. (1)

It is common practice to characterize violence like this as senseless, but this is becoming a more and more serious mistake. Some might say that, as an academic psychologist, I should probably be more reserved and scientific, clearly separating fact from opinion in discussing the tragedy before wielding a diagnostic pen. But that will not do here. Instead, the images that hold together the cultural complex that makes tragedies like this possible demand dirt-flying-over-the-shoulder excavation. The mythologies from which killers emerge may be and must be studied and thought through so that patterns that put us in danger may be made clear, independent of the individuals who attempt to own them through infamy.

 

Frankly, this is also a bit of retribution. If Holmes is like many other mass murderers, the fantasy of himself that he is following puts him in the spotlight and elevates him to stardom. In this analysis, the opposite result is encouraged. Absolute certainty about his personal word and choices is not required, and so the personality he constructs is not terribly interesting, especially as it is a clichÃ©. Very few people know Holmes well, and the full truth may never be known, but what is accessible is the series of cultural patterns into which any "Holmes" fits, transformed into "The Shooter."

 

It doesn't even matter for the purposes of this investigation to determine if he was acting alone or a pawn of some other individual or group. What matters is that sense be established in working with possibilities--the images and beliefs that make actions like this possible. Then one may make better sense of mass violence and not get stuck, as Aurora Fire Chief Mike Garcia does with "I just don't want the shameless and senseless act of one man to make this difficult for families to move on...Go out. See a movie. Go out into your city. Don't be afraid."(2) Instead, don't move on. Don't go to the mall. Stay home and think about what makes this possible.

 

If you like, consider all that is before you as fiction and put to the side the idea that psychology can be scientific. Imagine instead, that psychology is about what its name indicates, psyche's logic or soul sense, and remember that scientific-sounding devices have a very poor track record relating to or understanding soul. The rising cultural pandemic of violence, of which this slaughter is a part, is a soul issue. It is revealed through study of the patterns and stories we inherited, live in, and perpetuate, rather than being attributable to brain dysfunction and diagnosed away into isolated incidents by madmen who may dismissed as aberrations.

 

Understanding fictions like those driving The Shooter requires fictional tools wielded by people with mad mythological skills, capable of digging up all that metaphors can mean, rather than searching for tidy comforts to put an end to grief. That is not how grief works. Chris Cuomo of ABC News' Good Morning America program, insists that "one of the few messages that we can pull out of a tragedy like this,...that helps us move forward together, [is] that recognition that we have to appreciate life because you never know what will happen next."(3) I suggest that there are many messages to pull from this wreckage and that events like these make obvious sense if you are not only a mythologist but also fascinated by the darker side of humanity, fictions, and how things work, which is to say, a geek. Any mytho-geek can tell you that the story being crafted around, and perhaps by this Shooter is driven by narrative causality ("That's how things work in stories") to set him on the path to being a Supervillain.

ABC TV's Good Morning America 20120721
Chris Cuomo: Good Morning, Bianna. You know that we've been talking about the seventy people who were injured here, and that being the biggest number in American history. It's a very dubious statistic to lean on but, as we learned about this tragedy, the first name that came out was a young woman who really captured what this was all about: full of life, so much promise, and a life taken too soon, almost twice.

(Voiceover piano music): Described as vivacious and full of life by family and friends, Jessica Ghawi had dropped everything to move to Denver to pursue her career in journalism. We spoke to her brother, Jordan.

JG: What made her different was her passion for life. There obstacles that she constantly overcame.

CC (voiceover): And Jessica had been challenged. The twenty five year old aspiring sportscaster from San Antonio, Texas, was at a Toronto mall earlier this year when another gunman went on a rampage. Her mother told Dianne Sawyer about how Jessica felt after the ordeal.

DS: She wrote afterwards; it was the final post on her personal blog: "I can't get this odd feeling out of my chest, this empty, almost sickening feeling won't go away."

Sandy Philips, Jessica's Mother: Yes, and she was very effected by watching the victims being brought out of that shooting, and realizing that several of them were very close to her own age, and realized that life is very fragile, and she had an epiphany at that moment that it could happen to any of us at any time. And instead of being afraid of that she embraced life even more fully from that time on and...uh [isn't able to continue] I'm sorry.

DS: There is no need to be sorry. I know that she read [sic] "I was shown how fragile life is. We don't know when our time on earth will end, when or where we will breathe our last breath."

SP: Beautifully written and we had really thought we had literally dodged a bullet that day. And I was so grateful that she was all right and that the chances of her experiencing anything like that ever agai...were impossible. Or so I thought.

DS: And she texted you. I believe her last text to you was "I'm so excited for your trip here next week..."

SP: Yes...

Both: "And I need my Mommy."

CC (voice over ominous music): On her way to the movie with her close friend Brent Lowak Jessica tweeted "Never thought I'd have to coerce a guy into seeing The Dark Knight Rises with me." But minutes into the movie shots rang out, and soon after Jessica's mother received a phone call from Brent.

SP: And I said "Is she OK?" and he said "I'm so sorry." And I just screamed "Please tell me she's alive!" and, of course, he couldn't tell me that.

CC (voiceover): Jessica's life has ended too soon and left her family struggling for answers.

SP (voiceover stills of Jessica): My life is forever changed, and forever damaged by one person's horrible violent choice.

CC (voiceover): Remembering a daughter they love so dearly...

SP (voiceover stills of Jessica):And we were blessed to have her every second.

CC: And that is the painful message that comes out of the loss of somebody like Jessica Ghawi. It is the reminder to everybody to love the people in their family, to enjoy their lives. That is one of the few message that we can pull out of a tragedy like this, Dan and Bianna, that helps us move forward together, that recognition that we have to appreciate life because you never know what will happen next.

I canâ€™t get this odd feeling out of my chest. This empty, almost sickening feeling wonâ€™t go away. I noticed this feeling when I was in the Eaton Center in Toronto just seconds before someone opened fire in the food court. An odd feeling which led me to go outside and unknowingly out of harmâ€˜s way. Itâ€™s hard for me to wrap my mind around how a weird feeling saved me from being in the middle of a deadly shooting.

 

What started off as a trip to the mall to get sushi and shop, ended up as a day that has forever changed my life. I was on a mission to eat sushi that day, and when Iâ€™m on a mission, nothing will deter me. When I arrived at the Eaton Center mall, I walked down to the food court and spotted a sushi restaurant. Instead of walking in, sitting down and enjoying sushi, I changed my mind, which is very unlike me, and decided that a greasy burger and poutine would do the trick. I rushed through my dinner. I found out after seeing a map of the scene, that minutes later a man was standing in the same spot I just ate at and opened fire in the food court full of people. Had I had sushi, I wouldâ€™ve been in the same place where one of the victims was found.

 

My receipt shows my purchase was made at 6:20 pm. After that purchase I said I felt funny. It wasnâ€™t the kind of funny you feel after spending money you know you shouldnâ€™t have spent. It was almost a panicky feeling that left my chest feeling like something was missing. A feeling that was overwhelming enough to lead me to head outside in the rain to get fresh air instead of continuing back into the food court to go shopping at SportChek. The gunshots rung out at 6:23. Had I not gone outside, I wouldâ€™ve been in the midst of gunfire.

 

I walked around the outside of the mall. People started funneling out of every exit. When I got back to the front, I saw a police car, an ambulance, and a fire truck. I initially thought that maybe the street performer that was drumming there earlier had a heart attack or something. But more and more police officers, ambulances, and fire trucks started showing up. Something terrible has happened. I overheard a panicked guy say, â€œThere was a shooting in the food court.â€ I thought that there was no way, I was just down there. I asked him what happened. He said â€œSome guy just opened fire. Shot about 8 shots. It sounded like balloons popping. The guy is still on the loose.â€ Iâ€™m not sure what made me stick around at this point instead of running as far away from the mall as possible. Shock? Curiosity? Human nature? Who knows.

 

Standing there in the midst of the chaos all around us, police started yelling to get back and make room. I saw a young shirtless boy, writhing on a stretcher, with his face and head covered by the EMS as they rushed him by us to get him into an ambulance. The moment was surprisingly calm. The EMTs helping the boy werenâ€™t yelling orders and no one was screaming like a night time medical drama. It was as if it was one swift movement to get the boy out of the mall and into the ambulance. Thatâ€™s when it really hit me. I felt nauseas. Who would go into a mall full of thousands of innocent people and open fire? Is this really the world we live in?

 

Police start yelling again â€œGET BACK NOW!â€ Another stretcher came rushing out of the mall. I saw a man on a stretcher, the blanket underneath him spotted with blood. Multiple gunshot holes in his chest, side, and neck were visible. Itâ€™s not like in the movies when you see someone shot and theyâ€™re bleeding continuously from the wound. There was no blood flowing from the wounds, I could only see the holes. Numerous gaping holes, as if his skin was putty and someone stuck their finger in it. Except these wounds were caused by bullets. Bullets shot out of hatred. His dark skin on his torso was tinted red with what I assume was his own blood. He was rushed into the ambulance and taken away.

 

More people joined the crowd at the scene and asked what happened. â€œThere was a shooting in the food court,â€ kept being whispered through the crowd like a game of telephone. I was standing near a security guard when I heard him say over his walkie talkie, â€œOne fatality.â€ At this point I was convinced I was going to throw up. Iâ€™m not an EMT or a police officer. Iâ€™m not trained to handle crime and murder. Gun crimes are fairly common where I grew up in Texas, but I never imagined Iâ€™d experience a violent crime first hand. Iâ€™m on vacation and wanted to eat and go shopping. Everyone else at the mall probably wanted the same thing. I doubt anyone left for the mall imagined they witness a shooting.

 

I was shown how fragile life was on Saturday. I saw the terror on bystandersâ€™ faces. I saw the victims of a senseless crime. I saw lives change. I was reminded that we donâ€™t know when or where our time on Earth will end. When or where we will breathe our last breath. For one man, it was in the middle of a busy food court on a Saturday evening.

 

I say all the time that every moment we have to live our life is a blessing. So often I have found myself taking it for granted. Every hug from a family member. Every laugh we share with friends. Even the times of solitude are all blessings. Every second of every day is a gift. After Saturday evening, I know I truly understand how blessed I am for each second I am given.

 

I feel like I am overreacting about what I experienced. But I canâ€™t help but be thankful for whatever caused me to make the choices that I made that day. My mind keeps replaying what I saw over in my head. I hope the victims make a full recovery. I wish I could shake this odd feeling from my chest. The feeling thatâ€™s reminding me how blessed I am. The same feeling that made me leave the Eaton Center. The feeling that may have potentially saved my life.

James Holmes Alleged Adult Friend Finder Profile And â€˜The Jokerâ€™ Photos

 
Posted: July 21, 2012

 

Suspected Aurora movie theater shooter James Holmes appeared to not only have an infatuation with â€œThe Jokerâ€ character from the â€œBatman Dark Knight Risesâ€ series but also a desire to connect online with women or couples for sexual interaction. The New York Daily News released photos of James Holmes with his hair dyed red to resemble â€œThe Jokerâ€ and information about Holmes alleged Adult Friend Finder account earlier this morning. Fox News also reports that James Holmes spent â€œa lotâ€ of time playing role playing or character games online, played soccer in high school and has always excelled as science.

The Aurora police are currently reviewing the Adult Friend Finder account attempting to verify the profile posted online does belong to the movie theater massacre suspect.

Before James Holmes â€œlawyered-upâ€ after the Colorado shooting, he reportedly told police officers he was â€œchannelingâ€ â€œThe Joker,â€ the arch-nemesis of â€œBatman.â€ The photos of James Holmes taken after his arrest with bright red hair definitely resemble the classic comic book character.

The carnage in Auroraâ€™s Century 16 theater No. 9 is the largest mass shooting in United States history, according to the New York Daily News.

Early reports about James Holmes background noted he did not have any online profiles on Facebook, Twitter or other popular social networking websites. Although Aurora police are still in the process of verifying the information, Mediate reports James Holmes likely had an account on Adult Friend Finder. Photos and information posted on the profile of a man with the screen name, â€œClassic Jimboâ€ are presumed to belong to the suspected movie theater shooter.

The information on the alleged James Holmes Adult Friend Finder account note the user is a â€œGoldâ€ level member, â€“ meaning the account has been used frequently for an extended period of time and therefore not likely a hoax created in the wake of the Aurora shooting.

The Adult Friend Finder account allegedly linked to James Holmes notes the user is seeking â€œcasual sexâ€ or â€œa fling.â€ â€œWill you visit me in prison?â€ â€“ The Adult Friend Finder bio of user â€œClassic Jimboâ€ also states. The adult sexual connection website also shows several photos of a man with obviously dyed red hair which do appear to be the alleged movie theater shooter, James Holmes â€“ but are still being reviewed by Colorado law enforcement officers for authentication.

Adultfriendfinder.com lists â€œClassicJimboâ€ as a 24-year-old male who lives in Aurora, Colorado. The birthday listed for â€œClassicJimboâ€ on the Adult Friend Finder profile is December 10-, 1987 and the birthday of James Egan Holmes is December 13, 1987. The difference in birth dates for â€œClassic Jimboâ€ and the alleged movie theater shooting suspect could be intention, a typo or mean the two individuals are not the same person. If the two men are not one in the same, the physical likeness is very uncanny.

Category: Crime 
Tags : adult friend finder, adultfriendfinder,aurora, aurora police, aurora shooting, batman,bright red hair, classic jimbo, colorado,Colorado shooting, Dark Knight Rises, dyed red hair, fling, james egan holmes, james holmes, largest mass shooting, movie theater massacre, photos of james holmes, the joker,theater no. 9, theater shooting, will you visit me in prison
Posted: July 21, 2012

By Tara Dodrill


Read more at http://www.inquisitr.com/281731/james-holmes-alleged-adult-friend-finder-profile-and-the-joker-photos/#jJqsitHBoCcywY3S.99

I suggested in Part One of this two-article series that the mythologies from which killers emerge may be and must be studied and thought through so that patterns that put us in danger may be made clear, independent of the individuals who attempt to own them through infamy. James Holmes is made almost irrelevant through transformation into "The Shooter," which makes the images and beliefs that made his actions possible both more accessible as abstractions and harder to parse when it comes to responding adequately as individuals and as a society. To know The Shooter, especially in this case, one must examine the narrative causality ("That's how things work in stories") by which he set himself on the path to being a Supervillain.

With the words "He planned for months," one response is to envision preventative measures having to do with disturbing of the next mass murderer's logistic. Guns must be harder to come by, for inastance, as Cheryl Wheeler suggests in If It Were Up To Me, (see http://youtu.be/_S5CabGWsv4), her song that was played every hour by radio stations around Craighead County, Arkansas, after the middle school masacre there in 1998. But months of planning are not just the working out of logistics. What is being inadequately discussed involves the life of the imagination, in which Holmes' Joker fascination led to dying his hair red and posting images of himself on websites through which he pursued sexual fantasies as well. The first stage in the creation of a media-ready Supervillain begins in the imagination and involves "inner" narrative influenced by family history and childhood experience, media consumed and violence internalized as entertainment, and all the other dilemmas mentioned in Wheeler's song.

 

He surrender to the police so as not to be killed prematurely in order to set Phase Two in motion. This is not the apartment bombs, as suggested by the police. Holmes thought better of that and allowed the authorities to defuse that situation. Phase Two is the sensational trial now in progress.

 

Next will follow the chrysalis time in prison (Death Row is even better). What did he imagine would follow the trial? In the graphic novel behind is eyes, perhaps he sees escape or parole made possible by an insanity defense and assignment to a medical facility.

 

Whatever happens can be framed as moving on to the next phase in the evolution of a criminal mastermind. The neuro-science prodigy too advanced to be held back by doctoral work climb to the next rung of the ladder as Anti-Social Nemesis.

Posted on July 21, 2012, Printed on July 22, 2012

You can watch the video of Moyers' interview with Hedges at the bottom of this transcript.
